subclassFeature.name: Circle of Cycles
entries: A druidic circle whom venerate the passage of time itself. They read the sun, moon, stars, and seasons to glimpse into the future and delve into the past. They wish to see the aeons pass with their own eyes and value longevity above all else.

subclassFeature.name: Adaptive Wild Shape
entries: Through your knowledge of time and evolution, your wild shapes can gain the Traits of the animal's ancestors or descendants to adapt to your needs. Whenever you assume the form of an animal with your Wild Shape, you may choose to add one of the following additional characteristics to whatever you Wild Shape into:

items: You gain a climb speed of 30 ft., or it increases by 20 ft.

You gain a flight speed of 15 ft., or it increases by 10 ft. (optional rule at the DMs discretion, however we suggest allowing it, but limiting its use to Tiny and Small creatures you wild shape into until level 8).
You can breathe underwater and gain a swim speed of 30 ft., or it increases by 20 ft.
You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} (60 ft.) or increase your {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} by an additional 30 ft.
You may change the type of damage one of your attacks deals to Acid or Poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Cycles Spells
entries: When you reach the Druid level specified in the Circle of Cycles Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of Cycles Spells Table
rows: {@spell Find the Path|XPHB}, {@spell Contingency|XPHB}, {@spell Flesh to Stone|XPHB}, {@spell Circle of Death|XPHB}

entries.title: "The Circle of Cycles observe the evolution of all creatures, great and small."
entries.altText: A moss-covered Circle of Cycles Druid ponders an ammonite fossil, levitating it in front of themselves. Their robes transition to lava cracks at their base and they carry a long staff topped with a blue orb, orbited by several small floating spheres.

subclassFeature.name: Glimpse Future
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws. When an ally that you can see makes a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give them {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, so long as they can hear and understand you.

subclassFeature.name: Deep Hibernation
entries: You gain the ability to go into a deep rejuvenating hibernation at will. This hibernation lasts for a minimum of 24 hours but has no maximum length. While in this state, you do not age and do not need to eat, drink, or sleep. After the minimum 24 hours has passed, you become aware of your surroundings and can wake at any point you choose. When you wake up from your hibernation, you gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} and can permanently change how old you appear to be.
During your Deep Hibernation you can connect with the minds of past or future peoples, either your own ancestors/descendants or other inhabitants of this world.

If you commune with the past, you learn details about your world's history, from a time of your choosing in the past. These can be details that were long forgotten and have no written history but must have been common knowledge at some point in time. This can include things such as ancient legends, tribal rivalries, local wildlife, geography, and other noticeable differences between the past and the current time.

If you commune with the future, you learn details about your world's future, from a time of your choosing in the future. However, the answers provided are not set in stone and are merely one possible future - usually what would occur if your party were to be absent for the rest of their lifetimes. These details must be common knowledge for people of the time explored and can include things such as legends, civilisation rivalries, local wildlife, geography, and other noticeable differences between the current time and the future.

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: This feature gives the Dungeon Master the opportunity to show the consequences of the BBEG's long-term plans if they are not foiled by the party, or to show the history of your world that led to the rise of the BBEG (or other major factions)

subclassFeature.name: Improved Evolution/Devolution
entries: You gain better control over how you manipulate a creature's evolution. You can push or pull parts of their body through time, rapidly evolving or devolving them, sometimes painfully so.

Your spell {@spell Evolution/Devolution|PartneredDDDoD} gains a range of 30 ft. and a casting time of one {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. If you choose a harmful Devolution effect, it also deals {@damage 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier as Necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful save.

Additionally, you can cast the spell {@spell Evolution/Devolution|PartneredDDDoD} at 2nd level without expending a spell slot. You may do this once, then must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again.

subclassFeature.name: Cosmological Evolution
entries: You have the ability to superficially recreate ancient cosmological events from your world's past for a brief moment, drawing upon long past magic to empower yourself and your allies.
As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you may enact one of the following events, then must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again:

items: {@i Partial Eclipse:} Using illusionary magic, you recreate a moment where another celestial body briefly blots out the sun. You may shroud an outside area of up to 10 miles in diameter in non-magical darkness for 10 minutes.

{@i Full Lunar Phase:} Using illusionary magic, you recreate a moment where another celestial body brightly reflects the sun's light. You may illuminate an outside area of up to 10 miles in diameter in natural light for 10 minutes.

{@i Comet of the Warrior:} Using illusionary magic, you recreate a moment when a golden comet passes through the sky, invigorating your battle senses. For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can each reroll a single missed melee attack roll once per turn.

{@i Archer's Meteor:} Using illusionary magic, you recreate a moment when a shower of tiny red meteors shoots across the sky towards your foes, guiding your ranged strikes. For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can each reroll a single missed ranged attack roll once per turn.

{@i Planetary Rings:} Using illusionary magic, you recreate a moment when your planet had rings before any moon(s) formed, empowering you with a sense of protection. For the next minute, you and any allies within 15 ft. of you can each reroll one failed {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} once per turn.

entries.title: Earth during the Hadean eon
entries.altText: The Earth as seen in the Hadean period, a roiling landscape of molten rock.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Glimpse Future
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

When an ally that you can see makes a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give them the same ability above, causing them to take no damage if they succeed on the Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, and only half damage if they fail, so long as they can hear and understand you.

subclassFeature.name: Guided Evolution
entries: When casting {@spell Evolution/Devolution|PartneredDDDoD}, you may {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate} on that spell for 10 minutes. If you do, the changes become permanent until {@spell Evolution/Devolution|PartneredDDDoD} is cast on this creature again or until that creature completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Future Sight
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can peer into your own future, allowing you to glimpse moments just before they happen. For the next hour, so long as you are not {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attacks and all attacks against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Bonesmith
entries: This gory reimagining of a blacksmith makes armour, weapons, and trinkets from the carcasses of slain great creatures. Through a combination of muscle and necromantic magic, they are able to create fearsome weapons, armour, and fighting companions.

subclassFeature.name: Body Knowledge
entries: When you attack with a weapon that you crafted via your Melder of Flesh and Bone feature (see below), you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Grim Harvest
entries: You can harvest resources from slain creatures that you may use to craft items. The Creature Harvest Table below outlines suggestions for managing the resources harvested from a creature and how long it takes to harvest from that creature. When harvesting, the DM may decide (or roll) how much, if any, of that resource you can harvest within the appropriate range of values. These are just guidelines, and we recommend that you discuss this with your DM when the moment arises. Rotting and decayed carcasses are not generally suitable for harvesting.
Your allies may assist you in harvesting. If at least two other humanoids assist you in harvesting, you may halve the harvest time taken for each creature you harvest from.

subclassFeature.name: Melder of Flesh and Bone
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} and {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}. Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} and {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} to craft armour, shields, and weapons from the parts of slain creatures. The Bonesmith Suggested Crafting Table outlines suggestions for the resource requirements for crafting these items. These are just guidelines, and we recommend that you discuss this with your DM when the moment arises*.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with {@skill Medicine|XPHB} checks.

entries.caption: Bonesmith Suggested Crafting Table
rows: {@item Hide Armor|XPHB|Hide Armour} or {@item Scale Mail|XPHB}
4 Hide or Skin 1 Feathers or Scales
{@item Breastplate|XPHB} or {@item Half Plate Armor|XPHB|Half Plate}
4 Hide or Skin 1 Bone or Chitin 2 Feathers or Scales
{@item Splint Armor|XPHB|Splint} or {@item Plate Armor|XPHB|Full Plate}
6 Bone or Chitin 2 Hide or Scales
1 Bone or Chitin OR 1 Horn, Fangs, Claws, or Mandibles
2 Bone or Chitin 1 Hide or Skin OR 1 Bone or Chitin 1 Horn, Fangs, Claws, or Mandibles
3 Bone or Chitin 2 Hide or Skin OR 2 Bone or Chitin 2 Horn, Fangs, Claws, or Mandibles
2 Hide or Skin 5 Bone or Chitin OR 3 Horn, Fangs, Claws, or Mandibles 3 Bone or Chitin
3 Hide or Skin 1 Bone or Chitin OR 3 Bone or Chitin
1 Horn, Fangs, Claws, or Mandibles 1 Hide or Skin

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: Melder of Flesh and Bone is intended to allow a player to fulfil the role within a party as its armourer or blacksmith–granting party-wide bonuses through abundant equipment. It can also generate the party significant wealth. However, some players may seek to use these rules solely to generate excessive wealth. To deter such exploitation, they may find that local traders are repulsed by their designs, that their influx of goods lowers their value, and/or that regional bandits are quickly armed with their formerly sold equipment.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Bonesmiths use a combination of physical prowess, anatomical knowledge, and necromantic magic to create their gruesome armaments. As a byproduct of this, they have developed a knack to cast certain spells. The information below details how you as a Bonesmith can cast spells. Full details regarding spellcasting can be found in the {@book Players Handbook|XPHB|7|Casting Spells}.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know the {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB}, {@spell Mending|XPHB}, and {@spell Spare the Dying|XPHB} cantrips.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The {@book Bonesmith spellcasting table|PartneredDDDoD|11|Fighter: Bonesmith (2024)} shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. These spell slots may only be used to cast Bonesmith spells, and you regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: Rather than preparing a list of level 1+ spells from a pool that would be available for you to cast with this feature, you instead have a set list of specific spells that are always prepared, depending on your Fighter level. When you reach a Fighter level specified in the {@book Bonesmith Spells table|PartneredDDDoD|11|Fighter: Bonesmith (2024)}, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Bonesmith spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}, {@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB}, or a weapon that you have crafted with your {@subclassFeature Melder of Flesh and Bone|Fighter|XPHB|Bonesmith|PartneredDDDoD|3|PartneredDDDoD} feature as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Bonesmith spells.

entries.caption: Bonesmith Spells Table
rows: {@spell Inflict Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell False Life|XPHB}, {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB}
{@spell Ray of Enfeeblement|XPHB}, {@spell Alter Self|XPHB}, {@spell Protection from Poison|XPHB}
{@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB}, {@spell Animate Dead|XPHB}, {@spell Fear|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Construct of Flesh
entries: During a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you may craft a {@b Construct of Flesh}. This requires 4 hide/skin, 4 bone/chitin, and any combination of 4 horns, feathers, scales, fangs, claws, or mandibles.

The {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} is a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} Undead companion that obeys your commands. It is a Medium creature with the appearance of your choice (although is usually fairly gruesome) and the statistics outlined in the {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} stat block. You may only have a single {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} at a time. If you create a second one, the first collapses into the components you used to create it.

entries.name: The Construct of Flesh in Combat
entries: In combat, the {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but may only take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn to command it to take any other {@variantrule Action|XPHB}. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Crafting
entries: You better understand the creation of items from flesh and bone. The items you craft using your {@subclassFeature Melder of Flesh and Bone|Fighter|XPHB|Bonesmith|PartneredDDDoD|3|PartneredDDDoD} feature become +1 items of their respective type.

subclassFeature.name: Artisan Crafter
entries: Your knowledge of your craft deepens to that of an experienced crafter. The items you craft using your {@subclassFeature Melder of Flesh and Bone|Fighter|XPHB|Bonesmith|PartneredDDDoD|3|PartneredDDDoD} feature become +2 items of their respective type.

subclassFeature.name: Body Modification
entries: Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can incorporate one set of your crafted armour or up to two of your crafted weapons into your own flesh. They become a part of you and can only be removed if you choose to remove them over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The weapons can be concealed within your body or drawn out from your body as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You may only have up to three of your crafted items incorporated into your body in this manner at any one time.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Construct of Flesh
entries: You may select a second Trait for your {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} from its initial list of abilities. The selected Trait cannot be the same as the first one you picked. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can forgo any number of attacks to have the {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} make attacks in your stead.

subclassFeature.name: Combat Bonesmithing
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you may expend ten of your harvested resources in any combination (the resources must be within 5 ft. of you or in an extradimensional space that you can access within 5 ft., like in a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}). If you do so, you may replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Bonesmith spells that has the casting time of one {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

Each subsequent time that you use this feature, the harvested resource cost increases by ten (1st: ten, 2nd: twenty, 3rd: thirty, etc.). However, this cost resets back to ten when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Master Crafter
entries: Your creations are only rivalled by the works of master smiths. The items you craft using your {@subclassFeature Melder of Flesh and Bone|Fighter|XPHB|Bonesmith|PartneredDDDoD|3|PartneredDDDoD} feature become +3 items of their respective type.

subclassFeature.name: Flesh from Shadow
entries: You may cast the spell {@spell Creation|XPHB}, without requiring a spell slot. You may do this once, then must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again. When you cast this spell, you may "create" a fresh carcass of a beast up to Large in size that is suitable for harvesting from. The carcass persists for only 24 hours, however harvested materials from it persist for one week and can be used to craft items (which also only persist for one week) using your {@subclassFeature Melder of Flesh and Bone|Fighter|XPHB|Bonesmith|PartneredDDDoD|3|PartneredDDDoD} feature.

subclassFeature.name: Minion Master
entries: The AC of your {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} is increased by 2 (cumulative with the Robust Trait if you selected it) and you may select a second attack for your {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} from its initial list of attacks. The selected attack cannot be the same as the first one you picked. All attacks made by your {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} deal an additional {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage.

Additionally, when your {@creature Construct of Flesh|PartneredDDDoD} drops to 0 hit points, you may choose to instead have it drop to 1 hit point. You may do this once, then must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again.

subclassFeature.name: Big Game Hunter
entries: The Big Game Hunter is an individual who has honed their tracking and ranged attack skills to become a fierce monster slayer. Rather than specialising in slaying particular types of creatures, they instead focus on how to levy a creature's size against it–the bigger they are, the harder they fall.

subclassFeature.name: Bolas
entries: Specially modified ammunition allows you to fire spiralling bolas projectiles to ensnare your prey. At the end of each {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can make a number of bolas projectiles equal to your Wisdom modifier. These deal the same amount of damage as a normal piece of ammunition fired from your weapon, although you can also choose to have them deal no damage when they are fired.

When you hit a creature with a ranged attack that uses a bolas projectile, the bolas wrap around the creature, possibly ensnaring it. The hit creature must make a Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} (it chooses which) or becomes {@condition Grappled|XPHB}. The Grapple save DC is equal to 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If any bolas projectiles remain when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} (before you make any more), they break and become mundane ammunition for one of your weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Game Hunter
entries: Whether as a trophy hunter or monster slayer, you've honed your skills against creatures that are far bigger than yourself.

After each {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose a size category from Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. Until your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, your Ranged Attack Rolls against creatures of that size category deal an additional {@damage 1d8} Piercing damage and your Ranged Attack Rolls against creatures of the other two size categories deal an additional {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage. You can deal this additional damage up to twice per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Ranged Specialist
entries: A master of ranged combat, you are knowledgeable and disciplined with a variety of ranged weapons. You have training with all ranged weapons (including thrown weapons and firearms), and you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ranged attacks for an enemy being within 5 ft. of you.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Bolas
entries: As you improve your physical abilities, you also improve your equipment. The number of bolas projectiles you can make at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} increases. You can now make a number of bolas projectiles equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your Dexterity modifier.
Additionally, double your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} for determining the {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB|Grapple} save DC of your Bolas.

subclassFeature.name: Special Shots
entries: Your uncanny aim and specialist ammunition allows you to modify your attacks to whatever your situation requires. When you make a Ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}, before rolling the attack die, you may apply one of the following additional effects:

items.name: Drill Shot
items.entry: Twisting your ranged weapon suddenly at the moment of firing causes your projectile to spin rapidly, allowing it to drill through tough armoured hides. This Ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB} receives an additional +5 bonus to the hit roll.

items.name: Trick Shot
items.entry: With precise aim, you attempt to ricochet your shot off of one or more surfaces to reach an otherwise unreachable foe. Choose an unoccupied point that you can see and that is within 60 ft. of you. You may treat your location as if it were that point for the purposes of determining line of sight and range for this Ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}.

items.name: Power Shot
items.entry: Whether by drawing your string back as hard as possible or overloading your firearm with excessive gunpowder, you ensure that your shot hits as hard as it possibly can to inflict as much damage as possible. The weapon damage roll for this attack is treated as the maximum damage that could be rolled. Roll normally for any additional damage from this attack (e.g. from Game Hunter, or {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}), but additional damage dice from Critical Hits are also treated as the maximum damage that could be rolled.

entries: You may do this a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Special Shots
entries: You can use Special Shots a number of times equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, rather than just equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}

subclassFeature.name: Reliable Aim
entries: Years of harsh training with ranged weapons has made you an excellent shot. If you miss with an attack roll using a ranged weapon on your turn, you can reroll it. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns. You may only do so a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once), then regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Apex Hunter
entries: You are utterly relentless in the pursuit of prey that you have marked for death. Your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} has a duration of 48 hours. Also, while your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} is active on a living enemy creature, you do not require sleep and are immune to the effects of {@hazard Malnutrition|XPHB} and {@hazard Dehydration|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Finish the Hunt
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can declare that you are attempting to finish a target off. Select a creature that you can see, that is within 60 ft., unobscured, and is of size Large, Huge, or Gargantuan.

You make a single ranged attack against that creature that automatically hits so long as your character (and you the player) says a quip or one-liner, such as "This one's mine!", "I've got you now...", or "Hasta la vista." (or equivalent with sign language or other non-verbal communication). If you do not provide a quip or one-liner, the attack misses.

If a creature hit by this attack has 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer, it dies. Otherwise, it takes {@damage 10d10 + 30} Piercing damage. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Predator's Intuition
entries: Using your intimate knowledge of your prey, you can tell how injured it is. When you hit a Large, Huge, or Gargantuan creature with your Bolas or Special Shot, you can immediately determine how many {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} it has remaining.

items.name: Languages:
items.entry: Primordial (backgrounds don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here)

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) a {@item Shovel|XPHB}, a {@item Miner's Pick|PHB}, a {@item Hammer|PHB} and chisel, a reinforced {@item Backpack|XPHB} that increases your carry weight by 20 lb., gemstones worth 25 GP, and an additional 10 GP in coins.; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: Bonus Features
entries: {@b Eye for Faults:} Years of studying geology allows you to easily select weak points in rock, allowing you to break it and tunnel with ease. You have a tunnelling speed of 5 ft.
{@b Rock Knowledge:} You can identify any rocks or gemstones at a glance, and know their value.

entries.name: Rock Specialism
entries: Your previous work as a geologist has given you a type of rock that you're particularly passionate about. Roll a {@dice d8} and consult the table below or choose whichever you find most appealing.

rows: You love the sediments of rivers and streams and relish the opportunity to spend time wading in them. You're aware of the dangers of flooding.
The dramatic power of volcanoes excites you. You love to explore volcanic settings, but are wary of their dangers.
You love delving into natural caves, particularly those hollowed out by groundwater, but are very observant of potential cave-ins.
Deepwater sediments are your speciality. You jump at the opportunity to deep-dive into water, particularly in the ocean, and are a great swimmer.
You greatly enjoy walking on rolling hills, moors, and tors, and will favour taking longer routes if they take you over this terrain.
You are particularly excited by sharp jagged metamorphosed rocks and can navigate them with ease.
You have a fixation on rare minerals and gemstones that can be found within rich rock seams. You will go out of your way to acquire rare gemstones.
You love mountains and mountain-climbing, and are very good at it. You always want to climb to the very top, if you can.

entries.name: Characteristics
entries: Geologists come in many varieties. Below are some suggestions for traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws that a geologist may have.

rows: Exploration is everything, I have to get out there and find new things.
I fancy myself as an adventurer, but I'm not as surefooted as I think I am.
I'm more of a bookworm, reading about other people's work and adventures.
Given the option between taking a tunnel and climbing a mountain, I'll always take the tunnel!
If it's in the ground, it's anyone's fair game!
I find anything geology related interesting and pick up little rocks everywhere I go.
I don't like clean-nosed, stuck-up scientists of other fields.
We dig rocks, then we drink lots!
I'm an academic at heart, I want to know everything there is about the deep past.
I'm a naturalist at heart. Look at the beauty of our world–isn't it remarkable?!
I love spelunking. There're treasures beyond measure down in the depths.
I only work as a contractor. I've got to get the job done, everything else is secondary.
I'm on the run as a lawbreaker. They'll never find me if I'm deep underground.
I'm going to find the riches of a lifetime–there's gold in them-there mountains, I can feel it.
My parent was a famous geologist–I'm following in their footsteps.
Our world is sacred, both in the present and past.
My mentor expects big things from me, I don't want to disappoint.
I want to see firsthand the most impressive geological events - eruptions, earthquakes, and landslides!
If I can find the biggest, most precious gem, perhaps I can finally impress the person of my dreams.
The ancient past has mesmerised me, ever since I was a child.
I can only sleep in total darkness, usually with my head buried under something.
I can't resist expensive gemstones. They must be mine!
I get overly obsessed with tunnelling, always wanting to dig deeper.
I'm surprisingly destructive–getting to the rocks is what matters, things in the way be damned!
I have no regard for the laws of the land when it comes to my research.
My only loyalty is to whoever is paying me for my work.

items.entry: One language of your choice (backgrounds don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here)

items.name: Equipment:
items.entry: Choose A or B: (A) a {@item Shovel|XPHB}, a {@item Miner's Pick|PHB}, a brush, plaster of Paris with medical bandages, a fist-sized fossil (bone fragment, claw, skull, ammonite, or trilobite), a traveller's {@item Backpack|XPHB}, a {@item Tankard|PHB}, and 20 GP in coins; or (B) 50 GP

entries.name: Bonus Features
entries: {@b Natural Historian:} You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill History|XPHB} checks that involve animals or the natural world.
{@b Hazard Training:} You are acutely aware of geological hazards and have proficiency on Saving Throws against geological hazards (i.e. falling from cliffs, escaping landslides, cave-ins, etc.).

entries.name: Palaeontological Specialism
entries: In addition to being a general palaeontologist, you also specialise in one particular area of palaeontology. Roll a {@dice d6} and consult the table below or choose whichever you find most appealing.

rows: You can instantly recognise if a beast is carnivorous and likely to be {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to you if you approach it further.
You can tell if a beast has been unnaturally altered or is not behaving of its own accord.
Years of studying herbivores has given you insight into their behaviour. You can tell if they're likely to be {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} when approached.
You are able to recognise if a plant or plant-based creature may be dangerous.
You can tell if large arthropods (i.e. giant spiders, giant scorpions, giant crabs etc.) inhabit an area.
When encountering a carcass, you can easily tell how long the creature has been dead for.

entries.name: Characteristics
entries: Palaeontologists come in many varieties. Below are some suggestions for traits, ideals, bonds, and flaws that a palaeontologist may have.

rows: I talk about fossils all the time, much to the annoyance of my friends.
I like to watch modern animal behaviour to learn how ancient animals behaved.
I'm always looking at the ground in front of me, just in case I spot a fossil.
I sometimes find myself staring into the distance, imagining what this area may have looked like millions of years ago.
Whenever we visit a city, the museum is the first place I want to go.
I love to doodle sketches of dinosaurs.
I keep fossils as jewellery and wear them all the time.
Whenever I meet a new creature, I'm always trying to figure out its place in the tree of life.
{@b Theropoda.} Sharp-toothed predatory dinosaurs excite you the most.
{@b Sauropoda.} Giant long-necked dinosaurs excite you the most.
{@b Thyreophora.} Heavily armoured dinosaurs excite you the most.
{@b Marginocephalian.} Crested and horned dinosaurs excite you the most.
{@b Pterosauria.} {@variantrule Flying|XPHB} reptiles excite you the most.
{@b Sauropterygia.} Marine reptiles excite you the most.
I see myself as a 'Gentleman Scientist'. Studying these ancient creatures is a pastime that should be reserved for the academic elite.
Anyone with a trowel and the right attitude can do it! Let's get in the dirt.
There are wonders in our past that few people know about–I want to show them to everyone!
I'm a big fossil fan. Big teeth and big claws are what matter to me.
I want to be the name behind an awesome dinosaur.
I'm a fossil dealer. These fossils have great value, and I can make my living selling them, even if it has to be done shadily.
I'm a Splitter. Whenever I meet a non-humanoid creature, I always assume it's a new species and am wary of new abilities and behaviours it might have.
I'm a Lumper. I often assume that groups of similar beasts will all behave in the same way.
I'm overly experimental, setting up little vials of acid with rocks sizzling in them wherever I rest.
I have a clumsy swing. I'm prone to hurting myself when trying to smash rocks.
I'm a bit vacant. My head is so stuck in the past that I often lose interest in conversation and daydream about ancient worlds.
I'm jaded. I've seen so many bones and carcasses that the sight of a dead body doesn't bother me in the slightest.

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: We have designed these bonds around the idea that palaeontologists have a group of organisms that they are most excited to encounter, but feel free to come up with a different bond if you prefer.

entries.name: Bonus Features
entries: {@b Way of the Wild:} While in an environment that is the same type as your origin, you are not slowed by {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} generated by that environment.

entries.name: Environmental Origin
entries: In your previous time, you inhabited a particular environment and are most familiar with that terrain type. Roll a {@dice d8} and consult the table below or choose whichever you find most appealing.

rows: You are unbothered by trekking through thick undergrowth.
You have a fondness of foraging for wild berries in forests.
The desert sun feels wonderful on your face and you like to bask in it.
Getting chilly outside makes for a warmer, more welcoming, hearth at home.
You enjoy taking the difficult route, so long as it gives the best view.
Catching fish is one of your favourite pastimes and is second nature to you.
You love diving and collect exotic shells you find on the seafloor.
You always enjoy the calming breeze blowing across the plains.

entries.name: Characteristics
entries: The time-lost come from many different periods of time, environments, and cultures. However, they all share a lack of knowledge of the modern world. How they respond to that lack of knowledge differs–they may find things frightening, exciting, or uninteresting.

rows: I love to collect beautiful feathers and adorn my clothes/armour with them.
Gold is commonplace to me, and I find it boring.
I find slaying certain creatures reprehensible.
I venerate creatures of great power.
Every new piece of technology is extremely interesting to me, but also confusing.
The sounds of a city keep me awake at night.
I keep the teeth of monsters I slay on a necklace or bracelet.
I must find a way to return to my time.
My ancestors are out there somewhere. I must find them and reunite.
This new world is so strange, I'd like to explore what it has become.
There's a bounty of wealth that I never could have imagined, I'd like to sample it.
I'm the last of my kin. I must re-establish my clan/tribe.
I left without settling a score. I must find out whether my old enemy was destroyed.
I see myself as nature's protector. I want to bond with and protect the modern wilds.
I see myself as an explorer and there are so many new things to discover!
I'm an expert hunter. I want to find this time's most dangerous beast, and hunt it!
I'd like to return home. I need to learn about time travel and how I got here.
I seek to gain as much power and prominence as I can in this new time.
I miss the good ol' days. I want to change this world to be more like my time.
In my savage world, those who fell behind were left behind. I keep to this code.
I'm fearful of technology, it seems like evil magic to me.
I'm from a violent time, I act quickly and violently, worrying about consequences later.
I'm naive about the dangers of this world.
I think these modern comforts make people weak.
I'm gluttonous with the bounty of all this exotic food!

backgroundFluff.name: Geologist
entries: {@i Geologists are those who have dedicated a portion of their lives to the study of rocks and earthly processes. They are able to see beyond the immediately obvious and interpret the landscape around them, providing valuable field knowledge.}

backgroundFluff.name: Palaeontologist
entries: {@i Palaeontologists are those who have dedicated a portion of their lives to the study of ancient organisms and environments. They are able to interpret how creatures may behave, based on their morphology.}

backgroundFluff.name: Time-Lost
entries: {@i The time-lost are those unfortunate individuals who have been propelled through time, either by accident or against their will. They find themselves in a strange land, surrounded by unfamiliar cultures and creatures.}

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Ankylier live for between 110 and 130 years. They enter Ankylier society at about 12 years old, and fully mature at around 25 years old.

entries.name: Musclebound
entries: You count as a Large creature for determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can manoeuvre.

entries.name: Clubbed Tail
entries: When you attack, you may replace any of your attacks with a tail attack. This is a Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB} with a reach of 5 ft. that you are proficient/trained with and uses your Strength modifier to hit, dealing {@damage 1d6} + Strength modifier Bludgeoning damage. From level 10 onwards, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the damage.

entries.name: Metalworker
entries: You have proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} and training with Medium Armor. You can create a single mundane shield, simple weapon, martial weapon, or medium armor over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, provided you have access to materials and a forge. If you use this time to create an item in this manner, you only gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Osteoderms
entries: You have thick, bony osteoderms in your skin. You gain +3 to your AC, but cannot add your Dexterity modifier to your AC. Alternatively, you may have an unarmoured AC of 17, but cannot add your Dexterity modifier to your AC. We suggest agreeing which of these you use with your DM.

entries.name: Bonus Languages
entries: You know {@language Archosauric|PartneredDDDoD} (species don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here).

fly.condition: while wearing Medium or Heavy Armor

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur and pterosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur or pterosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Children of Seth live for between 300 and 400 years. They mature at around 50 years old.

entries.name: Flight
entries: You are capable of flight and have a fly speed of 30 ft. This is reduced to 20 ft. if you are wearing Medium or Heavy Armor.

entries.name: Global Migrators
entries: You have proficiency in {@skill Athletics|XPHB}. So long as you can see the sky, you always know which way North is.

entries.name: Verbal Culture
entries: The Children of Seth have excellent memories and can recall details from years ago with relative accuracy. You have proficiency in two of the following skills: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill Religion|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}. Alternatively, you may have expertise in one of them instead. You remember every person you have interacted with, including their name if you learnt it.

entries.name: Well-Travelled
entries: You know the value of any trade goods at a glance, so long as you have come across them before.

entries.name: Bonus Languages
entries: You know {@language Archosauric|PartneredDDDoD} and one additional language of your choice (species don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here).

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Jeholrak typically live up to 50 years old and mature at 16-17 years old. Although this is largely a result of the competitive nature of their society. If isolated, an individual Jeholrak could live to their late 70s or early 80s.

entries.name: Power of Persuasion
entries: To the untrained eye, it appears that Jeholrak are blessed with impeccable persuasive skills. The reality is that they are able to produce hypnotic pheromones that can subdue those around them.

When you reach certain levels, you can manifest this trait in the form of the spells listed below. You can cast one of these spells once (at the spell's minimum level) without using a spell slot or requiring components, then require a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you may do so again. When you cast this spell, the only indication that something is happening is a faint sweet smell. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma, Constitution, or Wisdom (your choice) and these spells are ineffective against other Jeholrak.

items: Level 1: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}
Level 5: {@spell Suggestion|XPHB}

entries.name: Cutthroat Society
entries: The Jeholrak of Mount Karao'kr can be dastardly in their backstabbing (sometimes literally) to achieve their goals.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} checks. Additionally, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you may hide a small one-handed weapon or item on your person that can only be detected by a successful {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check, or by any magical means. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: Cutthroat Society is designed for wands, daggers, hand axes, hand clubs, and other small items. It cannot be used to hide a short sword, for example.

entries.name: Subdue Beast
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} checks and can cast the spell {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} without using a spell slot. Your spellcasting ability for this spells is Charisma, Constitution, or Wisdom (your choice), and you regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Limukin have short lifespans and mature quickly. They reach adult-size at between 6 and 8 years old, although are not fully mature until they reach 9 or 10 years old. They typically live until their early 20s. The oldest elders will be in their late 20s to early 30s.

entries.name: Hunter-Gatherer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Stealth|XPHB} and {@skill Survival|XPHB} checks while in a forest, wood, jungle, or otherwise heavily-vegetated area. If you are familiar with the vegetated habitat you are in, you can forage twice as much food as you normally would be able to (this trait stacks with other similar abilities).

entries.name: Envenomed Weapons
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can coat your weapon (or up to 5 ammunition) with a powerful venom you secrete, envenoming it. When a creature is damaged by an envenomed weapon or ammunition, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, taking {@damage 2d4} Poison damage and gaining the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute on a failed save. At level 5, this Poison damage is increased to {@damage 3d4}. The DC for this save is equal to 10 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

The Poison lasts for 1 minute on the weapon or ammunition, as it loses its potency after it dries. You can use this trait once, then require a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can do so again.

entries.name: Watcher's Eyes
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} 60 ft.

entries.name: Innate Toxicology
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any check or {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Bonus Languages
entries: You know {@language Archosauric|PartneredDDDoD} (species don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here).

entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Manyhorn live for between 40 and 120 years, and mature between 15 and 32 years old, depending on their specific species, with larger species generally living longer.

entries.name: Musclebound
entries: You count as one size category larger than your current size for determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can manoeuvre.

entries.name: Guild Connections
entries: When entering a new city, town, or other major settlement, roll a {@dice D4}. You gain the associated benefit below while you are there:

items: You can find simple overnight accommodation for yourself and your party for free.
Trader's prices are 10% cheaper for you and your party.
Town guards will be more lenient with you and your party.
One NPC will share uncommon information with you and your party.

entries.name: Head Crest
entries: You are proficient in {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks. You can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to flood your crest with blood, causing it to display bright pinks and reds. If you do, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intimidation checks for the next minute.

entries.name: Horned Repose
entries: If an enemy fails to hit you with a melee attack while within 5 ft. of you, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a single unarmed attack back at them with your horns. You are proficient/trained with your horns and they have the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property. They deal {@damage 1d6} + Strength/Dexterity modifier Piercing damage. From level 10 onwards, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the damage as well.

entries.name: Bonus Languages
entries: You know {@language Archosauric|PartneredDDDoD} (species don't usually provide languages, but we feel that it is fitting here).

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Small or Medium

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: You are a humanoid. You are considered a dinosaur for any prerequisite or effect that requires you to be a dinosaur.

entries.name: Lifespan
entries: Pluvenn live for 40-50 years and mature at the age of 11 or 12.

entries.name: Razormaw
entries: Your teeth are natural weapons. You can use these to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, dealing {@damage 1d4} + Dexterity modifier Piercing damage, instead of the Bludgeoning damage that you would normally deal with with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Grappleclaws
entries: Large recurved claws on each of your feet help you to climb, as well as {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB|Grapple} foes. Creatures that you attempt to Grapple have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their saving throw to resist that Grapple and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Athletics|XPHB} checks for climbing. While {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} a creature, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to inflict {@damage 1d4 +  PB} Piercing damage to that creature.

entries.name: Nocturnal/Diurnal
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} 60 ft. and only require 4 hours to complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Pneumatised and Feathered
entries: As long as you are not {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to falling damage.
