{@i (ANKYLOSAURUS MAGNIVENTRIS)}

entries.name: Physical Description
entries: The Ankylier are a species of heavily armoured, herbivorous humanoids. They have a large and broad appearance, with thick, bony osteoderms covering their back, flanks, limbs, and head which are, in turn, covered in tough scutes. They are so heavily armoured that even their eyelids are reinforced. Their skin is thick, scaly, and gives them a leathery appearance. Ankylier have low brows, large, muscular limbs, bulging stomachs, and a thick tail that ends in a heavy, bony {@item club|XPHB}.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Ankylier are, of course, based on the well-known dinosaur Ankylosaurus. They emulate its impressive bulk and defences, and play as a relatively slow and extremely durable species. We envision them as industrious, expansionist, and aggressive relative to most herbivorous creatures. This aggression stems from their inability to outrun foes, forcing them to stand and fight. The Ankylier described below are but one group of this species, and your own character could deviate from these characteristics significantly, perhaps even portraying a peaceful, gentle species.

entries.name: Reproduction
entries: Ankylier familial bonds are strong. Pairs mate for life and eggs are laid individually several years apart, with offspring cared for up until maturity before the next egg is laid. Eggs are usually carried in threaded wire baskets lined with dried plants to create a portable nest. Hatchlings and young children form close attachments with their parents, usually following in their footsteps, figuratively and literally. Children are incorporated into Ankylier society as fast as possible, working as apprentices as soon as they are able. Some other species see this attitude as akin to child labour, but the Ankylier value the safety and contribution of their children very much. While parents offer harsh criticism, they also provide great praise when deserved.

entries.name: Bladestone Gully
entries: The most well-known Ankylier society is that of Blazestone Gully. Blazestone Gully incorporates a huge expanse of land–originally a series of riverways that crossed a wide-open, hilly plane. Over centuries, shallow gorges were carved by rivers, steep valleys in an otherwise open region. These once lush ravines were ravaged by a drying climate, creating a relatively barren and rocky scrubland, quenched only by trickling waterways. These environmental conditions are important, as they shaped Ankylier society.

The erosion exposed rich iron deposits in the rusty-coloured sandy rocks that allowed the Ankylier to forge their existence. Decades of mining and smithing have produced huge, industrial iron-clad towns of punished metal where the Ankylier forge all manner of industrial goods. Their society is constructed around this commerce, relying entirely on their craft to trade for other essential goods. This lifestyle has made most Ankylier natural smiths and master metalworkers, often hammering iron with their own tails.

Their brutal appearance is conveyed in their overall culture. Although individuals vary dramatically, softer-spoken Ankylier exist in the shadows of their aggressive kin. Most are quick to anger, but value discipline and reign in their tempers just as fast. They take great pride in their own constitution, and regularly engage in tests of endurance. Competitions to see who can stomach the toughest foliage or forge the hottest steel with just their tail are common.

entries.name: History and Religion
entries: The Ankylier of Blazestone Gully have a long history of conflict and warfare. Their stern attitudes and aggressiveness often land them in hot water with other species, and their politics are no different. Harsh words and bruised egos tend to cause a backlash in smithing pricing, and if another city backs out of a large contract, the Ankylier armies will be sent to recover costs by force. Given Blazestone Gully's monopoly over the region, such conflicts are commonplace.

Blazestone Gully has an official policy on religion whereby any deity that favours honour, strength, or war should be worshiped openly, and other deities are generally not accepted. That being said, the joint worship of additional deities that embody the attributes of commerce, wisdom, honesty, philosophy, valour, or discipline are tolerated publicly. The worship of any remaining deities is considered socially taboo and akin to weakness.

entries.name: Names
entries: The Ankylier invariably give their offspring names that convey strength or power by combining two words, and are usually in their native tongue Archosauric. Names are nether gender- or sex-specific. Common names include: Boulderfist, Ruggedhide, Ironguts, and Booming-Chest. If their names are in Archosauric, to a non-speaker they would sound like: Karko-ragh, Gurrgu, Oo-tarm-ma, and Vro-fath.

images.title: An Ankylier Fighter surveys the battlefield

entries: {@i (THALASSODROMEUS SETHI)}

entries.name: Physical Description
entries: The Children of Seth are tall humanoids with long arms, short legs, and membranous wings connecting from an elongate finger to their lean bodies. They have a soft, downy fuzz, long pointed beaks, and a large, vividly-coloured crest atop their very large head.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Children of Seth, also known as the Dromeus, are based on {@i Thalassodromeus sethi}, a medium-to-large sized pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of South America. The species name {@i sethi} is taken from the Egyptian god Seth. We envision them as tall, nomadic humanoids that have no definitive racial homeland. There are many different clans or tribes of the Dromeus, each with its own subtle differences. The Children of Seth described below are but one tribe, and your design could deviate from these substantially.

entries.name: Reproduction and Gender
entries: The Children of Seth birth live young after a 3-year gestation period. Their offspring are precocial, meaning that they are able to walk and fly shortly after birth, albeit slowly. This is a trait shared among many pterosaurs, and means that infants require significantly less care compared to other species. However, due to their nomadic lifestyle, the Children of Seth adopt the social traditions of whichever society they spend the most time in, including parental care approaches. Over time, these traditions will change as they move between societies. Sometimes, older members of the Children of Seth instead pick and choose their preferred traditions from different societies that they've encountered.

entries.name: Tribe: Children of Seth
entries: The Children of Seth are nomadic traders and adventurers who seek to share in the experiences of other peoples across the multiverse. They usually travel in small groups of 4-5 individuals, or on their own. Most tend to travel very light, favouring lightweight, high-value goods to trade, such as precious stones, fine silks, and magical trinkets. Those lucky enough to obtain one or more bags of holding may ferry many times their normal flight weight with them.

The Children of Seth have remarkable memories and are able to recall specific details of their long lives with ease. This aptitude for memory is one of the reasons they seek out different cultures and societies. They value experiences and knowledge above personal possessions, and greatly enjoy sharing what they know. Every few decades a clan or tribe will have a grand gathering, where each member shares stories of their travels or adventures over magnificent feasts. These are culturally significant celebrations that may last weeks or months, and are often the only opportunity for the Children of Seth to form mated pairs before departing again.

entries.name: History and Religion
entries: Due to their remarkable memories, the Children of Seth have no written records. Despite this, most can read and write multiple languages. As they do not record their own history, they have no sacred texts or religious scriptures. Instead, their religions and ideals are composed of a series of fables and tales that have, naturally, changed over time. Some contain deep truths about their society and nature, while others are now little more than children's stories. This has led to a wide range of beliefs and religions among the Children of Seth, as they are often greatly influenced by the varied places they visit and the myriad societies they encounter.

entries.name: Names
entries: The Children of Seth names are influenced by the societies they interact with. A parent may choose to name their offspring with a human or elven name if they have spent a considerable amount of time with these societies. As such, they have a wide variety of names. Examples include: Borra, Chavazin, Guzzleguts, Vargrelly, Teaneethyn, Thricestrike or Tim.

images.title: A Children of Seth Bard plays a Song of Rest

entries: {@i (JEHOLORAUS SHANGYUANENSIS)}

entries.name: Physical description
entries: The Jeholrak are small-statured, weedy creatures with a short, stout tail and three-clawed hands. They have a stout, beaked snout and a row of fan-shaped teeth. Their bodies are covered by soft, downy feathers that look superficially like a short layer of fur. Their feathers are typically dull greys and browns, although colourful variants do exist.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Jeholrak are based on Jeholosaurus, a small herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Jehol biota that had a downy layer of feathers. We envision the Jeholrak as small humanoids who love to supplement their drab natural colours with spectacular dyed robes and feathers from various bird and dinosaur species. We also imagine that the Jeholrak have overcome their weak stature with specialised pheromone glands that allow them to subdue other species. This gives the Jeholrak a faint sweet aroma. The Jeholrak have several large kingdoms, spread across the multiverse. The largest city (imagined here to be from the Jehol Formation) is built into the side of a large mountain, Mount Karao'kr. Below, the society of the city of Mount Karao'kr is described.

entries.name: Reproduction and Gender
entries: The Jeholrak are an egg-laying species and typically construct a nursery within their homes. This is often an elaborate and colourfully decorated room in which hatchlings spend their first few years. Jeholrak rarely have a single offspring and will instead lay clutches of eggs, raising 3 to 5 hatchlings at a time every five years or so. Caring for hatchlings is typically undertaken by females and this is largely a pragmatic response to resource investment, as it is quite taxing to produce several eggs. Once the hatchlings are 5-6 years old and venture out of the nursery, males will assist in their care. Outside of offspring care, gender roles vary greatly among different Jeholrak societies. Some only allow one gender to be the ruling class or military force, while others have no restrictions whatsoever.

entries.name: The Jeholrak of Mount Karao'kr
entries: Mount Karao'kr is both the name of the mountain and the name of the extravagant city carved into its side. It is a mighty metropolis of stone, with grand spires piercing the sky. It houses tens of thousands of individuals of many species, but the Jeholrak make up the vast majority of its population. The city itself is patrolled by large dinosaur cavalry, kept domesticated by the intoxicating pheromones of their Jeholrak riders.

The Jeholrak of Mount Karao'kr may be small, but they have big personalities. Despite their docile, herbivorous ancestry, they have developed a complex political society of backstabbing and blackmail, with each Jeholrak trying to claw their way to the top. The hierarchy of the city is built entirely on personal gain by any means. Political sabotage, backstabbing, and bribery are commonplace and considered the norm within the city. This city is ruled by a single dictator (or occasionally a 'monarch'), usually for a very short period of time, and has a strictly tiered class system based on personal wealth. Class mobility is exceptionally high between these tiers, with individuals able to purchase or swindle their hierarchical position, often trading places with another. As mentioned above, Jeholrak typically have large numbers of offspring, so inherited wealth is quickly divided among large families. The naturally reclusive nature of the Jeholrak has allowed them to thrive within this society, although it by no means attests to the personal beliefs of every Jeholrak within the city.

Most of these Jeholrak prefer the finer things in life, and they are decadent herbivores, though they do partake in meat occasionally. They have a rich, artistic culture and produce fantastic sculptures, poems, and music. Despite their drab natural colours, the Jeholrak of Mount Karao'kr value beauty highly and they decorate themselves with brightly coloured robes, jewellery, and vivid feathers from other species. They see the value of education, and their societies house great libraries and schools, giving rise to remarkable scholarly pursuits.

entries.name: Religion and ideals
entries: A variety of religions permeate Jeholrak culture, with no one religion being permanently dominant. In Mount Karao'kr, all manner of deity-worship, cults, and churches have risen and fallen throughout the city's existence. Religions are followed passionately, and so the only uniting factor is that their Jeholrak members tend to be aggressive fanatics. It is no surprise that vast conflicts have been fought in the names of various deities, although usually by paid mercenaries, rather than by the Jeholrak themselves.

entries.name: Names
entries: Within Mount Karao'kr, a hatching Jeholrak is typically given a simple name. However, once coming of age, Jeholrak begin to bestow upon themselves ever more extravagant names with reference to (supposedly) heroic deeds they have achieved. As such, the older or more influential a Jeholrak is, the longer and more ludicrous their name becomes. Below are some examples:
{@b Hatchling names} Rassolax; Zilfor; Perfrill; Blukkar.
{@b Adolescent names} Mighty Herebra; Urgine the Quick; Jabara Blade-Touched.
{@b Adult names} Tribe-Herald Wurranii the Impeccable; Warrider Runolox, Jewel-Eater of the Throne.
{@b Official names} Grand-Leader Taltor, Bringer of Dawn and Ender of Revolutions; Battlemaster Scarb the Bloodied Maw of Venomspire's Bane.
{@b Example Elder name} Arch Councillor Kukuok Blade Mind, Herald of the Five Banners, Grand Monarch of Karao'kr, Magister of the Golden Ring, Throne-taker, Slayer of Giants, Bastion of Wisdom.

images.title: A Jeholrak Wizard ponders her orb

entries: {@i (LIMUSAURUS INEXTRICABILIS)}

entries.name: Physical Description
entries: The Limukin are a small, lean reptilian species of humanoids. They are remarkably gracile, and what they lack in strength and size, they make up for with speed. Their thin, scaly skin comes in a variety of hues, but is typically earthy in colour (greens, browns, and deep yellows). These can be mottled with dark or vivid spots, stripes, and other forms of camouflage. They have relatively short forelimbs.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Limukin are based on Limusaurus inextricabilis, a small Jurassic dinosaur that was an early member of Ceratosauria (the same group that contains the large predatory Ceratosaurus). This species' name translates to "Mud Lizard" and they underwent unusual morphological changes as they developed into adulthood, transitioning from toothed omnivores to beaked herbivores. We envision the Limukin as a species of river-, forest-, and jungle-dwelling dinosaurian creatures. They are among the most ancient of the dinosaurian species and inhabit many regions, although the bulk of them are found along the Shisux River. A description of the largest population of Limukin is given below, but many other populations exist scattered across the multiverse that differ in significant ways.

entries.name: Reproduction and Gender
entries: The Limukin are an egg laying species and will either hide their eggs in chambers within their dwellings, or carry one or two eggs in slings, pressed close to their body. Offspring are typically cared for communally and an individual Limukin will not notably recognise two others as it's parents. In general, Limukin society typically has no definitive gender identities or roles. Individuals court and may decide to pair as a couple for several years. When two individuals of the same sex couple up and choose to reproduce, one of them may opt to change sex over a period of several weeks. Also, an opposite sex couple may choose to swap sexes if it would be preferential for the male to egg-lay at any given point and they may do this many times throughout their relationship. Limukin offspring are omnivorous and will actively hunt small prey such as insects and small mammals, learning the basics of stealth, trapping, and fishing. As they mature, they eventually transition into a more herbivorous diet before becoming entirely herbivorous as adults.

entries.name: The Shisux River Limukin
entries: The Limukin of the Shisux Riverways typically form small-to-medium societies (kinlins) of dozens to a few hundred individuals that live in the root hollows of trees, small cave systems, or otherwise create burrows near running water. Larger kinlins are composed of multiple such dwellings over a large area, usually spread across the Shisux delta or along a large portion of the river's length.

The Limukin of the Shisux Riverways choose to pursue a fisher-gatherer society, and do not typically pursue technology. They instead try to stay in-tune with the ebb and flow of nature; fishing and foraging, supplemented with limited seasonal agriculture. This Limukin society has a hierarchical leadership, with the elder-most members guiding the younger ones. They typically have a council of elders, rather than a single ruling individual. Decision-making is slow, as simple topics may be debated for days or weeks before a consensus can be reached.

The Shisux River kinlins prefer to defend themselves using silent ranged weapons, such as slingshots and bows. They also fashion melee weapons such as daggers, spears, and short swords from the bones and teeth of larger creatures. This, combined with their naturally dextrous nature, makes them formidable guerrilla fighters, able to strike and disappear into the undergrowth. Some Limukin are able to secrete toxins that they coat their weapons with.

entries.name: Religion and Ideals
entries: The Shisux River Limukin have a very close relationship to nature, which can take many forms. Some venerate great beasts, admiring their vicious, predatory behaviour, while others see the tranquillity of the forest as a divine gift that must be nurtured. In all cases, the natural world forms the basis of the Shisux River religions. The Limukin make great celebrations of harvests, building small shrines within their burrows for each event. These Limukin also see themselves as part of nature, and so celebrate their own achievements in a form of ancestry worship. For example, they will honour both a predated great Limukin as well as the beast that hunted them. Hunter and hunted are equally respected. The Shisux River Limukin have no formal religious texts and instead use a simplistic pictographic form of Archosauric to paint on the walls of their dwellings.

entries.name: Names
entries: Limukin typically have short names with two, three, and (rarely) four syllables. Their names, and language in general, include many hard 'K', 'N', and 'I' sounds. Typical names include: Piphi, Torsek, Nuek, Nanzaahn, Gerumal, Jam'reer, Liph'ko, Neararu.

images.title: A Limukin Ranger stalks their prey

entries: {@b (VARIOUS SPECIES, I.E. {@i STYRACOSAURUS ALBERTENSIS})}

entries.name: Physical Description
entries: The Manyhorn is a name given to the array of ceratopsian humanoids (evolved from {@i Styracosaurus albertensis}, {@i Diabloceratops eatoni}, {@i Sinoceratops zhuchengensis}, {@i Protoceratops andrewsi} etc.) that have formed a cohesive society of multiple guilds. They vary greatly in size and horn shape/number, but otherwise look quite similar. They are bulky dull-coloured scaly-skinned humanoids with short, stout limbs, large, bony head crests, a beaked mouth, and horns. A handful of Manyhorn (i.e. those evolved from {@i Protoceratops}) do not actually possess horns, but are still considered Manyhorn nonetheless. Most Manyhorn are generally dull greens, reds, and browns in colour, but brighter variants exist.

Manyhorn prefer to dress formally, with well-fitted suits and multi-layered robes or tabards. They invariably display their guild sigil prominently on their clothing, but sometimes also have it painted or tattooed onto their crest. When armoured, their armour usually is accompanied by tabards displaying their guild's colours.

entries.name: Background
entries: We have constructed Manyhorn society to primarily operate as a series of guilds that can exist within any regional setting. The guilds protect and employ each of their members, who in turn help the guild prosper. Each guild consists of members of every species of Manyhorn who are extremely loyal to their guild. Each guild can (and does) function entirely independently of other guilds, but each guild also typically focuses on mastering a specific aspect of society. These may be tied to philosophical ideals, commercial aspirations, or political conquest of a region. The number of guilds within a region may vary, but typically range from 3 to 6.

It is exceedingly rare for a Manyhorn to leave their guild and swapping guilds is almost unheard of. Those without a guild are branded socially as 'guildless', a considerable insult within Manyhorn society.

entries.name: Reproduction
entries: Manyhorn undertake ceremonial marriages that must occur with a different guild. It is not acceptable for any Manyhorn to marry or reproduce internally within a guild as this has historically led to reduced gene pools within each guild. Members who breach this rule risk expulsion from their guild.

Manyhorn tend not to be attentive parents, and females lay between 3 and 10 eggs in a clutch (depending on species) that are then raised by communal "hatchwatchers". Offspring are cared for in large groups of 20 or more hatchlings. All eggs are the centre of a fierce custody battle between the different guilds of each parent. Even before they hatch, both guilds vie for the "right of adoption" to bolster their own numbers. Some guilds will amicably divide the eggs, others will issue a winner-takes-all challenge.

entries.name: The Guilds of Un Grazook
entries: Once a small fishing port, Un Grazook was utterly transformed by the prosperity brought by the Manyhorn guilds over several centuries. The city now boasts a vast population with inhabitants from every conceivable species and every corner of the world. A metropolis of trade and culture, founded on the competing principals of five different guilds, each specialised in different areas of society:

items: The Alorah–The guild of stonemasonry and land lordship, whose colours are green and gold and whose sigil is a sapling with deep roots.
The Janth–The guild of shipbuilding and commerce, whose colours are red and black and whose sigil is a sailboat on stormy waters.
The Orb'eth–The guild of politics and negotiation, whose colours are yellow and purple and whose sigil is a fired arrow with a ribbon attached.
The Umalai–The guild of arts and entertainment, whose colours are orange and royal blue and whose sigil is a four-winged bird (or Microraptor).
The Thyrothe–The guild of education and science, whose colours are pale blue and white and whose sigil is a torch held aloft within a circle.

entries: The guilds compete openly for political power, but also engage in espionage to undermine each other's influence. Every year, one high-ranking member of each guild is selected as a representative to form a council that makes city-wide decisions and guides the overall rule of the region. City districts are predominantly run by a single guild and may range from peaceful areas of reason and enlightenment to crime-ridden hubs of corruption, the former being more likely due to the self-respect of most guilds.

entries.name: History and Religion
entries: The history of Un Grazook is one wrought with strife, violence, and ultimately prosperity. When the Manyhorn first arrived at the small port, they were a disparate people of many different cultures pressed together by circumstance. Species prejudice gave rise to clans that fought in gang warfare for generations before the fallout of their battles brought the city to near destruction. This turning point caused younger members of each clan to overthrow their elders, toppling the philosophy of division. Eventually, the clans were entirely disbanded and their members distributed between ten guilds dedicated to specific tasks to restore the city both physically and culturally. Within a matter of years, the bubbling tension between different ceratopsian species was ejected entirely from their society. However, philosophical differences developed between each guild, ultimately producing a new kind of tension. Thankfully, this largely manifested as a competitive and industrious economic battle, rather than a bloody one. The five lost guilds were not slain in gory battles, but were rather slowly absorbed by larger and/or more successful guilds.

Religious worship varies dramatically between guilds. Some guilds have a strictly enforced single religion, others allow their members to worship whoever or whatever they please, and others still outlaw religion entirely, seeing it as a distraction from loyalty to the guild. In the more restrictive guilds, most Manyhorn keep their religious beliefs private and simply project the status quo.

entries.name: Names
entries: A name is not given to a Manyhorn until its "right of adoption" has been completed. Names are then issued by a guild elder and each elder may follow a different naming convention. Some examples of different guild names are as follows:

items: The Alorah–Hard guttural Archosauric names: Grulgrug, Arough-Roth, or Barr.
The Janth–Double-barrelled names in Archosauric: Hur-Kreck, Uy-Gungg, or Farenk-Aron.
The Orb'eth–Sharp and relatively high-pitched Archosauric names: Kreenk, Flarek, or Brekbrek.
The Umalai–All names begin with the prefix "Un-" to honour their cultural heritage: Un-Krof, Un-Tharalla, or Un-Palapa.
The Thyrothe–Are given names that are intended as guidance for their future careers or area of research: Astroquoth, Minerag, or Chemokruln.

entries: {@b (VARIOUS SPECIES, I.E. {@i SAURORNITHOLESTES LANGSTONI})}

entries.name: Physical Description
entries: The Pluvenn are a society of raptorfolk, made from a collection of different species of raptors (evolved from {@i Saurornitholestes langstoni}, {@i Sinornithosaurus millenii}, {@i Deinonychus antirrhopus}, etc.). This gives them a very diverse appearance, varying greatly in size, colour, plumage, and robustness. On the whole, they are lightly built and gracile bipeds, covered by a thick coat of fluffy feathers. The feathers on their forelimbs are long and sturdy, and they have long flowing feathers on their tails. Their plumage can be vivid, drab, patterned, or even camouflaged. They have long, snouted heads and a row of extremely sharp teeth. All Pluvenn have scaled bird-like feet with a large, recurved claw on the inside toe.

entries.name: Background
entries: The name Pluvenn comes from the Cornish word for feather and is a fitting reference to rural English society, which the Pluvenn are inspired by. Most raptorfolk in fiction are portrayed as a savage and vicious jungle-dwelling species. We have taken a very different approach and instead envision them as a peaceful society of townsfolk that fit into the idealistic Beatrix Potter-esque rural life. They live in quiet towns and villages, busying themselves with gardening, tea drinking, cooking, artistry, and socialising. Despite this humble appearance, the Pluvenn have other characteristics that some species find disturbing, most notably their vicious, predatory nature. They are obligate carnivores and so do not bother with agriculture (other than growing herbs and spices to season their meat). They instead rear livestock and partake in gory festival hunts.

entries.name: Courtship and Reproduction
entries: Pluvenn undertake a prolonged period of courtship when seeking a mate. This usually begins as simple conversations, followed by long (sometimes chaperoned) walks, then joint attendance of social events. During this time, they will exchange gifts of wild flowers, hand-crafted trinkets, and specialist foods. Public displays of affection rarely exceed handholding. Eventually, they will ceremonially pair to publicise their relationship and this commitment is for life.

Pluvenn are egg-laying species and lay eggs in clutches of 3-4. Incubation is carried out at home by both parents, but hatchlings are cared for in a dedicated community nursery during the day and only return home to sleep. These nurseries are run by particularly gentle and well-spoken members of the Pluvenn community and hatchlings remain there until they are about 6 months old. After this, they enter a strict schooling system where they attend almost every day and are schooled by dedicated educational {@item staff|XPHB}.

entries.name: Bristlebush Vale
entries: Hidden amongst the strife and hardship of the ancient world lies Bristlebush Vale. This idyllic region is famed for its long bright summers, drizzly autumns, spring meadows full of life, and twinkling icicle winters. Aside from the hunting activities of the Pluvenn themselves, Bristlebush Vale is a peaceful and quiet setting. Between gnarled, misty forests and rolling hills lie secluded villages and hamlets. In these settlements, the Pluvenn play out their pleasant lives of socialising, gardening, farming livestock, and hunting.

Pluvenn hunts are a combination of whimsy and horror. One-to-two times a month, the Pluvenn will undertake ritualistic group hunts at dusk. Donned in their finest garb, they venture into the surrounding forests, setting traps and positioning in the shadows to ambush game. They prefer to kill ensnared prey with their jaws and claws, letting their otherwise docile nature drop away in that gory moment. In a single night, dozens of creatures are slaughtered in a bloodbath that leaves many non-Pluvenn horrified.

Slain prey are returned to the village for a night-time festival of roaring fire barbecues and butchery. Bunting and stalls decorate the village, with each stand boasting their own cooking technique or particular spices. These are considered bonding experiences and family units will often hunt together and share their stories around the firelight. In the morning, the remaining meat is prepared for consumption in later weeks. It may be stored in cool underground buildings or spiced and cured in great smoking barns. Some Pluvenn favour making specialist gravy-like meat teas that are brewed from jerky mixed with spices.

entries.name: History and Religion
entries: The Pluvenn of Bristlebush Vale have a relatively simple history of village life. Their ancestors arrived in the region centuries ago as several disparate travelling tribes, composed of different species of raptorfolk. Over time, these intermingled until a single cohesive culture was formed. Since then, they have had a docile history with no major conflicts beyond the repelling of unwanted bandits. These invaders are sometimes ritualistically devoured in a grand post-battle feast (called a "gool").

Pluvenn religion revolves largely around ancestor worship. Their dead are buried with precious trinkets and sentimental items in sacred burial mounds and small catacombs hidden deep within nearby forests. These places are sacred to the Pluvenn and are, unfortunately, usually the targets of any intruding raids. Pluvenn may travel to these sites to ask their forebearers for guidance during the rare times of hardship or social strife.

entries.name: Names
entries: The Pluvenn favour high-pitched squawky names spoken in their ancient Archosauric tongue, such as Skree, Kek, Kareese, or Pip. They also sometimes have names spoken in Common, such as William, Hermione, Richard, or Audrey. Typically, the naming convention of an individual village will be similar among its populace, either all having Archosauric names or all having Common names.

images.title: A Pluvenn Druid taking a long rest on an adventure

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Catch Jaws
entries: If a creature hits you with an attack that uses its mouth (i.e. a bite or maw attack), you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce any incoming damage by {@dice 1d10} + your level.

entries.name: Heroic Moment
entries: The first time you fail an {@skill Athletics|XPHB} check each day, you can choose to succeed it instead.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Enchant
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can select an item you can see and touch, and enchant it. You may only have a single item enchanted at any given point, and when you use this {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, any previous enchants you have made end. The item gains one of the following enchantments based on its type:

items.name: Weapon
items.entry: For the next minute that weapon deals {@damage 1d6} additional damage of any damage type that your spells can deal. At level 16, you may add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to this additional damage.

items.name: Armour
items.entry: For the next minute that armour provides the wearer with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one damage type that your spells can deal. At level 16, you may select two damage types that this armour provides {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to.

items.name: Wondrous
items.entry: For the next minute, that item provides the bearer {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Saving Throws and checks to prevent or end a condition of your choice. At level 16, you may select two conditions that this item provides {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} for.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Intelligence by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Animal Behaviour Expert
entries: You have expertise in {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} checks.

entries.name: Bespoke Saddles
entries: Creatures you tame gain +1 to their AC, attack rolls, and damage.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: "What a beauty!"
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} checks and Beasts that you attempt to {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB|Grapple} have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their saving throw to resist that Grapple.

entries.name: "Crikey!"
entries: Any Large, Medium, or Small beast you are {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} cannot select you as a target for its attacks.

entries.name: Portable Lamp
entries: You possess a physical lamp that weighs 1 lb. and can produce 20 ft. of {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} and a further 20 ft. of {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}. The lamp attaches to your belt/armour and does not need to be carried.

entries.name: Familiar Rumble
entries: While underground, you have {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} 30 ft. If you already have {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB}, its range is increased by 20 ft.

entries.name: "Cave-in!"
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any skill check or {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to escape falling natural rocks (i.e. from cliffs, caves, tunnels, etc., but not from traps or buildings).

entries.name: Taxonomist
entries: When rolling a {@skill Survival|XPHB} check to identify the remains of any beast, plant, or humanoid, any roll of a 1-9 is treated as a 10.

entries.name: Fieldwork
entries: You have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in Survival checks when tracking a beast.

entries.name: Functional Morphology
entries: The first time you encounter a beast that you have not seen before, you are able to discern either its AC, maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or one {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} it has (your choice).

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Wisdom by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Stone Whisper
entries: You can cast the {@spell Stone Shape|XPHB} spell once per day without requiring material components and without using a spell slot. This is increased to three times per day at level 10, five times per day at level 15, and an unlimited number of times per day at level 20.

entries.name: Whisper Back
entries: You have {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} 10 ft.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Increase your Intelligence or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.

entries.name: Heat Handler
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.

entries.name: Assess Volcano
entries: If you can see a volcano, you may take 10 minutes to assess it. If you do, you are able to determine whether it is likely to erupt in either the next >100 years, 10 years, 1 year, 30 days, 7 days, or 24 hours. If the volcano is going to erupt in the next 7 days or less, you are able to determine the minimum safe distance from it.

spell.name: Evolution/Devolution
entries: By touching a creature, you can cause it to take on attributes of its ancestors or descendants. A creature may accept these changes willingly or, if not, they must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you may pick one of the following changes and apply it to the creature's stat block.

items: Increase or decrease the damage of all of the creature's attacks by {@dice 1d4}.
Increase or decrease the creature's speed by 20 ft.
The creature gains a climbing speed equal to half its speed, or its climbing speed is reduced by 30 ft. (it can be reduced to 0).
The creature gains a flying speed of 10 ft., or its flying speed is reduced by 30 ft. (it can be reduced to 0).

Select one of the creature's attacks or abilities that deals damage and change the damage type of that attack. If it deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you may change it to Acid or Poison damage. If it deals any other damage type, you may change it to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

The creature gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} 60 ft., or reduces its {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} (if it has it) by 60 ft. (it can be reduced to 0). If this creature does not have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, you may alternatively reduce its maximum normal vision range to 60 ft. instead, causing anything beyond 60 ft. from it to only be visible as amorphous blurry shapes.
Increase the creature's maximum and current hit points by {@dice 1d4 + 4}, or reduce its maximum and current hit points by {@dice 1d4 + 4} (to a minimum of 1).

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you may pick another Trait to change for each slot above 2nd level. You cannot pick the same Trait more than once.

item.name: +1 Theropod Jaw
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This huge axe is crafted from the harvested jaw of a mighty predatory dinosaur.}
{@b Rules:} This weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage with each successful hit.

item.name: +2 Theropod Jaw
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This huge axe is crafted from the harvested jaw of a mighty predatory dinosaur.}
{@b Rules:} This weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage with each successful hit.

item.name: Amber Necklace
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A simple twine necklace binding a small lump of amber, or a chain of amber beads.}
{@b Rules:} While wearing this necklace, you have a +2 bonus to any roll to resist or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. This effect is not cumulative with further amber items.

item.name: Analysis Tools
entries: This collection of hand lenses, rubbing papers, chalk, and tweezers allows for more thorough investigation of small objects than the naked eye would allow.

items.name: Ability:
items.entry: Intelligence

items.name: Utilize:
items.entry: When attempting a {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check of an object small enough to fit in your hand, you may replace the check's DC with this tool's DC (DC 8).

item.name: Ancient Horn
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A curved and polished bone horn made from the skull of a large hadrosaur.}

{@b Rules:} This instrument can be used as a spell focus by a Bard. Once per day, as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, the horn can be blown to alert allies. When used in this way, it cannot be heard by anyone except the bearer and their allies, who can hear it regardless of where they are in the multiverse. The sound itself does not convey specific information, and is simply a deep note.

entries.name: Theropod-footed Healing Balm
entries: This plant's bird- foot-shaped leaves can be crushed into a {@item Araliaephyllum sp. Healing Balm|PartneredDDDoD|paste} and applied to a wound to help it heal. If this balm is applied to a creature during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, that creature heals {@dice 1d6 + 2} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and its speed is increased by 10 ft. for the next 24 hours.

item.name: Automimicry Cape
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This large cape is dull on the back, but the inside is patterned and coloured with two huge eyes. When held up from either side, it gives the wearer the superficial image of a huge bestial head with glaring eyes.}

{@b Rules:} While wearing this cape, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks until the end of your turn against any creature with an Intelligence score of 5 or lower.

item.name: Azdarchid Beak Greatsword
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This lightweight sword is crafted from the huge beak of an Azdarchid pterosaur. It can slide through the air with ease.}

{@b Rules:} When using your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} with this weapon, your melee reach is increased to 10 ft. for that attack. Furthermore, attacks made with this weapon against creatures from the elemental plane of air are made at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

item.name: Cladophlebis Rhizome Grenade
entries: Alternatively, the rhizome can be carefully extracted with a DC 10 {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} check and then may function like a {@item Cladophlebis Rhizome Grenade|PartneredDDDoD|grenade}:

entries.name: Rhizome grenade
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, a humanoid creature can throw the grenade (20/60 ft.). Any creature within 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of where it lands must succeed a DC 12 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, or take {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 1d4} Fire damage.

item.name: Dead Deity Robes
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i These beautiful, pristine red and black robes are the last remnants of a civilisation from millions of years in the past who worshiped a deity forgotten by all, aeons ago. They are inscribed with runes in an ancient unreadable language.}

{@b Rules:} While attuned to these robes, you have an additional spell slot of whatever your current highest level spell slot is. The level of the additional spell slot is reset and replenishes after each {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If you aren't wearing armour, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} becomes 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

item.name: Dice of the Dinosaur
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This six-sided dice has the visages of six different large dinosaurs carved into each face. Once rolled, a strange bellowing noise can be heard in the distance.}

{@b Rules:} The first time that this dice is rolled each day, it summons a dinosaur that matches the carved visage of the face it rolls to. The dinosaur is summoned somewhere within a 1 mile radius and is {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to whoever rolled the dice, actively seeking them out.

If the dinosaur is slain, it disintegrates into {@item Amber|XDMG|amber gemstones} worth 100 GP multiplied by the corresponding number below. Once that dinosaur has been slain, the corresponding facing on the dice turns blank and becomes weighted in a way that it cannot roll with that side face-up. At the next dawn, if the dinosaur is alive, it vanishes and the dice remains unchanged. The dice faces are:

items: {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD}
{@creature Centrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}
{@creature Utahraptor|PartneredDDDoD}
{@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD}
{@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD}
{@creature Tyrannosaurus Rex|XMM|Tyrannosaurus}

entries.name: Toxic Maturity
entries: Fresh shoots of this plant are non-toxic and can be brewed into a simple, but delicious, {@item Equisetum sp. Potion|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that heals {@dice 1d4 + 1} hit points when consumed. However, {@item Equisetum sp. Potion (Incorrectly Harvested)|PartneredDDDoD|mature plants} are highly toxic and any creature that consumes them (or a derivative of them) is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 24 hours. A successful DC 10 {@skill Nature|XPHB} check is required to determine which shoots are safe to consume.

entries.name: Toxic Maturity

Potion|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that heals {@dice 1d4 + 1} hit points when consumed. However, {@item Equisetum sp. Potion (Incorrectly Harvested)|PartneredDDDoD|mature plants} are highly toxic and any creature that consumes them (or a derivative of them) is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 24 hours. A successful DC 10 {@skill Nature|XPHB} check is required to determine which shoots are safe to consume.

item.name: Ethereal Egg
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This football/ball sized egg is partly translucent, and wisps of coloured smoke constantly drift off of it.}

{@b Rules:} If incubated (kept warm) for {@dice 2d4} days, the egg will hatch into a familiar for the player who incubated it last. This functions in the same manner as a familiar would via the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell, with the following exceptions:

items: The familiar's appearance and stats are selected by the hatching player from a list of known familiars (we recommend one of the familiars from this book), and then cannot be changed.
Once the familiar drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it disappears and can be resummoned as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

Once the familiar drops to 0 HP for the third time, instead of disappearing, it reverts back to its Ethereal Egg form and must be incubated for a further {@dice 2d4} days before re-hatching as the same familiar.

item.name: Evolunite Shard
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A tiny shard of iridescent rock that sparkles when in moonlight. When it comes into contact with a creature's integument (skin/scales/feathers/hair/etc.), it sparks and sizzles as it dissolves into them.}

{@b Rules:} If this mineral touches a creature's exposed body, it is destroyed. The DM then rolls on the Minor Mutation Table (see {@book Mesozoic Reptiles in Your World|PartneredDDDoD|9|Mutation Tables}) for that creature, and it gains the associated mutation for 1 hour. If more than five Evolunite shards are used on the same creature within 1 hour of each other, the creature is polymorphed into a tiny crab with 2 hit points for 1 hour.

item.name: Excavator's Tools
entries: These fine picks, chisels, and brushes allow for precise extraction of precious material from rock.

items.name: Ability:
items.entry: Dexterity

items.name: Utilize:
items.entry: Increase the value of fossils or gemstones by 20% when extracting them from rock (DC 5).

item.name: Exceptional Refractive Index Crystal
item.reqAttune: by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This large, jagged crystal has a pastel colour hue to it, but when turned in light it refracts brilliant rainbows.}

{@b Rules:} This item can be used as a spell focus by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer. While wielding this item, you may cast the {@spell Light|XPHB} cantrip a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} per day, and you may cast the spell {@spell Color Spray|XPHB|Colour Spray} at 1st level once per day without using a spell slot.

item.name: Flawless Refractive Index Crystal
item.reqAttune: by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This large, jagged crystal has a pastel colour hue to it, but when turned in light it refracts brilliant rainbows.}

{@b Rules:} This item can be used as a spell focus by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer. While wielding this item, you may cast the {@spell Light|XPHB} cantrip a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} per day, and you may cast the spell {@spell Color Spray|XPHB|Colour Spray} at 1st level once per day without using a spell slot.

entries.name: Psychodysleptic
entries: If a creature consumes the {@item Jaguariba wiersemaniania Flower|PartneredDDDoD|flowers} of this plant, it must succeed a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} or be {@condition Stunned|XPHB} for {@dice 1d4} minutes. On a successful save, it is instead {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of all other creatures for {@dice 1d4} minutes. Whenever that creature takes damage while under either effect, it may make another DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Hyper-thermo-genetic
entries: If the strobile of this plant is crushed into a {@item Khitania columnispicata Paste|PartneredDDDoD|paste} and smeared on a creature's body, that creature gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage for 24 hours. Consuming the {@item Khitania columnispicata Seed|PartneredDDDoD|seeds} of this plant provide {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage for 1 minute.

entries.name: Hyper-thermo-genetic
entries: If the strobile of this plant is crushed into a {@item Khitania columnispicata Paste|PartneredDDDoD|paste} and smeared on a creature's body, that creature gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage for 24 hours. Consuming the {@item Khitania columnispicata Seed|PartneredDDDoD|seeds} of this plant provide {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage for 1 minute.

entries.name: Babel Leaves
entries: If a single {@item Klitzschophyllites flabellatus Leaf|PartneredDDDoD|leaf} is plucked from this plant and placed under the tongue of a creature with an Intelligence score of 8 or more, it is able to speak and comprehend any language for 1 minute. Once the effect wears off, the leaf shrivels and cannot be used again.

item.name: Kriss of Haţeg
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This slender weapon has a wavy oscillating blade engraved with strange symbols.}

{@b Rules:} +3 weapon. A creature hit by an attack with this weapon must succeed a DC (8 + PB) Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} or be reduced by one size category and have the damage from its attacks reduced by {@dice 1d4} for 1 minute. While reduced in size, it cannot be reduced in size again by another attack or similar spell/effect.

item.name: Liaoningocladus boii Pseudofruit
entries: 1. {@b {@i Anaesthetic.}} This tree will yield {@dice 1d20} red {@item Liaoningocladus boii Pseudofruit|PartneredDDDoD|pseudofruits}. These can be eaten and restore 1 hit point each, but also contain a large central seed. If a creature swallows one of these seeds it must succeed a DC 12 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} or become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 24 hours and fall asleep for 1 minute. The creature awakens if it takes damage.

entries.name: Neurotoxic Stimulant
entries: The leaves of this plant are a powerful stimulant. They can be crushed to create a {@item Marsilea sp. Potion|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that, if consumed, gives {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws for 24 hours. However, if the wrong parts of the plant are included in the {@item Marsilea sp. Potion (Incorrectly Harvested)|PartneredDDDoD|potion}, it also inflicts {@damage 2d4} Psychic damage when consumed. When harvesting the plant as an ingredient, a DC 14 {@skill Nature|XPHB} check is required to ensure that only the correct parts are harvested.

entries.name: Neurotoxic Stimulant

Potion|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that, if consumed, gives {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws for 24 hours. However, if the wrong parts of the plant are included in the {@item Marsilea sp. Potion (Incorrectly Harvested)|PartneredDDDoD|potion}, it also inflicts {@damage 2d4} Psychic damage when consumed. When harvesting the plant as an ingredient, a DC 14 {@skill Nature|XPHB} check is required to ensure that only the correct parts are harvested.

item.name: Perfect Refractive Index Crystal
item.reqAttune: by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This large, jagged crystal has a pastel colour hue to it, but when turned in light it refracts brilliant rainbows.}

{@b Rules:} This item can be used as a spell focus by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer. While wielding this item, you may cast the {@spell Light|XPHB} cantrip a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} per day, and you may cast the spell {@spell Color Spray|XPHB|Colour Spray} at 1st level once per day without using a spell slot.

item.name: Potion of Plumage
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This simple vile is filled with feathers immersed in a strange blue liquid.}

{@b Rules:} When this potion is consumed, the creature that drank it sprouts soft downy feathers all over their body and long flight feathers from their forearms for 10 minutes. While under this effect, they have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to falling damage and are able to glide 1 ft. horizontally for every 1 ft. they descend while falling.

item.name: Potion of Redirected Ancestry
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This ornate glass vial is inlaid with gold filigree. It contains a dully-glowing, green liquid that has tiny double helix shapes drifting within it.}

{@b Rules:} Consuming this potion allows you to take on the appearance and abilities of any humanoid species that you share a common ancestor with. These replace your character's original racial/species abilities and appearance. This effect lasts for 1 hour, however if you drink a second {@item Potion of Redirected Ancestry|PartneredDDDoD} while under this effect, the change becomes permanent unless removed by a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

item.name: Primal Drums
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A small set of palm drums that are fashioned traditionally from skin stretched over hollowed wood.}

{@b Rules:} This instrument can be used as a spell focus by a Bard. Once per day, as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, these drums can be used to cast the spell {@spell Bless|XPHB} at 1st level without requiring a spell slot or components.

item.name: Pure Lotus Broach/Barrette
entries: {@i Appearance:} A large perfectly formed lotus flower, coloured with soft pink and white petals.

{@i Rules:} This flower hardens into a durable porcelain form and can be attached to clothing or hair. While attuned to this item, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws.

item.name: Research Scrolls
entries: This extensive collection of scrolls and paper notes contains useful information about biology and the natural world.

items.name: Ability:
items.entry: Intelligence

items.name: Utilize:
items.entry: When attempting a {@skill History|XPHB} check to recall information about an animal, plant, or natural feature (geographical or geological), you may replace the check's DC with this tool's DC (DC 8).

item.name: Ring of Palaeobotany
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This wooden ring has a large emerald inlay. Within the emerald is a single tiny golden leaf.}
{@b Rules:} While wearing this ring you are able to recognise all ancient plants (that existed before your original timeline/lifespan) and you have knowledge of their uses and dangers.

item.name: Ring of Primal Speaking
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This small gold ring has the visage of a toothed maw biting onto a gemstone.}
{@b Rules:} While wearing this ring, you can read, speak, and understand Archosauric.

entries.name: Antiseptic
entries: The {@item Ruffordia goeppertii Root|PartneredDDDoD|roots} of this plant have a horribly bitter taste, but also have medicinal properties. Eating them grants {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 24 hours.

entries.name: Synaptic Regulator
entries: The small dry {@item Sabalites longirhachis Fruits|PartneredDDDoD|fruits} that this plant produces have a bitter taste and cause a creature to feel nauseous for a few minutes if consumed. However, they also stimulate the nervous system and provide that creature {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence Saving Throws for the next 24 hours.

item.name: Shell Coin
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This shell has been carved into a small disc. It retains many of the surface features of the shell, including ribbing and growth lines.}

{@b Rules:} When entering a settlement of 100 inhabitants or more, this shell takes on the appearance of the highest value coin for that settlement. A DC 12 {@skill Arcana|XPHB} check can determine that the coin is magical, but an effect that dispels magic is required to reveal its illusion.

entries.name: Psychoactive
entries: This plant is used as a key ingredient in spiced ales and is highly valued by some merchants. It can also be brewed into a delicious {@item Siphonospermum simplex Brew|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that provides {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws for 1 hour when consumed.

item.name: Staff of Time Sight
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This wooden and brass staff is topped by a large, spinning brass sphere. This sphere is orbited by several smaller brass spheres that are not physically connected to the staff, yet cannot be removed from their orbit.}

{@b Rules:} This +2 {@item staff|XPHB} can be used as a spell focus by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer. This {@item staff|XPHB} has two charges. While wielding this {@item staff|XPHB}, at the end of your turn in combat, you may choose to expend 1 of its charges. If you do, undo your entire turn (all Actions, movement, and damage dealt/received) and re-take your turn. The {@item staff|XPHB} regains 1 charge each day at dawn.

item.name: Staff of Unspared Expense
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This pale ivory-coloured staff is topped with a piece of polished amber that contains a large insect fossil.}

{@b Rules:} This +3 {@item staff|XPHB} can be used as a spell focus by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer. While wielding this {@item staff|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Charisma checks and Charisma Saving Throws.

{@b Curse:} While in possession of this {@item staff|XPHB}, all vendors try to sell their wares at prices 50% more expensive than normal to you. This {@item staff|XPHB} is cursed and, once attuned, a player cannot unattune to it. If they were to abandon the {@item staff|XPHB}, it appears among their belongings during the next {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The curse can be broken by selling the {@item staff|XPHB} at 200% of its usual value (DM's choice).

Alternatively, the curse can be broken by destroying the {@item staff|XPHB} by succeeding on a DC 25 Strength check. If the {@item staff|XPHB} is destroyed in this manner, a blinding flash of light emits from the shattered amber, then heavy and intermittent stomping footsteps can be heard in the distance that steadily grow louder. This is the sound of a {@creature Young Tyrannosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|young}/{@creature Tyrannosaurus Rex|XMM|adult}/{@creature Ancient Tyrannosaurus Rex|PartneredDDDoD|ancient} {@i Tyrannosaurus rex} approaching (age depends on the party level, at DM's discretion). It is {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to the party, cannot be tamed, and will pursue them as long as it can. It will actively hunt them if the party escapes.

item.name: Survivalist's Kit
entries: This kit is used to carefully extract natural medicines from plants and animals. It consists of a small flint-knapped blade, wooden tweezers, water-proof pouches, and adhesives.

items.name: Ability:
items.entry: Wisdom

items.name: Utilize:
items.entry: When attempting a {@skill Medicine|XPHB} check while in a Forest, Jungle, Island, or Swamp environment, you may replace the check's DC with this kit's DC (DC 8).

item.name: Theropod Jaw
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This huge axe is crafted from the harvested jaw of a mighty predatory dinosaur.}
{@b Rules:} This weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage with each successful hit.

item.name: Trusty Rusty
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This worn pick is rusted and corroding, but still maintains a sharp point.}
{@b Rules:} +3 weapon. While wielding this weapon, you gain a burrowing speed of 5 ft. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against creatures made of rock or stone.

item.name: Wand of the Wondering Mind
entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A simple, wooden wand bound with twine and a small feather embedded in its tip.}

{@b Rules:} This wand has 3 charges. While holding it, you can use an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to expend 1 of its charges and a beast you can see within 40 ft. of you must make a DC 12 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}. On a failed save, select Behaviour Table (see {@book Mesozoic Reptiles in Your Worlds|PartneredDDDoD|9|Behaviour}). You may then roll two dice for a behaviour and select whichever option of the two you prefer. The creature then behaves in that manner.
This wand regains all expended charges every day at dawn.

entries.name: Congestant
entries: The thick {@item Weichselia reticulata Stem|PartneredDDDoD|stem} of this plant causes a creature's sinuses and ear canals to swell if chewed, dulling their hearing. A creature that chews this stem gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Thunder damage for 24 hours, but also has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks that involve sound for 24 hours.

itemGroup.reqAttune: by a Druid, Wizard, or Sorcerer
items: Exceptional Refractive Index Crystal|PartneredDDDoD
Flawless Refractive Index Crystal|PartneredDDDoD
Perfect Refractive Index Crystal|PartneredDDDoD

entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i A metal trumpet-like gun with a wide nozzle and bespoke wooden handle.}

{@b Rules:} This weapon can be loaded with any type of ammunition, or alternatively pebbles, scrap, or any cluster of small items you desire. However, its range becomes 60 ft. if you do so. Additionally, a DM can alter the damage type of this weapon to match what it is loaded with (i.e. putting a large rock in could change the damage to Bludgeoning, or icicles could change it to Cold damage).
{@b Appearance:} {@i Heavy sculpted armour with a horned helm and shoulders in the visage of a large ceratopsian.}

{@b Rules:} +1 or +2 armour. If you move at least 20 ft. in a straight line towards a creature and end your movement within 5 ft. of it, you may use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to strike the creature, dealing Bludgeoning damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and Piercing damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to it.
You and the creature must then make contested Strength checks. If you win, the struck creature is also knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.
{@b Appearance:} {@i A thick coat of feathers lined with leather on the inside.}

{@b Rules:} +1 or +2 armour. While attuned to this item, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to falling damage. When taking falling damage, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to instead gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to falling damage until the end of your turn.
{@b Appearance:} {@i This gnarled sword is covered in sharp teeth embedded into its cutting edge.}

{@b Rules:} A creature hit by an attack with this weapon gains one level of "Bleed Effect", as described below. The bonus conveyed by +1/+2/+3 versions of this weapon do not increase the damage this weapon deals when hitting, but instead add additional levels of "Bleed Effect" equal to the weapon's bonus (i.e. a +1 sword applies a total of 2 levels of Bleed Effect per hit).
{@b Bleed Effect (cumulative):}

items: A creature with this affect suffers 1 Slashing damage at the start of its turn in combat for each level of bleed effect it has.

Outside of combat, a creature suffers 1 Slashing damage every minute for each level of bleed effect it has, so long as it is not taking a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
One level of bleed effect is removed per hit point of healing received.

All bleed effects can be simultaneously removed by completing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, being restored to full health, or by a successful {@skill Medicine|XPHB} check (DC 6 + level of bleed effect, to a maximum of 15).

{@b Appearance:} {@i This hammer has a broad flat head, and the back of the hammer is pointed into a triangular edge.}
{@b Rules:} In addition to its use as a weapon, this item can be used as a tool to efficiently extract resources from rock.
{@b Appearance:} {@i This wooden crossbow's end is carved into the beaked-mouth of a Protoceratops and its frill forms the crossbow's sights.}

{@b Rules:} This weapon's bolts detonate with tiny spines on impact. When a creature is hit by an attack made with this weapon, {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage is inflicted to each creature within 5 ft. of the hit target.

{@b Appearance:} {@i This slender bow is made from pterosaur bones and stringed with a fine muscle tendon. The tendon can magically extend into a full wing membrane, connecting and wrapping the bones to form a gliding wing.}

{@b Rules:} +2 weapon. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the bow can be unfurled into a gliding wing, allowing the wielder to descend safely from any height, so long as they are not {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. Additionally, they may glide 2 ft. in any horizontal direction for every 1 ft. they descend, without using any movement. When descending in this manner, you do not take falling damage.

The bonus conveyed by +1/+2/+3 versions of this weapon do not increase the damage this weapon deals when hitting, but instead add additional levels of "Bleed Effect" equal to the weapon's bonus (i.e. a +1 sword applies a total of 2 levels of Bleed Effect per hit).
{@b Bleed Effect (cumulative):}

items: A creature with this affect suffers 1 Slashing damage at the start of its turn in combat for each level of bleed effect it has.

Outside of combat, a creature suffers 1 Slashing damage every minute for each level of bleed effect it has, so long as it is not taking a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
One level of bleed effect is removed per hit point of healing received.

All bleed effects can be simultaneously removed by completing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, being restored to full health, or by a successful {@skill Medicine|XPHB} check (DC 6 + level of bleed effect, to a maximum of 15).

entries: {@b Appearance:} {@i This bony mace is topped with a large bulbous head. Despite its size, it is remarkably light.}
{@b Rules:} This weapon weighs half as much as it usually would, but is just as effective.
{@b Appearance:} {@i A long pole with a bladed steel tip and a hooped ring of rope dangling from the end. A line of rope then runs parallel to the shaft and can be pulled to open or close the hoop.}

{@b Rules:} +1 weapon. While attuned to this weapon, you may attempt to tame an animal an additional time per day (either the same animal or a different one, see {@book Mesozoic Reptiles in Your Worlds|PartneredDDDoD|9|Taming and Domestication}).

language.name: Archosauric
entries: Accompanying these species is an additional custom language. Archosauric (or Archosauran) is the official/state language of the species described in this book and may be selected as one of your player character's languages. We envision it as the root language of fantasy dragon and bird languages, despite those languages' great differences. As such, it functionally sounds like a hybrid of the two, sharing features of both. Archosauric combines high-pitched clicks and whistles with deep guttural growls and rolling harsh syllables. The frequency and abundance of these two starkly different tones within the language are typically a result of the formality of the conversation. That is, higher pitched clicks and squarks are usually casual slang, whereas deeper tones are more formal, although there is certainly intermingling between the two in many conversations.

trait.name: Power Over Speed
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws, but {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all Dexterity checks and Dexterity Saving Throws.

trait.name: Territorial Titan
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks with its Strongest Bite against creatures with a size category of Huge or Gargantuan.

trait.name: When Dinosaurs Ruled the Earth
entries: All non-Tyrannosaurus beasts that can see Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

Every minute while within line of sight of Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex, or at the end of each of its turns in combat, a beast can make a {@dc 17} Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to this Trait for 24 hours. Succeeding this Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} does not grant {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex's Iconic Bellow.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries: If Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, it can choose to succeed it instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex makes one Strongest Bite attack and one Crushing Tail Slam attack.

action.name: Strongest Bite
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+13, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}23 ({@damage 3d12 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 23 ({@damage 3d12 + 4}) Force damage, and the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions (escape {@dc 21}). Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex cannot use its Strongest Bite attack against any other creature until the Grapple ends, but gains an additional {@hit 5} to hit with its Strongest Bite attack against the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} creature.

action.name: Crushing Tail Slam
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 21}, each other creature within a 10 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that is not {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex. {@actSaveFail} 28 ({@damage 3d12 + 9}) Bludgeoning damage and the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Iconic Bellow
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 20}, each non-Tyrannosaur creature within a 200 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that can hear Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex. {@actSaveFail} 13 ({@damage 1d12 + 7}) Psychic damage and the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A creature may repeat this saving throw at the end of their turns (do not take the Psychic damage). {@actSaveSuccess} {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition effects of Iconic Bellow for 24 hours.

legendary.name: Lunging Head Bash
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex can move up to 10 ft., then make the following attack:
Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+13, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}20 ({@damage 2d10 + 9}) Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Imparted Speech
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex can understand Archosauric and another language of your choosing (usually Common). It can speak Archosauric, albeit slowly. Increase its Intelligence score to 8.

items.name: Wise Old Beast
entries: Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Ankylier Enchanter casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}, {@hit 7} to hit with spell attacks):

trait.name: Osteoderms
entries: Ankylier Enchanter's AC is increased by 3 (included above), but it cannot benefit from its Dexterity modifier to improve its AC.

trait.name: Industrial Enchanter
entries: When performing the Enchant Weapon or Enchant Armour {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, Ankylier Enchanter may choose to spend an hour doing this instead of a single {@variantrule Action|XPHB}. If it does so, the enchantment becomes permanent until replaced by a similar effect and is not lost when another weapon/armour is enchanted.

trait.name: Arcane Intuition
entries: Ankylier Enchanter has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Saving Throws to avoid the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition and prevent {@variantrule Curses|XPHB}.

action.name: Enchant Weapon
entries: Select a weapon that Ankylier Enchanter can see and is within 40 ft. of it. For the next 1 minute, that weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d6} damage of any type of your choosing.

If that weapon already had this effect (or a similar effect) applied to it, the new effect temporarily overrides it. Only one weapon may be enchanted by this {@variantrule Action|XPHB} at a time and if a new weapon is enchanted, the effect ends on the previous one.

action.name: Enchant Armour
entries: Select a set of armour that Ankylier Enchanter can see and is within 40 ft. of it. For the next 1 minute, that armour provides the wearer with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one damage type of your choosing.

If that armour already had this effect (or a similar effect) applied to it, the new effect temporarily overrides it. Only one armour may be enchanted by this {@variantrule Action|XPHB} at a time and if a new armour is enchanted, the effect ends on the previous one.

action.name: Blessing Rod
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Force damage.

trait.name: Osteoderms
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster's AC is increased by 3 (included above), but it cannot benefit from its Dexterity modifier to improve its AC.

trait.name: Rippling Muscles
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks, Strength Saving Throws, and {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks.

trait.name: Forge Master
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster is an expert blacksmith, has {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with Smith's Tools, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage (included above).

trait.name: Forge Armament
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster can create a metal +1 weapon or armour during a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, so long as it has the raw materials and an anvil.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster makes two Forge Greatmaul attacks.

action.name: Forge Greatmaul (+1)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 1d10 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 ({@damage 3d6}) Fire damage.

legendary.name: Clubbed Tail
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}: {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 17}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

legendary.name: Give Order
entries: Ankylier Forgemaster gives a verbal command to an Ankylier Karl within 60 ft. that can hear it. That Ankylier Karl can immediately move up to 25 ft. and take an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

trait.name: Osteoderms
entries: Ankylier Karl's AC is increased by 3 (included above), but it cannot benefit from its Dexterity modifier to improve its AC.

trait.name: Impressive Physique
entries: Ankylier Karl has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intimidation checks.

action.name: Smith's Hammer
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Clubbed Tail
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 2}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Show of Strength (1/Day)
entries: Ankylier Karl flexes, giving itself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its next Strength Check or Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, but {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next Dexterity Check or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sail Reliant Reptilian Metabolism
entries: During the day, Arizonasaurus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. During the night, Arizonasaurus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.

action.name: Bite and Shake
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Piercing damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Slashing damage and, if the hit creature is Medium or smaller, the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition until the start of Arizonasaurus' next turn.

bonus.name: Dorsal Sail Flush
entries: Arizonasaurus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intimidation Checks for the next 1 minute.

items.name: Arizona Heat
entries: Arizonasaurus radiates incredible heat. At the end of each of Arizonasaurus' turns, each creature in a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from Arizonasaurus takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage. Then, each creature in a 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} takes an additional 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage. Arizonasaurus has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage.
If there are multiple Arizonasaurus persisting in a region with this Trait, that region will experience a prolonged drought.

trait.name: Dexterous Aquatic Predator
entries: While submerged in water, the Bahariyan Polycotylid has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity checks, {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws, {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Saving Throws to prevent the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, and has immunity to the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition (included above). The Bahariyan Polycotylid can also hold its breath for up to 10 minutes.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Bahariyan Polycotylid makes one Swim-by Bite attack and one Paddle Slap attack.

action.name: Swim-by Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d6 + 6}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Paddle Slap
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d4 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Stir Mud
entries: The Bahariyan Polycotylid uses its paddles to stir up sediment from the riverbed/seabed. For 30 seconds all connected water within 30 ft. becomes clouded with mud, rendering it opaque. A creature submerged in this water has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition and is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}.

items.name: Echosnap
entries: The Bahariyan Polycotylid has a Blindsight of 40 ft.

trait.name: Ambush Predator
entries: Balaur has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Stealth checks.

trait.name: Flutter-Leap
