These creatures will now steal eggs and/or young of other species (including humanoids), but rather than devouring them, will instead care for them diligently and raise them as their own. Oviraptor has proficiency in {@skill Stealth|XPHB} checks (for a total of +5) while stealing offspring.

trait.name: Immutable Stature*
entries: Paralititan is immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} and {@condition Prone|XPHB} conditions (included above). It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength Saving Throws, and any {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to resist the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions. However, it automatically fails any Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}.

Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing attacks have no effect on it as its hide is far too thick (included above). Attacks from Huge and Gargantuan creatures/sources bypass this {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.

action.name: Rear Up
entries: Paralititan rears up onto its hind limbs. Its speed is reduced to 0 ft. and it is able to use its Almighty Stomp attack until it is no longer rearing up.
If Paralititan attacks, it lands on all fours and it ceases rearing up.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Paralititan makes (A) two Huge Stomp attacks, or (B) one Almighty Stomp attack if it is Rearing Up.

action.name: Huge Stomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}28 ({@damage 4d8 + 10}) Bludgeoning damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 16}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Almighty Stomp
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 15}, reach 10 ft., up to two targets. {@h}75 ({@damage 10d10 + 20}) Bludgeoning damage and the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Any non-magical metal, stone, or wooden objects hit by this attack that are not being carried or worn are shattered and destroyed. {@actSave str} {@dc 16}, each non-sauropod creature within a 30 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Paralititan must be rearing up to use this attack.

bonus.name: Bellowing Call
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 16}, each non-Paralititan creature within a 60 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} {@variantrule Condition|XPHB} for 1 minute. A creature may repeat this {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} at the end of each of their turns. {@actSaveSuccess} {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of Bellowing Call for 24 hours.

items.name: Lightning Rod
entries: The first time Paralititan uses its Bellowing Call {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} each day, the sky darkens and storm clouds form directly above it. For the next hour, each time Paralititan uses its Bellowing Call, include this additional effect: {@actSave str} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 60 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} (including Paralititan). {@actSaveFail} 16 ({@damage 3d10}) Lightning damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.
After an hour passes, the storm clears.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Pluvenn Flowertender casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit 4} to hit with spell attacks):

trait.name: Rose Picker
entries: Pluvenn Flowertender has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing damage (included above).

trait.name: Pinning Grapple
entries: Pluvenn Flowertender has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Unarmed Strikes if it is attempting to Grapple the target. If a creature is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by Pluvenn Flowertender, it takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage.

trait.name: Nocturnal/Diurnal
entries: Pluvenn Flowertender only requires 4 hours of sleep per day

action.name: Weed-Pulling Razormaw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Piercing damage.

trait.name: Pinning Grapple
entries: Pluvenn Huntleader has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Unarmed Strikes if it is attempting to Grapple the target. If a creature is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by Pluvenn Huntleader, it takes {@damage 1d4 + 3} Piercing damage.

trait.name: Master of the Hunt
entries: Pluvenn Huntleader only requires 4 hours of sleep per day, unless pursuing a marked target, in which case it only requires 2 hours of sleep per day. Pluvenn Huntleader also has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Athletics checks for climbing.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Pluvenn Huntleader makes any combination of three Exquisite Longsword attacks, Wrist Crossbow attacks, and {@variantrule Grappling|XPHB} Hook attacks.

action.name: Exquisite Longsword (+1)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d8 + 6}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Wrist Crossbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 60 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 5}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Grappling Hook
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 40 ft., one target. {@h}2 (2) Piercing damage plus the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 15}). Pluvenn Huntleader does not gain the benefits of its Pinning Grapple Trait for this Grapple and it must use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} if it chooses to end the Grapple.

bonus.name: Mark Target
entries: Pluvenn Huntleader applies a magical mark to a target that it can see within 60 ft. The mark is a blood-red, dully-glowing symbol.

The mark can only be removed via magical means (i.e. {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} or a similar effect), if the marked creature dies, or if Pluvenn Huntleader dies. Alternatively, Pluvenn Huntleader may dismiss the mark at will.
Pluvenn Huntleader has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Survival checks to pursue a marked target and its attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d6} damage (of the same damage type) to the target.
Only one mark per Pluvenn Huntleader may be active at a time.

bonus.name: Endure Pain
entries: {@actTrigger} Pluvenn Huntleader is hit by an attack. {@actResponse} Pluvenn Huntleader has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to either Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Pinning Grapple
entries: Pluvenn Villager has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Unarmed Strikes if it is attempting to Grapple the target. If a creature is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by Pluvenn Villager, it takes {@damage 1d4 - 1} Piercing damage (minimum of 1).

trait.name: Nocturnal/Diurnal
entries: Pluvenn Villager only requires 4 hours of sleep per day.

trait.name: Community Member
entries: Select one skill from the list below, this Pluvenn Villager gains a +3 bonus to any checks for that skill. Alternatively, you can select any tool (excluding Forgery Kit, Poisoner's Kit, and Thieves' Tools) and this Pluvenn Villager instead gains proficiency with that tool and an additional +1 bonus to any checks with it.

items: {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}
{@skill History|XPHB}
{@skill Medicine|XPHB}
{@skill Nature|XPHB}
{@skill Performance|XPHB}
{@skill Persuasion|XPHB}
Religion This Pluvenn Villager should be appropriately dressed in simple clothing to match their community contribution/role.

action.name: Razormaw Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 2}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

trait.name: Vast Herd
entries: Psittacosaurus swarm in vast herds of dozens to hundreds of individuals, roaming the mountainsides, rivers, and hills. When fleeing from a threat, it is difficult to make out individual Psittacosaurus among the crowd. So long as there are three or more Psittacosaurus fleeing within 20 ft. of each other, Ranged Attack Rolls against them have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

trait.name: Group Sentinel
entries: If three or more Psittacosaurus are together, select one of them to be the Group Sentinel. That Psittacosaurus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Perception checks.

action.name: Beak Snap
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Quill Stab
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Quilled Back
entries: {@actTrigger} Psittacosaurus is hit by a Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB} within 5 ft. {@actResponse} Psittacosaurus makes a Quill Stab attack at the attacking creature.

items.name: Quill Spray
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 11}, each creature in a 10 ft. {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

trait.name: Filter-Feeder
entries: Pterodaustro cannot gain the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition or be damaged by contaminated or laced food or water.

trait.name: Group Sentinel
entries: If three or more Pterodaustro are within 50 ft. of each other, select one of them to be the Group Sentinel. That Pterodaustro has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Perception checks and all other Pterodaustro in the group lose this Group Sentinel Trait.

action.name: Wing-Buffet
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Quad-Launch (Pterodaustro)
entries: If it is standing on the ground, Pterodaustro launches itself into the air. {@actSave str} {@dc 8}, each other creature in a 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Pterodaustro flies 10 ft. in a straight line.
Pterodaustro can only begin flying by using this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or if it is falling.

items.name: Swallowed Gemstone
entries: When encountering a group of Pterodaustro, one or more of them may be enchanted with a magical element from a gemstone they have swallowed. That Pterodaustro will glow with a soft hue and the damage type of its attacks will change to the corresponding type for that gemstone. You may roll a {@dice D10} or select from the table below to determine the gemstone swallowed, colour hue, and damage type:
When Pterodaustro is slain, the gemstone it swallowed is regurgitated (worth 50 GP).

trait.name: Stalking Stalk, Silent Glider
entries: If Quetzalcoatlus is walking within a forest or is flying, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Stealth checks.

trait.name: Vicious Descent
entries: If Quetzalcoatlus began the turn flying and subsequently lands before making an attack, increase the damage of its first Colossal Peck attack by {@dice 1d10} this turn.

trait.name: Eye in the Sky
entries: While fling, Quetzalcoatlus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Perception checks that involve sight.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Quetzalcoatlus makes three Colossal Peck attacks.

action.name: Colossal Peck
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}19 ({@damage 2d10 + 8}) Piercing damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 16}, a Medium or Small creature hit by this attack. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Thunderous Flap {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 15 ft. {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Bludgeoning damage plus 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Thunder damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

bonus.name: Quad Launch (Quetzalcoatlus)
entries: If it is standing on the ground, Quetzalcoatlus launches itself into the air. {@actSave str} {@dc 16}, each other creature in a 10 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Quetzalcoatlus flies 20 ft. in a straight line.
Quetzalcoatlus can only begin flying by using this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or if it is falling.

items.name: Low-Gravity Aura
entries: Quetzalcoatlus drastically reduces the weight of objects and creatures in contact with it (including itself). A real Quetzalcoatlus would usually be able to carry a maximum weight of about 80-100 lb. This Trait to increases its carry weight limit to 500 lb. and any howdah or saddle attached to it are considered weightless for the purposes of its carry weight. For each 100 lb. Quetzalcoatlus is carrying, reduce its fly speed by 10 ft.

items.name: Aircraft-Sized Animal
entries: Quetzalcoatlus can carry up to three Medium (or smaller) humanoids on its back, and two further Medium (or smaller) humanoids in its hind claws. For each creature carried in this way, Quetzalcoatlus' fly speed is reduced by 10 ft.
If Quetzalcoatlus is carrying two or more creatures using this rule, it cannot use its Lift Off {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Feathered God
entries: You may choose for Quetzalcoatlus to be covered in vivid feathers.

items.name: Lift Off
entries: While flying, Quetzalcoatlus picks up an object or creature weighing up to 500 lb. and up to Large in size. While carrying this object, its fly speed is reduced by 10 ft. for each 100 lb. the object/creature weighs.

items.name: Drop Off
entries: While flying, Quetzalcoatlus drops an object or creature it is holding: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16} or 12 (if dropped from above 50 ft.), a creature below Quetzalcoatlus. {@actSaveFail} The creature below takes 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage, or 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Bludgeoning damage (if from above 50 ft.). {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The dropped object/creature takes appropriate falling damage.

trait.name: Morbid Regurgitation
entries: Rhamphorhynchus vomits up its stomach contents upon death. {@actSave dex} {@dc 8}, one creature within 5 ft. of Rhamphorhynchus. {@actSaveFail} 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Acid damage.

trait.name: Growth Spurt
entries: Rhamphorhynchus can be found as either a juvenile (Tiny) or adult (Small) creature.

action.name: Spike-Toothed Snap
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Swooping Evasion
entries: {@actTrigger} Rhamphorhynchus is hit by an Opportunity Attack or must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}. {@actResponse} Rhamphorhynchus increases its AC by 3, potentially causing the attack to miss, and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws until the end of the turn.

items.name: Snatch & Swallow
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 12}, one creature within 5 ft. of Rhamphorhynchus. {@actSaveFail} Rhamphorhynchus snatches and swallows a small item (trinket, Potion, wand, dagger, etc.) that it can see that the creature is wielding or has on their clothing.

If the item is a wand, Rhamphorhynchus' Spike-Toothed Snap damage type becomes Force (or another appropriate damage type). If the item is a Potion or food, Rhamphorhynchus consumes that item. Any swallowed non-food or non-potion item is regurgitated upon Rhamphorhynchus' death, and each Potion is returned as an empty vial.

trait.name: Morbid Regurgitation (Swarm)
entries: Each time Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm) drops below the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} thresholds of 34, 24, 14, and 4, one of its members vomits up its stomach contents, causing the following effect: {@actSave dex} {@dc 12}, one creature within 5 ft. of Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm). {@actSaveFail} 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Acid damage.

trait.name: Swarming Flurry
entries: Melee attacks against Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm) are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

trait.name: Naive Juveniles
entries: This swarm is composed entirely of inexperienced juvenile animals. It has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny beast. The swarm can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

The swarm has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Prone|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions (included above).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm) makes five Spike-Toothed Snap attacks.

action.name: Spike-Toothed Snap
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Enchanted Swarm
entries: Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm) has already snatched dozens of magical items and incorporated them into their attacks. Each time Rhamphorhynchus swarm makes a Spike-Toothed Snap attack, you may roll a {@dice D10} and change the damage type of the attack according to the list below:

trait.name: Oblivious and Armored*
entries: Scelidosaurus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and creatures that hit it with melee attacks take {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage. It automatically fails and Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}.

action.name: Serrated Tail
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Slashing damage.

reaction.name: Razor Osteoderms
entries: {@actTrigger} Scelidosaurus is hit by a melee attack. {@actResponse} Scelidosaurus increases the Slashing damage of its Oblivious and Armored Trait to {@dice 2d4}.

items.name: Domesticatable
entries: Scelidosaurus is particularly trustful of Small and Medium-sized creatures, largely due to its formidable defences. It is relatively easy to domesticate, and players can befriend a Scelidosaurus by feeding it consistently for a {@dice 1d4 + 1} days. However, its Razor Osteoderms prevent Scelidosaurus from being ridden without a bespoke saddle. Nevertheless, they make for friendly travelling companions.

trait.name: Pelvic Membrane
entries: Sharovipteryx has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to falling damage and can move up to 2 ft. horizontally for every 1 ft. it descends in the air, at no movement cost.
While descending in the air in this manner (or while flying if you are using the Optional Magical Rules), Sharovipteryx does not provoke Opportunity Attacks when it moves out of an enemy's reach.

action.name: Gliding Snap
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}1 (1) Piercing damage.
Sharovipteryx may only use this attack while descending in the air (or while flying if you are using the Optional Magical Rules).

items.name: Familiar
entries: Sharovipteryx may be used as a familiar via the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell or any similar effect.

items.name: Podopteryx (1/Day)
entries: Sharovipteryx takes on the appearance of its original namesake, the Damselfly Podopteryx, for 1 minute. During this time, it has a 40 ft. fly speed, its size becomes Tiny, and its AC becomes 17.

trait.name: Crocodile Mimic
entries: Spinosaurus can hold its breath for up to 30 minutes.

trait.name: Rostral Dermal Pressure Sensors
entries: While submerged in water, Spinosaurus has Blindsight 10 ft. (included above).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Spinosaurus makes one Snapping Jaw attack and one Hooked Claw attack.

action.name: Snapping Jaw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}27 ({@damage 5d6 + 10}) Piercing damage, the hit creature is pulled up to 5 ft. directly towards Spinosaurus, and the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 16}). Spinosaurus cannot attack another target with its Snapping Jaw attack until the Grapple ends.

action.name: Hooked Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}21 ({@damage 3d8 + 8}) Slashing damage and moved up to 5 ft. in a direction of Spinosaurus' choice.

reaction.name: Reactionary Thermoregulation
entries: {@actTrigger} Spinosaurus is hit by an attack or makes a {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}. {@actResponse} Spinosaurus has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to either Cold or Fire damage until the end of the turn.

items.name: Dramatic Reinterpretation
entries: Select one option listed below and apply it to Spinosaurus. The next time the party encounter a Spinosaurus, select a different option, which overrides the previously selected option.

items: Increase Spinosaurus' Strength to 28, but decrease its Dexterity to 10. Its attacks deal {@damage 1d8} additional damage (of the same damage type), but subtract 2 from any rolls to hit.
Change Spinosaurus' speed to 60 ft., but it may no longer swim.
Increase Spinosaurus' AC to 20.
Spinosaurus gains a fly speed of 40 ft. (This may not be selected the first time a party encounter Spinosaurus).

trait.name: Aquatic
entries: Stomatosuchus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Stealth checks while submerged in water. It can hold its breath for up to 30 minutes.

trait.name: Size Matters
entries: Stomatosuchus will not attack a creature of Medium size or larger, unless to defend itself or its feeding grounds.

trait.name: Throat Pouch
entries: Stomatosuchus can hold Small or Tiny creatures in its throat pouch (see Needle Maw).
If Stomatosuchus becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, it will regurgitate any creature in its throat pouch. If a creature dies while in the throat pouch, Stomatosuchus consumes it.

trait.name: Crocodilian Immune System
entries: Stomatosuchus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition (included above).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Stomatosuchus makes one Needle Maw attack and one Tail Swipe attack.

action.name: Needle Maw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 14} (Stomatosuchus can only have one creature in its Throat Pouch at a time). {@actSaveFail} The creature is swallowed into the Throat Pouch, has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and {@condition Blinded|XPHB} conditions, has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from attacks and effects outside of Stomatosuchus, and takes 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of their turns (escape {@dc 14} Strength Check).

action.name: Tail Swipe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Careless Swallow
entries: Stomatosuchus gulps huge volumes of water daily as it filters out tiny fish to devour. In doing so, it occasionally swallows small gemstones or trinkets that wash into the water. Roll a {@dice d6} and consult the list below, Stomatosuchus gains the corresponding effect.

items.name: Gemstone
items.entry: Select a damage type from Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. Stomatosuchus' Needle Maw attack deals an additional {@damage 1d4} damage of that type and also change the damage of its Throat Pouch to that type.

items.name: Ring of Protection
items.entry: Increase Stomatosuchus' AC by 1.

items.name: Holy Symbol
items.entry: Stomatosuchus has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

items.name: Gold Coins
items.entry: Stomatosuchus' throat pouch deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage and it regurgitates 100 GP when slain.

items.name: Wand Shard
items.entry: Stomatosuchus knows either the {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB}, {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB}, or {@spell Thunderclap|XPHB} cantrip (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 4} to hit with spell attacks). It may cast this cantrip as though it were level 5.

items.name: Ticking Clock
items.entry: Stomatosuchus loses its {@variantrule Size|XPHB} Matters Trait and becomes exceptionally aggressive. It also constantly makes a faint ticking sound.

items.name: Treasure Trove
entries: When Stomatosuchus is slain, its throat pouch contains {@dice 1d4} trinkets, small items, or gemstones (DM's choice, typically including whatever is described above).

trait.name: Bladed Osteoderms
entries: Any creature that hits Struthiosaurus with a melee attack takes {@damage 1d4} Slashing damage.

action.name: Defensive Stance
entries: Struthiosaurus takes up a defensive stance, lowering its head and limbs, only allowing its armoured back to be attacked. This stance lasts until it attacks. Struthiosaurus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage while in this defensive stance.

action.name: Armoured Tackle
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) Slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Rainbow Osteoderms
entries: {@actTrigger} Struthiosaurus is hit by an attack or fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} while in its Defensive Stance. {@actResponse} Struthiosaurus swaps one of its current Resistances to any other damage type of its choosing and its Bladed Osteoderms trait deals an additional {@damage 1d2} damage of that type. This effect lasts until it attacks or uses this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} again.

trait.name: Dip Feeder
entries: Tanystropheus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against creatures that are submerged in water, so long as Tanystropheus' body is not also submerged in water. Tanystropheus can hold its breath for 5 minutes.

trait.name: Farstrike
entries: Tanystropheus often attacks from a concealed position, hiding its body while reaching out with its long neck to strike prey.
If Tanystropheus attacks while Hidden, its first attack deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Tanystropheus makes one Neck Strike attack and one Nip attack.

action.name: Neck Strike
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Bludgeoning damage, plus: Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} (hit creature's choice). {@dc 12}, Medium or smaller hit creature. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Nip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Basal Hydra
entries: Increase Tanystropheus' {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to 58. Each time Tanystropheus takes damage, it grows an additional head up to a maximum of six. When Tanystropheus uses Multiattack, it may make an additional Nip attack for each head beyond the first, up to a maximum of six Nip attacks.
Tanystropheus starts with two heads.

trait.name: Tiny Squiggly Wriggly
entries: So long as Tetrapodophis is in water, attacks against it are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws, and if it would take half damage after succeeding a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} it instead takes none.
Re-interpretation. You may opt for Tetrapodophis to have a burrow speed of 10 ft. instead of a swim speed.

action.name: Vicious Tiny Nip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 1}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}1 (1) Piercing damage.

items.name: Deadly Snake-like Venom
entries: Tetrapodophis is brightly coloured with stripes or other patterns warning of its venomous nature. Tetrapodophis' Vicious Tiny Nip attack gains the following effect when it hits:

{@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} 4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Poison damage, the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, and one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (to a maximum of four). {@actSaveSuccess} The {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (to a maximum of four).

trait.name: Storm Flyer
entries: Tupandactylus has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning and Thunder damage (included above).

trait.name: Focused on Flirting
entries: If Tupandactylus performed a Dazzling Display or Thundering Display, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Perception checks for the next 1 minute.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Tupandactylus makes two Beak-Slash attacks.

action.name: Beak-Slash
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Dazzling Display
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 12}, each creature in a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that can see Tupandactylus. {@actSaveFail} {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma Saving Throws and Charisma Checks for 1 minute. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Tupandactylus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma Saving Throws and Charisma Checks for 1 minute.

bonus.name: Quad Launch (Tupandactylus)
entries: If it is standing on the ground, Tupandactylus launches itself into the air. {@actSave str} {@dc 12}, each other creature in a 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Tupandactylus flies 20 ft. in a straight line.
Tupandactylus can only begin flying by using this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or if it is falling.

items.name: Tupi Thunder God
entries: Tupandactylus takes its name from the Tupi Thunder God. Tupandactylus has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder damage and its Beak-Slash attack deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage.

items.name: Thundering Display {@recharge 3}
entries: Tupandactylus channels the power of thunder, generating a shock wave by vibrating its wings. {@actSave con} {@dc 12}, each other creature in a 15 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Thunder damage and {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the end of their next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

trait.name: Filamentous Mane
entries: "Ubirajara"; gains a +5 bonus to {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks (included above) and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Stealth checks while in foliage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: "Ubirajara" makes three Gnashing Nip attacks.

action.name: Gnashing Nip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) Piercing damage.

reaction.name: Filamentous Integument
entries: {@actTrigger} "Ubirajara" is hit by an attack that deals only Bludgeoning or only Piercing damage. {@actResponse} "Ubirajara" takes half damage from that attack.

items.name: Lord of Spears
entries: "Ubirajara" can alternatively make a single ranged attack whereby it fires spears of filamentous integument at a creature with the following profile:

items.name: Filamentous Spear
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5}, range 30 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Return Home (1/Day)
entries: "Ubirajara" opens an interplanar portal 10 ft. in front of itself. The portal leads to a destination that it considers to be home anywhere in the multiverse and remains open for 1 minute or until "Ubirajara" falls {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. The portal is big enough to allow creatures up to a size of Large through it.

trait.name: Leaping Ambush
entries: If Utahraptor was Hidden at the start of its turn, its Razor-Clawed Kick gains the following benefits this turn:

items: An additional {@hit 3} to hit.
An additional {@damage 1d8 + 3} Slashing damage (as the weight of Utahraptor rends its claws down the target's body).
Any Medium or smaller creature hit by it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition

trait.name: Athletic and Pneumatized
entries: Utahraptor can jump up to 30 ft. from standing and has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to falling damage (included above).

trait.name: Social Hunter
entries: If more than one Utahraptor is tracking a creature together, they all have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Survival and {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks to track that creature.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Utahraptor makes one Vicious Bite attack and one Razor-Clawed Kick attack.

action.name: Vicious Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Razor-Clawed Kick
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage. If the target is smaller than Utahraptor, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 17}). If the target is the same size or larger than Utahraptor and has already been hit by another Razor-Clawed Kick this round (from another Utahraptor), it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 20}).

items.name: Mimicking Cry
entries: Utahraptor can imitate the sound of any creature or noise it has heard with accuracy, much like a parrot. It tends to use this Trait while Hidden to lure prey closer to it.

If a creature uses its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to examine the sound, it can determine that it is a mimicked effect with a successful {@dc 14} {@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Perception|XPHB} check.

trait.name: Feathered and Pneumatized
entries: Velociraptor can leap up to 15 ft. from standing. It has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to falling damage, unless {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} in which case it has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to falling damage instead (included above).

trait.name: Grasping Predator
entries: If Velociraptor hits a creature the same size or larger than itself with its Clawed Kick, it can opt to grasp onto it. Whenever that creature moves, Velociraptor moves with it (without using any of its own movement) and is considered to be occupying the same space as it. A Small creature has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition while Velociraptor is grasping onto it.

As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, the hit creature may make a {@dc 12} Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to remove Velociraptor, ending this effect and pushing Velociraptor 5 ft. directly away from it on a success. Alternatively, Velociraptor may choose to end this effect at any time.
If two or more Velociraptor are grasping the same Medium or Large creature with this Trait, halve that creature's speed.

trait.name: Silent Ambush
entries: Velociraptor can move without making a sound. It automatically passes any {@skill Stealth|XPHB} check to avoid being detected by sound while Hidden. Other creature's {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks that would detect Velociraptor only by sound automatically fail.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Velociraptor makes one Sharp Bite attack and one Clawed Kick attack.

action.name: Sharp Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 5}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Clawed Kick
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Vivid Familial Groups
entries: Each time the party encounter Velociraptor, it may be present in groups of 3-6 animals, representing a family group. Some of these animals may be Hidden nearby. This group consists of an adult male, adult female, and 1-4 subadult animals.
These animals all share a similar dazzling under-plumage that is hidden by overlying feathers (it does not hinder their ability to be stealthy) and is unique to their group.

items.name: Dazzling Reveal
entries: Velociraptor unleashes a dazzling array of magical display feathers. {@actSave dex} {@dc 12}, one creature withing 30 ft. that can see Velociraptor. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage of a type corresponding to the feather's colours (DM's choice).

trait.name: Subsurface Monster
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light can hold its breath for up to 10 hours and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Stealth checks while submerged in water.

trait.name: Bioluminescence
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light can opt to emit a dull glow of any colour, creating dim light for 40 ft. around it. It can activate/deactivate this light at will at any time but, while active, it cannot take the Hide action.

trait.name: Oscillating Thermoregulation
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold and Fire damage (included above).

trait.name: Intelligent
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light is capable of planning in combat and is able to use its environment to help defeat foes (i.e., drowning foes or causing cave collapses).

trait.name: Rostral Dermal Pressure Sensors
entries: While in water, Wretchglow, the Last Light has Blindsight 10 ft. (included above).

action.name: Bioluminescent Flash {@recharge 5}
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light unleashes a bright flash of light. {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 40 ft, {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that can see Wretchglow, the Last Light. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 2 rounds.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light makes one Colossal Needle-Toothed Jaws attack and one Hooked Claw attack.

action.name: Colossal Needle-Toothed Jaws
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+11, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}32 ({@damage 6d6 + 11}) Piercing damage and the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 19}). Wretchglow, the Last Light cannot use its Colossal Needle-Toothed Jaws attack against any other creature until the Grapple ends.

action.name: Hooked Claw
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+11, reach 5 ft, one target. {@h}24 ({@dice 3d8 + 11}) Slashing and moved up to 5 ft. in a direction of Wretchglow, the Last Light's choice.

bonus.name: Lure
entries: If Wretchglow, the Last Light is Hidden, it creates an illusionary lure, following the same rules as its Bioluminescent Lure Legendary Action.

legendary.name: Misdirecting Strobe
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 13}, each creature in a 40 ft, {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that can see Wretchglow, the Last Light. {@actSaveFail} {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Attack rolls until the end of their next turn. Critical Failure: The {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of their next turn.

legendary.name: Direct Currents
entries: So long as Wretchglow, the Last Light is submerged in water, it may pick up to 4 creatures within 60 ft. who are also submerged in connected water and move them up to 10 ft. in any direction, so long as they remain submerged in water (no save allowed).

legendary.name: Bioluminescent Lure
entries: Wretchglow, the Last Light creates a visual illusion up to 10 ft. in size that must be within 30 ft. of itself. The illusion ends if Wretchglow, the Last Light moves more than 30 ft. away from it, if it uses this Legendary Action again, or if it chooses to dismiss the illusion. Any other creature that sees the illusion must succeed a {@dc 16} Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, or perceive the illusion as real (and generally be drawn to it).
On its turn, a creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful {@dc 16} {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check.

trait.name: Surging Power
entries: At the start of Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror's turn, select one of the following effects:

items: It may make an additional Hooked Claw attack this turn when it takes the Multiattack action.
It may take the Dash action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} this turn.

items.name: Dexterity Saving Throw:
items.entry: {@dc 16}, each other creature in a 10 ft, {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Lightning damage.

items: It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Semi-Aquatic
entries: Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror can hold its breath for up to 30 minutes.

trait.name: Rostral Dermal Pressure Sensors
entries: While in water (or lava), Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror has Blindsight 10 ft. (included above).

trait.name: Crystalline Form
entries: Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror is immune to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Petrified|XPHB} conditions (included above).

action.name: Unleash Energies {@recharge 5}
entries: Crackling magical energies erupt from Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror. {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each other creature in a 40 ft, {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@actSaveFail} 33 ({@damage 6d10}) Lightning damage plus 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Force damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror makes one Shardmaw Bite attack and one Hooked Claw attack.

action.name: Shardmaw Bite
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+12, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}22 ({@damage 3d6 + 12}) Piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Force damage.

action.name: Hooked Claw
entries: Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}:+12, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}25 ({@damage 3d8 + 12}) Slashing damage and moved up to 5 ft. in a direction of Xu'Thul, the Prismatic Terror's choice.

reaction.name: Reactionary Crystalline Regulation
entries: {@actTrigger} Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror would take damage from an attack, spell, or effect. {@actResponse} Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to its choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder damage until the start of its next turn. The crystals on its body visibly flicker/crackle/bubble with energies of the chosen damage type.
This {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} is in addition to any gained by its Elemental Absorb Legendary Action.

legendary.name: Shard Breath {@recharge 3}
entries: Ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}: {@hit 6}, range 10 ft. {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, up to four targets {@h}16 ({@damage 2d10 + 5}) Slashing damage.

legendary.name: Elemental Absorb
entries: Until its next turn, Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror gains {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to one damage type from the list below, however if it has already gained an {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} from this Legendary Action, it instead replaces it. Its crystals change colour to the associated colour.

items: Fire (red)
Cold (blue)
Lightning (yellow)
Poison (green)

entries: This {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} is in addition to any gained from its Reactionary Crystalline Regulation {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

legendary.name: Prismatic Glow
entries: Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror produces a bright light, illuminating an area of up to 60 ft. with bright white light and a further 60 ft. with dim light (total 120 ft.). Each other creature within a 10 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} takes {@damage 1d10} Radiant damage (no save allowed).
If Xu'thul, the Prismatic Terror has used Elemental Absorb this turn, the light is that associated colour instead.

trait.name: Naive
entries: Young Tyrannosaurus has a -3 modifier to Wisdom Saving Throws (included above).

action.name: Snapping Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) Piercing damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 14}). Young Tyrannosaurus cannot Snipping Bite another target until the Grapple ends.

bonus.name: Burst of Speed
entries: Young Tyrannosaurus takes the Dash action.

bonus.name: Tailswipe
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature within 5 ft. of Young Tyrannosaurus that is not {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by Young Tyrannosaurus. {@actSaveFail} 17 ({@damage 3d6 + 7}) Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Cliff Scene
entries: When Young Tyrannosaurus is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it lets out a shrill cry. A few moments later, the roar of two adult Tyrannosaurus rex can be heard in the distance. After 1 minute, two Tyrannosaurus Rex (see Monster Manual) appear and attack the party, focusing initially on whoever reduced the Young Tyrannosaurus to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If another adult Tyrannosaurus is already present, this affect does not occur.

trait.name: Thick Feathered Coat
entries: Yutyrannus has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage (all included above).

If Yutyrannus is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, it loses its {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage and replaces its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

trait.name: Arch-Predator
entries: Yutyrannus cannot be easily swayed from the hunt. It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma and Wisdom Saving Throws.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Yutyrannus makes one Feathermaw Bite attack and two Feathered Claw attacks.

action.name: Feathermaw Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}19 ({@damage 4d6 + 5}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions (escape {@dc 16}). Until this Grapple ends, Yutyrannus cannot Feathermaw Bite another target.

action.name: Feathered Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d12 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Downy Shoulder Bash
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 11}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage. If Yutyrannus moved 30+ ft. straight toward the target immediately before the hit: {@actSave str} {@dc 16}. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and Yutyrannus can make one Feathered Claw attack against it.

bonus.name: Call the Pack (1/Day)
entries: Yutyrannus lets out a gut-wrenching bellow alerting other members of its pack to the conflict.

At the start of the next round, up to two additional Yutyrannus join the combat as allies to this Yutyrannus. They approach from nearby cover and do not have the Call the Pack {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

If this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} is used by a polymorphed or otherwise shapeshifted humanoid, their friends, family, or party members (their choice) are considered to be their 'pack' instead, and are made aware of the conflict, regardless of where they are.

legendary.name: Coordinate
entries: Yutyrannus signals its pack with grumbles and tail flicks. On its next turn, Yutyrannus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature that has at least one other Yutyrannus within 10 ft. of it that isn't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.

legendary.name: Hunt
entries: Yutyrannus searches for its prey. It may make a {@skill Perception|XPHB} check. If a hidden creature within 60 ft. has taken damage, Yutyrannus has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check, specifically for detecting that creature (disregard the additional {@dice d20} for all uninjured creatures).

items.name: Legendary Might
entries: Yutyrannus may take an additional Legendary Action (increasing its total to 2).

items.name: Frost Bellow {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 20 ft.. {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 40 ({@damage 10d8}) Cold damage and speed reduced by 10 ft. until the end of the creature's next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage and no reduced speed.

items.name: Frenzy
entries: Yutyrannus can move up to 5 ft. and make a Feathered Claw attack.

trait.name: Stout Body
entries: Zalmoxes' unusually stout body makes it remarkably tough for its size. It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage (included above).

trait.name: Docile and Cowardly
entries: Zalmoxes will not attack unless provoked. It will flee from creatures it perceives as predators.

action.name: Beaked Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Shrieking Demise
entries: When Zalmoxes is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} it lets out a cowardly shriek. This shriek afflicts the creature that inflicted lethal damage to Zalmoxes. That creature is cursed by Reverberation of Cowardice, which triggers each time it enters combat.

items.name: Curse: Reverberation of Cowardice
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 10}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition ({@condition Frightened|XPHB} of all enemies) for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} at the end of each of its turns.
This curse can be removed by a {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} spell or similar effect, or ends after 24 hours.

trait.name: Ankylosaur Osteoderms
entries: Zuul has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, has an AC of 20, a -10 modifier to Arcobatics checks, and a -8 modifier to {@skill Athletics|XPHB} checks (all included above).

trait.name: Hulking Mass
entries: Zuul has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all Dexterity Saving Throws, but {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Constitution and Strength Saving Throws.

action.name: Clubbed Tail
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}19 ({@damage 2d12 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage, plus: {@actSave str} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and suffers a 'Shattering Blow' (see below). {@actSaveSuccess} The hit creature is unaffected, unless it already had the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If so, it suffers a 'Shattering Blow' (see below).

entries.name: Condition: Shattering Blow
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}. {@actSaveFail} The creature gains 1 level of Shattering Blow (cumulative), reducing its speed by 10 ft. (to a minimum of 5 ft.). Each level of Shattering Blow can be removed by a {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} spell, equivalent effect, or by completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Ectoplasmic Reach
entries: A ghoulish jelly-like substance extends the from Zuul's tail. Increase the reach of Zuul's Clubbed Tail attack to 15 ft. and change its damage type to Necrotic.

items.name: The Gatekeeper (1/Day)
entries: Zuul attempts to open an interdimensional portal directly in front of it that ejects malicious energies. Roll a {@dice D20}: On a 1, Zuul detonates with malicious magical energies, dealing {@damage 8d8} Necrotic damage to itself and {@damage 4d8} Necrotic damage to each other creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

On a 2-10, an unstable portal forms for 1 minute and pulses with malicious energy, triggering the following effect: {@actSave con} {@dc 12}, each non-Zuul creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. {@actSaveFail} {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

On a 11-19, an metastable portal forms for 1 minute and pulses with malicious energy, triggering the following effect: {@actSave con} {@dc 12}, each non-Zuul creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. {@actSaveFail} {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage for 1 minute and {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

On a 20, an stable portal forms for 1 minute and radiates malicious energy. Each non-Zuul creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage and takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage at the start of each of their turns.
If Zuul is slain, the portal it created either closes or stabilises to another plane of existence (DM's decision) for {@dice 1d20} minutes.

items.name: Pulse Portal
entries: Zuul pulses an unstable or metastable portal, triggering the portal's effect again.
{@i "Tie-ran-o-sore-us"} {@b (Tyrant Lizard King)} Chosen by Ross Grundler

For a week we had been restin' at a small settlement in the Southeast of the continent, eager to explore further South. Our gracious hosts warned us not to go traipsin' through the southern forests, as it was guarded by a fearsome beast. They just kept callin' it the "Blue Death" and told hyperbolic stories of a maw so great that'd swallow a full party whole and limbs so powerful that they couldn't be stopped.

Nevertheless, our adventurin' drive was strong so we decided to push on with our plans, while takin' their warnin's to heart. We were cautious and travelled quietly. After a couple days walk, we were enterin' its territory. The first signs we got of its presence was a rumblin' that shook the very ground. A deep-bass bellow in the middle of a bright night, well-lit by a full moon. It shook our bedrolls and our campfire clanged as the pots fell from their hooks.

We just had to see this thin' before we move on. We tracked its location over the course of a few weeks, the bellows stronger every night. Once we knew we were close, me and a few of the stealthier members of our party set out in the night to sneak up on it, keepin' to the moonlight shadows as much as possible. As we approached, the rumblin' was so intense that it was hard to stand. Crouchin' in the bushes, a clearin' ahead revealed an absolutely colossal deep blue, almost black, Tyrannosaurus rex. This thin' outsized any of our other records for rex size. We could immediately see why it was called the Blue Death and imagined that it could live up to that name. All big carnivores pick up a few scars, but the Blue Death had the most any of us had ever seen. Its face 'n' belly had been shredded in the past, probably failed attempts by other big predators to kill it. They'd healed in big archin' scars. There are even some scorch marks that were probably made by dragon's breath. We wondered how the other beasties might've looked after toillin' with this thin'.

Its eyes were a piercin' as it raised its head and bellowed motionlessly in the moonlight. Our rogue asked whether it was a buck, callin' for a mate... but I'm not so sure. Truth be told, we usually rely on colour patternin' for this species, but the hyperpigmentation of this one put a stop to that and none of us was willin' to check the plumbin'. Whatever it was, I have no doubt that it sired most of the offspring in the region.

The lack of rumblin' answers back suggested that it was the dominant predator for a hundred miles or so around and it'd probably be easier to list what it didn't eat, rather than what it did. Its territory encompassed grasslands, forests, lakes, and even a small mountain range. Our ventures over the followin' weeks saw evidence of Blue Death all over. It evidently patrolled its territory constantly and it seems that no settlements could safely be founded there. I feel remorse for the foolish ones who tried in the past.

entries.name: Size and Age Limits
entries: {@i Tyrannosaurus} long held the title of largest land carnivore at 40 ft. long and weighing up to 8 tonnes. However, since the 1990s newly discovered or re-examined species like {@i Giganotosaurus}, {@creature Carcharodontosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} and {@creature Spinosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} (see {@book The Bahariya Formation|PartneredDDDoD|4|Spinosaurus}) have shown that many giant predators stalked the Mesozoic (though none were probably as heavy as {@i Tyrannosaurus}). This prompted the question: {@i "What really was the largest size these animals could reach?"}.

It's been suggested that the largest theropod dinosaurs couldn't get much bigger than 40-50 ft. long, due to limitations in their body plan and metabolic rate. However, a 2023 presentation highlighted that only a tiny fraction of life is preserved in the fossil record, meaning that we will never find the largest individuals of any given species. Research using statistical modelling demonstrated that the largest {@i Tyrannosaurus} could have probably reached over 13 tonnes in weight, over 50% bigger than our largest specimen. These models also highlighted that, statistically, over 500 specimens would need to be found before we were likely to find an individual over 10 tonnes, which could take another century.

Further evidence suggests that the {@i Tyrannosaurus} specimens we previously considered to be adults are in fact subadults, with more growing to do. We previously calculated that it had a maximum lifespan of 28 years, but a recently discovered carcharodontosaurid named {@i Meraxes} has brought that into question. It died somewhere between the ages of 38 to 50, demonstrating that large predators could live for much longer than we anticipated. All of this highlights that {@i Tyrannosaurus} almost certainly lived for decades longer than we previously thought and reached sizes far larger than any specimen found so far. Ultimately, palaeontology is an ever-developing science and even an animal as well-studied as {@i Tyrannosaurus} can yield new dramatic discoveries.

entries: Carr, T.D. 2020. A high-resolution growth series of {@i Tyrannosaurus rex} obtained from multiple lines of evidence. {@i PeerJ}, {@b 8}, e9192.
Henderson, D.M. 2023. Growth constraints set an upper limit to theropod dinosaur body size. {@i The Science of Nature}, {@b 110(1)}, 4.
Horner, J.R., and Padian, K., 2004. Age and growth dynamics of {@i Tyrannosaurus rex}. {@i Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, Series B: Biological Sciences}, {@b 271(1551)}, 1875-1880.

Mallon, J. C., and Hone, D.W.E. 2022. How big could {@i T. rex} get? A case for the estimation of maximum body size in extinct animals. {@i Society of Vertebrate Paleontology 82nd Annual Meeting Program Guide, Toronto, Ontario}, 241.
Persons IV, W.S., Currie, P.J., and Erickson, G.M. 2020. An older and exceptionally large adult specimen of {@i Tyrannosaurus rex}. {@i The Anatomical Record}, {@b 303(4)}, 656-672.
{@i "Ar-rah-zone-ah-sore-us"} {@b (Arizona reptile)}

Occasionally, the doldrum of the scrub'n'dry rock was broken by large, fanned sails dottin' the horizon. We learnt pretty quickly to give these a wide berth, as the beasties that they was attached to were vicious predators. Although sluggish at first, these thin's could dash right up and deliver some really nasty bites. If you gotta pass em, do it in the early mornin' when they're baskin' to warm 'emselves.

{@i Arizonasaurus} is a Middle Triassic (243 million years ago) reptile from the Moenkopi Formation in Arizona, which was once an ancient floodplain. As a member of the Archosauria, it is a distant relative of modern crocodiles and the large Triassic predator Postosuchus. One of its distinguishing features was a large sail running down its back.

entries.name: Ecology
entries: {@i Arizonasaurus} was a quadrupedal (walking on all four legs) archosaur with hyper-elongated vertebral spines, extending up to 2 ft. above the animal's back, forming a sail-like structure similar to that seen in animals like {@i Dimetrodon} or {@creature Spinosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} (see {@book The Bahariya Formation|PartneredDDDoD|4|Spinosaurus}). It was a robust, powerful animal, with an estimated length of 10 ft. and height of 1.5 ft. (excluding the sail). Unlike many early reptiles, the limbs of {@i Arizonasaurus} were held beneath its body, giving it an erect posture.

{@i Arizonasaurus} was carnivorous, with a mouth full of blade-like teeth, and was one of the larger predators of the Middle Triassic (although smaller than several other members of its group). It would probably have predated upon pretty much anything smaller than itself that it could catch.

The function of {@i Arizonasaurus}' sail has been debated for many years and suggested uses include sexual display, threat display, and thermal regulation. The latter is plausible, given the hot climate of the Middle Triassic, and {@i Arizonasaurus} could have flushed blood into its sail to cool itself or orientated it perpendicular to the sun to warm itself in the early mornings.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries: As a large predator for its day, {@i Arizonasaurus} likely spent much of its time conserving energy and resting. When hunting, it probably ambushed prey with a burst of speed, but likely also consumed carrion when available. {@i Arizonasaurus} shared its environment with other larger carnivores and would have been cautious about lingering near a carcass for too long.

We suggest playing {@i Arizonasaurus} as a patient predator, willing to rest for extended periods. This can give the impression that it is a sedate animal, but an attack could come at any moment. Smaller party members should be more at risk, as they are seen as easier prey.

entries.name: Phylogeny
entries: {@i Arizonasaurus} is a member of Poposauroidea, the cosmopolitan group that includes the huge Postosuchus. These animals were the dominant terrestrial predators in the Triassic, before the rise of the dinosaurs. Sails were a common feature of a subgroup of poposaurs called ctenosauriscids, of which {@i Arizonasaurus} is a member.

As the earliest member of Poposauroidea, its occurrence in the Middle Triassic pushes the divergence of crocodiles and dinosaurs from Archosauria back by millions of years. This confirms an Early Triassic split of these groups and makes {@i Arizonasaurus} an important species for understanding the evolution of both crocodiles and dinosaurs.

entries.name: References
entries: Blakey, R.C. 1974. Stratigraphic and depositional analysis of the Moenkopi Formation, southeastern Utah. {@i Utah Geological and Mineral Survey Bulletin}, 104.
Mann, A., and Reisz, R.R. 2020. Antiquity of "sail-backed" neural spine hyper-elongation in mammal forerunners. {@i Frontiers in Earth Science}, {@b 8}, 83.
Nesbitt, S.J. 2003. {@i Arizonasaurus} and its implications for archosaur divergence. {@i Proceedings of the Royal Society B}, {@b 270}, S234-S237.
Nesbitt, S.J. 2005. Osteology of the Middle Triassic pseudosuchian archosaur {@i Arizonasaurus} babbitti. {@i Historical Biology}, {@b 8(1}), 19-47.
{@i "Pol-e-coh-tea-lid"}

When we approached a small pool, the water was murky and muddy. Practically opaque–couldn't see a thin' through it. The only indication that somethin' was in there were the rollin' splashes in the otherwise calm water. We threw a large pebble in to see if we could spook whatever it was away. The splashes stopped for a bit, then a slick shiny reptilian head poked out of the water to look at us. It almost looked friendly, like a croc crossed with a seal. But the set of nasty pointed teeth interlockin' along its mouth hinted otherwise.

The Bahariyan Polycotylid is a relatively long (>10 ft.) freshwater plesiosaur from the Bahariya Formation, Egypt. We initially included this animal based on its original identification as the cosmopolitan genus {@i Marsilea}. However, recent studies noted the lack of leptocleidids in the Bahariya Formation and the reappraisal of these fragmentary specimens to the family Polycotylidae. As the fossil material has not been redescribed since its original study in the 1920s, we will refer to it here as the "Bahariyan Polycotylid".

entries.name: Ecology
entries: Plesiosaurs are relatively morphologically conservative within their group, with streamlined bodies, elongated necks, squat heads, short tails, and four highly modified paddle-like limbs. Polycotylids deviated from this norm however, and had much shorter necks, as well as relatively thin and elongated jaws. This gave them a superficially streamlined crocodile-like appearance, similar to the giant oceanic pliosaurs, which are a group of plesiosaurs adapted to hunt other large marine reptiles. The Bahariyan Polycotylid was, in contrast, much smaller and better suited to life in shallow water. Its occurrence in the Bahariya Formation indicates that it likely ventured into estuaries, freshwater lagoons, and riverways, as well as along the coastal shelf. Its smaller body would have allowed greater mobility in these restricted environments, while its long jaws would have allowed it to easily snap up passing fish or potentially grab small animals from the shoreline.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries: While the Bahariyan Polycotylid would have been a prominent predator of fish in the African lagoons and coastal areas, its small size meant it would have been vulnerable to larger aquatic predators. This means it may have been relatively cautious, perhaps using the murky waters as a means of evading attacks or hiding from prey.

We suggest that it be played as a wary animal. Most humanoids should be too large to be considered potential prey, but players entering the water may be considered a disturbance to their feeding or breeding grounds, which could result in an attack–especially if the animal has limited options to escape. If more than one Bahariyan Polycotylid is in the area (especially a mother and large calf), they may attack in a co-ordinated manner, making them much more dangerous to unlucky parties.

entries.name: Phylogeny
entries: Polycotylids were a globally successful group of plesiosaurs found in deposits throughout the Cretaceous. Their highly modified bodies mean that it is difficult to place them precisely within Plesiosauria, with different phylogenies resolving them in very different positions. The current consensus associates them with similarly highly modified leptocleidids, potentially even as a sibling group.

entries.name: Escaping the Land
entries: For many years, it was theorised that plesiosaurs were capable of limited terrestrial movement. This was largely tied to the idea that they needed to lay eggs on land, like turtles. However, new polycotylid specimens have since demonstrated that they birthed a single, relatively large, infant. The size of their offspring suggests a heavy investment from the parent and could indicate that plesiosaurs continued to nurture their young until maturity. If they did not lay eggs, then it also means that they had little need to come onto land and, given their highly adapted morphology, it is likely that they never willingly left the water.

entries.name: References
entries: Bunker, G., Martill, D.M., Smith, R.E., Zouhri, S., and Longrich, N. 2022. Plesiosaurs from the fluvial Kem Kem Group (mid-Cretaceous) of eastern Morocco and a review of non-marine plesiosaurs. {@i Cretaceous Research}, {@b 140}, 105310.
Fischer, V., Benson, R.B., Druckenmiller, P.S., Ketchum, H.F., and Bardet, N. 2018. The evolutionary history of polycotylid plesiosaurians. {@i Royal Society Open Science}, {@b 5(3)}, 172177.

Kear, B.P., and Barrett, P.M. 2011. Reassessment of the Lower Cretaceous (Barremian) pliosauroid {@i Leptocleidus superstes} Andrews, 1922 and other plesiosaur remains from the nonmarine Wealden succession of southern England. {@i Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society}, {@b 161(3)}, 663-691.
{@i "Bal-or"} {@b (Balaur, a dragon in Romanian mythology)}

As we pushed through the thick undergrowth, we entered a small clearin'. Light beamed down through the canopy revealin' a handful of nests sat on by some lil' theropods. We were immediately greeted by goose-like hissin'. Very angry lil' thin's. When they pounced, we learnt just how sharp their {@item sickle|XPHB} claws are–and that they had two on each foot for twice the pain!
{@i Balaur} is a small and unusual theropod that is an excellent example of the difficulty in clarifying the relationships of fossil animals.

entries.name: Ecology
entries: {@i Balaur} is only known from a partial skeleton that lacks several major parts, including its skull. This makes reconstructing {@i Balaur} difficult, but researchers estimate that it was up to 8 ft. long and weighed about 33 lb. It was clearly an unusual animal as it had remarkably stocky feet with a pair of large dromaeosaur-like {@item sickle|XPHB} claws on each foot. Dromaeosaurs like {@creature Velociraptor|PartneredDDDoD} and {@creature Utahraptor|PartneredDDDoD} (see {@book The Rest of the Alphabet|PartneredDDDoD|7}) hold these claws vertically, but {@i Balaur}'s could only be held flat, making it flat footed. Despite having wing-like forelimbs, it is also thought to be fully flightless, with a non-functional reduced third finger on each hand.

Without its skull, determining {@i Balaur}'s diet is difficult. Due to its dromaeosaur-like claws, it was originally classified as part of that group and therefore assumed to be carnivorous. However, later investigations noted that its relative bulkiness, large swept back pubic bone (suggestive of a big gut, but present in all paravian theropods), and robust limbs could indicate that it was herbivorous. A more recent study in 2015 focused on {@i Balaur}'s phylogeny, but also addressed its ecology and suggested that it was part of an evolutionary grade containing both herbivores and omnivores. Based on the more predatory elements of its morphology, they argued it was likely omnivorous.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries: With so much debate around {@i Balaur}, it is hard to pin down much of its behaviour. Still, we can make some suggestions based on similar animals. We know it was probably ground-dwelling and may have lived in pairs or small groups. It would likely have foraged for fruits and berries, while also taking down suitably sized prey using its stocky build to overpower them. With this in mind, we recommend that {@i Balaur} be played as an alert and curious animal. It may approach a party or player out of interest or in search of food and, as an island dweller, it may not view humanoids as a threat at all. However, a lone player could find themselves approached by several {@i Balaur} that are much more willing to attack.

entries.name: Phylogeny
entries: {@i Balaur}'s phylogeny has been the subject of debate since its discovery. Initially it was described as a dromaeosaurid based on similarities in shoulder girdle, forearm shape, and its {@item sickle|XPHB}-like claws, but was considered highly unusual within the group for its reduced third finger, fused wrists, and fused ankles. These peculiarities were assumed to be a result of its island isolation.

Several subsequent studies challenged this identification, noting features that are unheard-of in dromaeosaurs, but common in avialans (the non-bird dinosaurs that are most closely related to birds). After discussions about other occurrences of dromaeosaur-like {@item sickle|XPHB} claws in modern birds, it was determined to most likely be an avialan, with secondary flightlessness. This is a trait known to evolve in other island-dwelling birds, such as the dodo and kākāpō.

entries.name: References
entries: Cau, A., Brougham, T., and Naish, D. 2015. The phylogenetic affinities of the bizarre Late Cretaceous Romanian theropod {@i Balaur bondoc} (Dinosauria, Maniraptora): Dromaeosaurid or flightless bird?. {@i PeerJ}, {@b 3}, e1032.

Csiki, Z., Vremir, M., Brusatte, S.L., and Norell, M.A. 2010. An aberrant island-dwelling theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Romania. {@i Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America}, {@b 107(35)}, 15357-15361.

Godefroit, P., Cau, A., Hu, D.-Y., Escuillié, F., Wu, W., and Dyke, G. 2013. A Jurassic avialan dinosaur from China resolves the early phylogenetic history of birds. {@i Nature}, {@b 498(7454)}, 359-362.
Wright, N.A., Steadman, D.W., and Witt, C.C. 2016. Predictable evolution toward flightlessness in volant island birds. {@i Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences}, {@b 113(17)}, 4765-4770.
{@i "Bay-pee-sore-us"} {@b (Beipao Reptile)}

We were followin' a clearin' through the forest, hikin' in single file up the mountainside. Knackered from the walk, we stopped for a moment to catch our collective breath. Mid-swig o' water, I spotted 'em right there, less then 50 ft. away. Three slumped fuzzy creatures sat on their backsides, dozily graspin' at branches with their {@item sickle|XPHB} claws and pullin' leaves off 'em. One of 'em turned its head sluggishly towards me and just carried on chompin' slowly. It didn't care one bit that we were there.
{@i Beipiaosaurus} is a small therizinosaurid from China that sheds light on the phylogenetic relationships of therizinosaurs.

entries.name: Ecology
entries: {@i Beipiaosaurus} was a small (8 ft. long) therizinosaurid, a group of unusual theropod dinosaurs that evolved herbivory within an otherwise generally carnivorous group. It had a long neck, small leaf-shaped teeth, a short tail, enlarged gut, and strong forelimbs with large {@item sickle|XPHB}-like claws. {@i Beipiaosaurus} was an early member of the group, distinguished by its small size and relatively large head.

Some {@i Beipiaosaurus} specimens preserve a full body covering of simple quill-like feathers and {@i Beipiaosaurus} is unique among feathered dinosaurs due having secondary coat of more elongate feathers with unbranched filaments. Recent studies suggest that these feathers were brown in colour and were primarily for insulation in the chilly Yixian environment.

{@i Beipiaosaurus}' diet consisted mainly of ferns, early flowering plants, and leaves. However, it is possible that in the early stages of this group's transition into herbivory they supplemented their diet with insects.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries: Little is known for certain about the behavior of {@i Beipiaosaurus}, but some researchers report that their nests show that they were communal and probably cared for hatchlings, despite the hatchlings being able to feed themselves.

However, many parallels have been drawn between therizinosaurs and sloths (including giant ground sloths) due to their shared herbivorous diet, downy fuzz, enlarged guts, and {@item sickle|XPHB} claws. It is possible that they occupied very similar niches, with {@i Beipiaosaurus} functioning like an agile dinosaur-sloth equivalent. Therizinosaurs were hunted by larger theropods, and {@i Beipiaosaurus}' small size and slow speed would have made it cautious and potentially highly-aggressive when threatened.

We recommend {@i Beipiaosaurus} be played as a relatively relaxed and seemingly sedate animal, that can erupt into an aggressive display of sharp claws if disturbed. Adults should be particularly hostile if in groups or near nesting sites.

entries.name: Phylogeny
entries: Therizinosaur skulls and teeth are similar to prosauropods, the precursors to sauropods, and they used to be considered a relic lineage of this group, or an unknown form of saurischian. It wasn't until 1993 that they were confidently identified as theropods. Within Theropoda, therizinosaurs are part of the maniraptorans, the group that includes dromaeosaurs, oviraptorosaurs, and modern birds.

entries.name: References

{@i Allosaurus "Ah-low-sore-us"} {@b (Different Lizard)} Chosen by Lucian T. Moreman

More than once we came across a young injured Allosaurus. The rest of the party kept callin' it "{@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD}". No idea why the name stuck, but it did. It seemed to walk with a wobbly gait, like it had hurt its toe, but still pushed on. Poor thin' never had the stomach to really attack us... it kinda just followed our group for a while, fed on scraps, left, then returned every now 'n' again. I imagine it would have given it a go if our group had been fewer in number though.

entries.name: Ecology
entries: Allosaurus was a large predatory theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (155-145 million years ago) of North America and Western Europe. It was a strong and robust animal with powerful limbs and was up to 28 ft. long. "{@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD}" is the name given to a near-complete female sub-adult specimen from Wyoming that was approximately 22 ft. long.

entries.name: Palaeopathology
entries: Pathology is the science of disease and injury, and palaeopathology is the interpretation of pathology in fossils. We can use this information to identify predator/prey relationships, environmental hazards, (rarely) diseases present, and the life history of individual animals, including their susceptibilities and rates of recovery.

{@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} is the most famous case study of palaeopathology in dinosaurs, with at least 19 broken or injured bones. These include broken and damaged chest ribs, broken gastralia (belly ribs), injured vertebrae, an infected illium (hip bone), a broken vertebral arch, a punctured shoulder blade, a badly mangled right arm, and numerous injuries and infections on both feet. Many had healed, but not very well and had clear signs of infection, meaning {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} was in a sorry state towards the end of her life. This animal was likely in pain for many years but persisted perhaps in part due to a localised immune system that prevented serious infections from spreading around the body.

In fact, despite her grievous injuries, we think that {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} was still able to reproduce, as new evidence indicates that she likely laid eggs just before her death. We know this because of the presence of medullary bone, which is a type of bone laid down by female egg-laying animals as a calcium store for eggshell production. Not only does this identify {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} as female, but also provides a major insight into the extent of trauma these animals could endure while still following their reproductive instincts. Nevertheless, {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD}'s injuries to her feet and arm prevented her from hunting, and she ultimately died from emaciation.

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: If you use {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} as a recurring creature, eventually she should mature, losing the "Subadult" Trait (increasing her Wisdom Ability Score to 10) and the last sentence of her "Clumsy" Trait (removing the below 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} modifier).
