entries.name: Hateg Island Flora
entries: Although Hațeg island was in the sub-tropical part of the Tethys Sea, the warmer Cretaceous temperatures meant that its flora would have been comparable to a modern tropical island, rather than a modern sub-tropical one. This means that most of the island was covered by lush forest and jungle.

entries.name: Phyllites sp.

entries.altText: The small fern Phylittes with several large, long, and curling leaves.

entries: {@i Phyllites} sp. was a small undergrowth fern that would have grown around the bases of trees and in other shaded areas. It favoured damp soils and in summer would have likely developed rows of orange-brown or yellow sori (clusters of spore-making structures) along the underside of its leaves. {@i Phyllites} sp. would not have been edible, and may even have been an irritant or poisonous to humans.

entries.name: Phototoxic
entries: A viscous milky fluid runs through this plant's stem. If the plant is damaged, it oozes out. Any creature that comes into contact with this fluid gains {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage for 24 hours. This affliction can be removed with a {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} spell or effect.

entries.name: Pandanites trinervis
entries: {@i Pandanites trinervis} was a branching shrub with root supports at its base and rosettes of strap-like spiky leaves at the ends of branches that would have been sharp enough to cut skin. These leaves were also highly fibrous and could have been weaved into baskets or used to make thread or rope. Interestingly, modern relatives of this plant (Pandanus) are a key ingredient in many curries, and it is likely that {@i Pandanites trinervis}' leaves could have also been dried and used as a curry spice. The plant also produced fragrant flowers that could have been used as a perfume or to flavour drinks. Upon pollination, these would have developed into pineapple or cone-like fruits that were edible and yellow or orange in colour.

entries.name: High Scoville Pungency
entries: This plant is exceptionally spicy. If a creature consumes this plant's fruit, it takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage, but gains the following {@variantrule Action|XPHB} for 24 hours:

entries.name: Flamin' Breath (PB/day)
entries: {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Constitution modifier), each creature in a 15 ft. {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Fire damage.

entries.altText: The small branching tree Pandanites with a thin branching trunk and narrow mangrove-like roots.

entries.name: Araliaephyllum sp.

entries.altText: The shrub Araliaephyllum with thin stems and a bushy canopy.

entries: {@i Araliaephyllum} sp. was a small to medium sized lauraceous bush with multiple thin stems or trunks and a bushy canopy. This canopy was made up of narrow three-lobed leaves that had the silhouette of a bird's foot. Little is known about this plant, but its modern affinities suggest that it may have developed small inedible black fruits and possibly had medicinal uses.

entries.name: Theropod-footed Healing Balm
entries: This plant's bird- foot-shaped leaves can be crushed into a {@item Araliaephyllum sp. Healing Balm|PartneredDDDoD|paste} and applied to a wound to help it heal. If this balm is applied to a creature during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, that creature heals {@dice 1d6 + 2} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and its speed is increased by 10 ft. for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Sabalites longirhachis
entries: {@i Sabalites longirhachis} was a tall, thin, large-leaved palm tree that reached up to 45 ft. in height. It possibly produced bunches of small dry berry-like fruits, but these would have been extremely difficult to reach, given the tree's height, and were probably inedible to humans. The large leaves and long, straight trunks of this tree would have made it an ideal resource for building structures.

entries.name: Synaptic Regulator
entries: The small dry {@item Sabalites longirhachis Fruits|PartneredDDDoD|fruits} that this plant produces have a bitter taste and cause a creature to feel nauseous for a few minutes if consumed. However, they also stimulate the nervous system and provide that creature {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence Saving Throws for the next 24 hours.

entries.altText: The tall, large-leafed palm tree Sabalites.

entries.name: Ettingshausenia onomasta
entries: {@i Ettingshausenia onomasta} was a large plane-like tree with broad three-lobed leaves that favoured moist soils, growing near water. Its bark would have had a knobbly and mottled appearance, with a camouflage-like pattern. Its wood would have been highly resistant to splitting and therefore useful for making sturdy wooden objects (e.g. a butcher's block), but would have been hard to carve. Modern relatives of this plant produce hair-like new growth that can become a respiratory irritant when the wood is cut.

entries.altText: The tall broad-leaved tree Ettingshausenia.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
Polymorphic Fibres
entries: When this plant is cut down, pale pink hair-like fibres erupt from its central trunk, causing the following effect:

{@i Wisdom Saving Throw:} DC 12, each creature within a 10 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the trunk. {@i Failure:} The creature is polymorphed into a non-magical {@creature Sharovipteryx|PartneredDDDoD} (see {@area The Rest of the Alphabet|1ae|x}) for 10 minutes or until the creature takes damage.

entries.altText: The landscape of the Crato Formation, black storm clouds approach an otherwise oasis-like pool in an arid scrubby region. The water is ringed by trees as a startled flock of pterosaurs takes off. Dragonflies flit between the dry plants and water.

entries: When our ship arrived at the coast, we were greeted by the most beautiful lagoon I'd ever seen. The pale creams and oranges of the sun-baked sand were stunnin'ly contrasted with the milky-blue water and deep-green tropical plants. This felt like a lil' paradise in a dry desert. Once we made landfall, one of the crew set to restock their water. They scooped up a mouthful and in delight it was fresh! Well, at least the first gulp was. The second scoop their faces scrunched, and they spat it out. Seems there was only a sliver of fresh water on the top. Told 'em that the milky colour shows they shouldn't drink it. "Noted", said the crewman.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Crato Formation of north-eastern Brazil is a series of strata that boasts arguably some of the best-preserved fossils ever found. A unique combination of environmental, geochemical, sedimentological, and geological events caused fossils from this locality to be preserved with unbelievably high fidelity. It is approximately 120 million years old and was deposited near the equator during the hot Early Cretaceous.

There is a lot of controversy around the Crato Formation (and the nearby Santana Formation). Fossils from these locations have been routinely illegally exported for decades and can be found in almost every fossil shop around the world. While this has allowed exceptional Crato material to be widely studied, it has also impacted domestic Brazilian palaeontology and science tourism, as well as perpetuated colonial attitudes. We here at PalaeoGames Ltd. support the repatriation of illegally acquired fossils to their home country.

entries.name: Description
entries: There is still conjecture about the exact environmental setting of the Crato Formation, with some scientists arguing that it was an ancient lake/lagoon, and others that it was a semi-arid wetland. Regardless, the entomofauna (insects) and flora (plants) show a combination of species that are from harsh arid scrublands and lush freshwater environments. This, combined with the high salinity, geological data, and reduced fish fauna, indicates that the Crato Formation was a body of lush water in an otherwise arid region, but that that water was stratified–with fresh water on top and salty, oxygen-poor water at the bottom. Regardless of the exact parameters of its deposition, the Crato Formation was an oasis of beauty in an otherwise barren landscape. This desolate weather was intermittently broken by huge storm events that flooded the surrounding landscape, flushing many small ground-dwelling invertebrates into the water.

entries.name: Geology
entries: The Crato Formation is a sequence of rock about 200 ft. thick and is composed of a variety of rock types. The strata of interest (called the Nova Olinda Member) is a buff-coloured creamy rock made of 99% calcium carbonate. This mineral was precipitated in water by algae as they photosynthesised, causing a milky haze in the water that drifted down as tiny crystals. Over time, the accumulation and cementation of these crystals formed the rock that entombed any carcasses that sank to the bottom of the water body.

entries.name: Fossils
entries: The Crato Formation yields truly astonishing fossils. Some of them preserve details that most people would not believe is possible. A single insect fossil can be preserved entirely intact with every joint fully articulated, with every body segment complete, each covered in cuticular scales, with hair-like setae still attached to those scales, with each of those hairs retaining microscopic surface details (such as ridges and grooves), and with fossilised bacteria sat between those grooves. This sub-cellular level of preservation absolutely shatters the previous understanding of the limitations of fossilisation. Furthermore, some fossils not only retain their external-most features, but volatile internal tissues that usually degrade within hours of death can also be preserved. We do not exaggerate when we say that the Crato Formation may yield the best-preserved fossils in the world.

Interestingly, there are no skeletal records of large terrestrial vertebrates, like big dinosaurs, or large logs (although some amber has been found) in the Crato Formation. This suggests that there is a mechanism that prevents larger fossils from being preserved. That could either be environmental, with the harsh environment not sustaining bigger organisms, or (much more likely) a filtering mechanism that has prevented them from being preserved or us from finding them. The latter is favoured by scientists, as they believe that smaller fossils may have been blown/washed into a large body of water, then concentrated by gyres, and finally deposited in the middle of the water body. In the following pages, we have provided stats for {@creature Cratoavis|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Tetrapodophis|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Tupandactylus|PartneredDDDoD}, and "{@creature Ubirajara|PartneredDDDoD}".

entries.name: As a roleplaying environment
entries: The Crato lake/lagoon should be an oasis of life among an otherwise hot and harsh scrubland. Lush green plants teeming with vividly coloured insects, birds, and pterosaurs should provide a chorus of colour piercing the scorching yellows and browns of the surrounding scrublands. Temporary waterways are filled with tiny invertebrates that thrive after an annual wet season. This location makes an ideal rest stop on a long journey for both players and migrating animals, which can lead to conflict.

Small streams drain into a single massive waterbody, similar to an inland sea. The main waterbody itself persists all year around and has little-to-no drainage, so concentrates salts similar to (but not as extreme as) the dead sea. The water is not drinkable and should have a milky-white appearance with green-tinted algae-rich areas. It is populated by millions of tiny fish (1.5 - 2 inches long), but little else.

Rarely, a huge storm should roll in from distant mountains, bringing with it heavy thumping rainfall accompanied by a torrent of water that washes small creatures and objects into the water in a tropical storm event.

entries.name: Stratified Waters
entries: Water appears fresh and the first sip always is.... However, further drinking or filling up of water supplies only provides salt water.

entries.name: Perfect Preservation
entries: {@i Through the murky water, you can see fossilised creatures resting on the bottom.}

Any creature that touches the bottom of the Crato palaeolake/lagoon while more than 20 ft. from the shoreline must succeed a DC 18 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} or be {@condition Petrified|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blistering Sun
entries: If players travel for more than 8 hours without seeking shelter from the sun, they gain one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}. This effect is inactive during a Rainstorm Event.

entries.name: Rainstorm Event
entries: After {@dice 1d4} days in this environment, the players are met with a sudden drastic change in weather. Over the course of an hour or less, the skies darken and a heavy storm rolls over the landscape. Hammering rain makes travel difficult. The rain lasts for 1 hour. Shortly after the rain ends, there is a distant rumbling sound followed by a torrent of knee-high flash flood water. Creatures have one round to escape the oncoming flood (i.e. climbing a tree or flying away), then must succeed a DC 13 Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} to avoid being washed away. A creature washed away moves at 40 ft. per round in the direction of the flowing water. A creature that succeeds on this Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} may wade through the water, treating it as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} if they move against the flow.

entries.name: References
entries: Barling, N.T., Martill, D.M., Heads, S.W. and Gallien, F. 2015. High fidelity preservation of fossil insects from the Crato Formation (Lower Cretaceous) of Brazil. {@i Cretaceous Research}, {@b 52}, 605-622.

Barling, N.T., Martill, D.M., and Heads, S.W. 2020. A geochemical model for the preservation of insects in the Crato Formation (Early Cretaceous) of Brazil. {@i Cretaceous Research}, {@b 116}, 104608.

entries.name: Crato Formation Flora
entries: The Crato Formation was an environment of extremes, with scorching dry heat and intermittent tremendous downpours. Its waters had fluctuating salinities and most plants had to be particularly hardy to survive in these dynamic conditions.

entries.name: Klitzschophyllites flabellatus
entries: {@i Klitzschophyllites flabellatus} was an aquatic plant that grew in small clusters in shallow water. As no close modern relatives of this plant persist today, little is known about its biology beyond its overall morphology. It had roundish, leathery, gland-covered leaves with spikey edges and a thick root. These glands suggest that {@i Klitzschophyllites flabellatus} may have been able to tolerate intermittently hypersaline water.

entries.name: Babel Leaves
entries: If a single {@item Klitzschophyllites flabellatus Leaf|PartneredDDDoD|leaf} is plucked from this plant and placed under the tongue of a creature with an Intelligence score of 8 or more, it is able to speak and comprehend any language for 1 minute. Once the effect wears off, the leaf shrivels and cannot be used again.

entries.altText: The small aquatic plant Klitzachophyllites has a cluster of disc-like leaves with jagged edges.

entries.name: Equisetum sp.

entries.altText: Several thin horsetails (Equiseteum) growing in marshy ground.

entries: {@i Equisetum} sp. (horsetails) grew in and around the edges of ponds, marshes, and other quiet fresh-water, as well as in consistently moist ground. They have a distinctive banding and long thin leaves, that can give them a feather-like appearance in some species. They grew close together, forming 3-4 ft. tall dense reeds, but had relatively weak stems and could have been pushed through with ease. Adult plants were poisonous, but young stems were paler, succulent, and edible if cooked. When crushed, these plants could also be used to make green or pale-yellow dyes.

entries.name: Toxic Maturity
entries: Fresh shoots of this plant are non-toxic and can be brewed into a simple, but delicious, {@item Equisetum sp. Potion|PartneredDDDoD|potion} that heals {@dice 1d4 + 1} hit points when consumed. However, {@item Equisetum sp. Potion (Incorrectly Harvested)|PartneredDDDoD|mature plants} are highly toxic and any creature that consumes them (or a derivative of them) is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 24 hours. A successful DC 10 {@skill Nature|XPHB} check is required to determine which shoots are safe to consume.

entries.name: Jaguariba wiersemaniania
entries: {@i Jaguariba wiersemaniania} was a small aquatic plant that grew in the shallow waters of ponds and lakes. Its leaves floated on the surface and it occasionally produced flowers, in the same manner as a modern waterlily. It produced a rhizome (an underground stem), similar to a potato, which would have been edible (albeit quite soggy). The flowers it produced were likely a psychodysleptic narcotic (similar to a hallucinogenic).

entries.name: Delicious
entries: The root of this plant is edible and can provide one days' ration. However, it is also particularly delicious to herbivores/omnivores. If you offer this food to a herbivorous/omnivorous beast while performing an {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} check, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that check.

entries.name: Psychodysleptic
entries: If a creature consumes the {@item Jaguariba wiersemaniania Flower|PartneredDDDoD|flowers} of this plant, it must succeed a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB} or be {@condition Stunned|XPHB} for {@dice 1d4} minutes. On a successful save, it is instead {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of all other creatures for {@dice 1d4} minutes. Whenever that creature takes damage while under either effect, it may make another DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, ending the effect on a success.

entries.altText: The tall, waterlily-like plant Jaguariba has green leaves with purple undersides and a thick root cluster.

entries.name: Welwitschiophyllum brasiliense

entries.altText: The scrubland plant Welwithschiophyllum has sharp pointed leaves that jut out in all directions and small brown cones.

entries: {@i Welwitschiophyllum brasiliense} was a desert-dwelling plant with long, pointed, strap-like leaves, and clusters of cones at the end of long thin stems. The fibrous leaves came to a sharp point, with edges sharp enough to cut skin. {@variantrule Dead|XPHB}, dropped leaves could have been used to make fibres for twine or as kindling for a fire. The thick central stem would have been edible, probably tasting similar to an onion.

entries.name: Razor-leaves
entries: The leaves of this plant are rigid and come to a sharp point. If a Large, Medium, or Small creature falls onto, runs through, or is pushed into this plant, it takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage.

entries.name: Edible
entries: This plant's stem can be carefully harvested by succeeding a DC 10 {@skill Survival|XPHB} check, providing four days' worth of rations for a single humanoid. Failing this check results in {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and a nasty cut.

entries.name: Ruffordia goeppertii
entries: {@i Ruffordia goeppertii} was a drought-tolerant fern that grew as small clusters of plants in shaded areas. If crushed, it would have produced a balsam aroma similar to pine needles. Modern relatives of this plant contain essential oils that, once extracted, can be used as an antiseptic or to treat burns. In some traditional medicines (particularly in South Africa), these plants are used to prevent children's nightmares.

entries.name: Antiseptic
entries: The {@item Ruffordia goeppertii Root|PartneredDDDoD|roots} of this plant have a horribly bitter taste, but also have medicinal properties. Eating them grants {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 24 hours.

entries.name: Sound Sleeping
entries: If a creature completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} within 24 hours of consuming the roots of this plant, they gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to their {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.altText: The small fern Ruffordia has curling stems and spread leaves, as well as a large, brown root cluster.

entries.name: References
entries: Coiffard, C., Mohr, B., and Bernardes-de-Oliveira, M.E.C. 2013. Jaguariba wiersemana gen. nov. et sp. nov., an Early Cretaceous member of crown group Nymphaeales (Nymphaeaceae) from northern Gondwana. {@i Palaeobotany}, {@b 62(1)}, 141-151.
Dilcher, D.L., Bernardes-De-Oliveira, M.E., Pons, D., and Lott, T.A. 2005. Welwitschiaceae from the Lower Cretaceous of Northeastern Brazil. {@i American Journal of Botany}, {@b 92(8)}, 1294-1310.
Martill, D.M., Bechly, G., and Loveridge, R.F. 2007. The Crato Fossil Beds of Brazil: Window into an Ancient World. {@i Cambridge University Press, Cambridge}, pp 625.

Mohr, B., Bernardes-de-Oliveira, M.E.C., Loveridge, R., Pons, D., Sucerquia, P.A., and Castro-Fernandes, M.C. 2015. Ruffordia goeppertii (Schizaeales, Anemiaceae)–A common fern from the Lower Cretaceous Crato Formation of northeast Brazil. {@i Cretaceous Research}, {@b 54(3)}, 17-26.

Mohr, B., Bernardes-de-Oliveira, M.E.C., Barale, G., and Ouaja, M. 2006. Palaeogeographic distribution and ecology of Klitzschophyllites, an early Cretaceous angiosperm in southern Laurasia and northern Gondwana. {@i Cretaceous Research}, {@b 27(3)}, 464-472.

entries.altText: Cratoavis, a colourful tiny bird-like dinosaur with long tail feathers, sits peacefully on a branch.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Cratoavis|PartneredDDDoD|Cratoavis'} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Global Adventurer
entries: If {@creature Cratoavis|PartneredDDDoD} successfully charms a member of the party, it will then begin to follow the party if able, keeping a reasonable distance from them (>50 ft.) for most of the time.
Unless it is regularly fed, once per day it will attempt to perform a Charming Display to either a party member or another humanoid it encounters.

entries.name: Perfect Preservation
entries: If {@creature Cratoavis|PartneredDDDoD} is slain, its body does not decay or deteriorate in any way, and it instead enters a state of preservational stasis. While in this state, it is {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} and can be revived by receiving any healing from a magical source.

entries.altText: A Ludodactylus with several small holes in its left wing membrane soars through the sky.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD|Ludodactylus'} CR to 4 and increase its XP to 1100 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Bred for War
entries: {@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD} have been specially bred for combat. It can be equipped with Heavy Armor, increasing its AC to 18, but its fly speed is reduced to 35 ft. {@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD} takes on a heavily armoured appearance.

{@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD} can also be mounted by any Small humanoid. If it is mounted by an NPC, they are armed with a {@item lance|XPHB} and {@creature Ludodactylus|PartneredDDDoD} can use its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make one of the following attacks:

entries.name: Mounted Lance
entries: {@i Melee Attack Roll:} +7, reach 10 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} 11 ({@damage 1d12 + 5}) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Lancing Projectile
entries: {@i Ranged Attack Roll:} +7, range 30 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} 10 ({@damage 3d4 + 3}) Force damage.

entries.altText: Tetrapodophis, a small snake-like animal with four tiny legs, swims through shallow algae-rich waters.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Tetrapodophis|PartneredDDDoD|Tetrapodophis'} CR to 1/2 and increase its XP to 100 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Deadly Snake-like Venom
entries: Tetrapodophis is brightly coloured with stripes or other patterns warning of its venomous nature. Tetrapodophis' Vicious Tiny Nip attack gains the following effect when it hits:

{@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 14. {@i Failure:} 4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) Poison damage, the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, and one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} (to a maximum of four). {@i Success:} The Poisoned condition and one level of Exhaustion (to a maximum of four).

entries.altText: Two Tupandactylus pterosaurs fly past the tops of trees heavy with fruit. Their head crests form an enormous sail over each head, as well as hang down from their lower jaws.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Tupandactylus|PartneredDDDoD|Tupandactylus'} CR to 3 and increase its XP to 700 accordingly.

entries.name: Tupi Thunder God
entries: {@creature Tupandactylus|PartneredDDDoD} takes its name from the Tupi Thunder God. {@creature Tupandactylus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder damage and its Beak-Slash attack deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage.

entries.name: Actions
Thundering Display (Recharge 3-6)
entries: {@creature Tupandactylus|PartneredDDDoD} channels the power of thunder, generating a shock wave by vibrating its wings.

{@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 12, each other creature in a 15 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Thunder damage and {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the end of their next turn. {@i Success:} Half damage.

entries.altText: The small fluffy theropod dinosaur

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Ubirajara|PartneredDDDoD|"Ubirajara"'s} CR.

entries.name: Lord of Spears
entries: "{@creature Ubirajara|PartneredDDDoD}" can alternatively make a single ranged attack whereby it fires spears of filamentous integument at a creature with the following profile:

entries.name: Filamentous Spear
entries: {@i Ranged Attack Roll:} +5, range 30 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} 8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) Piercing damage.

entries.name: Return Home (1/day)
entries: "{@creature Ubirajara|PartneredDDDoD}" opens an interplanar portal 10 ft. in front of itself. The portal leads to a destination that it considers to be home anywhere in the multiverse and remains open for 1 minute or until "{@creature Ubirajara|PartneredDDDoD}" falls {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. The portal is big enough to allow creatures up to a size of Large through it.

entries.altText: Herds of different species of dinosaurs put their differences aside to drink together at a watering hole, wading through thick mud to reach the water.
Near a waterway, an Arizonasaurus carries off its unlucky prey. Its sail is tattered from damage.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Arizonasaurus'} CR to 2 and increase its XP to 450 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Arizona Heat
entries: {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} radiates incredible heat. At the end of each of {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD}' turns, each creature in a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage. Then, each creature in a 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} takes an additional 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Fire damage. {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage.
If there are multiple {@creature Arizonasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} persisting in a region with this Trait, that region will experience a prolonged drought.

entries.altText: A Centrosaurus wanders through some shrubland. Its thick nose horn is shiny black and very long.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Centrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Centrosaurus'} CR to 4 and increase its XP to 1100 accordingly.

entries.name: Bonus Actions
Mirror Image: Monoclonius (1/day)
entries: {@creature Centrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} casts {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} (level 2 version) without requiring components or a spell slot. Each illusion persists for 24 hours, rather than 1 minute.
When approaching a herd of {@creature Centrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}, at least one will already have this spell active.

entries.altText: Two Concavenator rest at sunset. Orange light fills the scene as they watch the sunset.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Concavenator|PartneredDDDoD|Concavenator's} CR to 4 and increase its XP to 1100 accordingly.

entries.name: Landshark
entries: {@creature Concavenator|PartneredDDDoD} gains {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} 30 ft. and a burrow speed of 30 ft., but cannot burrow through solid stone. While burrowing, it has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} (although its general location is revealed by its protruding hump, which glides along the ground).

entries.name: Actions
Burrowing Dive
entries: {@creature Concavenator|PartneredDDDoD} burrows downwards deeper underground, preparing to strike its next target. It has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} and cannot attack or be attacked (other burrowing creatures ignore this).

At the start of {@creature Concavenator|PartneredDDDoD}'s next turn, it bursts upwards, unearthing itself and ending its burrowing. Until the end of that turn, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks and cannot use its Burrowing Dive action.

entries.altText: Wandering through a marshland, ankle-deep in water, an enormous Deinocheirus chews on a leafy branch.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Deinocheirus|PartneredDDDoD|Deinocheirus'} CR to 8 and increase its XP to 3900 accordingly.

entries.name: Swamp Lord
entries: {@creature Deinocheirus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold and Poison damage.

entries.name: Swampy Vomit (Recharge 5-6)
entries: {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC 15, each creature in a 40 ft. long, 5 ft. wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@i Failure:} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Poison damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Bludgeoning damage. {@i Success:} Half damage.

entries.altText: An enormous Deinosuchus lifts its head above the water to finish off an unfortunate turtle. Its tail also juts out of the water, revealing the animal

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Deinosuchus|PartneredDDDoD|Deinosuchus'} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Regional Demigod
entries: {@creature Deinosuchus|PartneredDDDoD} is worshiped by local humanoids as the embodiment of primal power and is accompanied by an entourage of humanoids that adorn it with giant flower rings, vividly coloured paints, and fine silks, and ritualistically clean its teeth as it basks in the sun.

{@creature Deinosuchus|PartneredDDDoD} will not attack humanoids unless in self-defence and it is considered an extreme offence to these people to disrespect or attack {@creature Deinosuchus|PartneredDDDoD}. Typically, these humanoids will demand an offering of food for {@creature Deinosuchus|PartneredDDDoD} to safely pass through its territory.

entries.altText: The giant-headed Erythrosuchus wanders through an arid desert.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Erythrosuchus|PartneredDDDoD|Erythrosuchus'} CR to 9 and increase its XP to 5000 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Maw of Madness
entries: A creature bit by {@creature Erythrosuchus|PartneredDDDoD}' Monstrous Jaw attack suffers the following effect:

{@i Wisdom Saving Throw:} DC 12. {@i Failure:} The hit creature's Intelligence score is reduced to 3 for 1 minute. During this time, their PB is 0, they cannot speak, read, write, understand language, and may only act on their instincts.

entries.altText: As a flock of Falcatakely fly near two passing sauropods, one settles in for a sleep while another displays next to it, spreading its wings and raising its tail feathers.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD|Falcatakely's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Bountiful Harvest
entries: {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD} radiate druidic energies and their presence increases the yield of all surrounding plants. If {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD} is present in an environment for more than a week, all plants in the local region double the amount of fruit, berries, and flowers they produce. This effect diminishes and productivity returns to normal over the course of a week if {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD} leaves the area.
Islands inhabited by colonies of many {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD} are usually tropical paradises.

entries.name: Familiar
entries: {@creature Falcatakely|PartneredDDDoD} may be used as a familiar via the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell or any similar effect. If you do so, we recommend that its Fruitbringer Trait only activates each time it is summoned in a new area.

entries.altText: At a partially eaten carcasses, a giant-headed Garjania gets ready to defend its meal from a rival Garjania.

entries.title: Ogygiocarella
entries.altText: A top-down view of an Ogygiocarella trilobite fossil.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Garjainia|PartneredDDDoD|Garjainia's} or {@creature Garjainia (Swarm)|PartneredDDDoD|Garjainia (Swarm)'s} CR.

entries.name: Piranha-like Swarm
entries: If you wish, you may treat a group of 4-5 {@creature Garjainia|PartneredDDDoD} as a CR 6 swarm (see the {@creature Garjainia (Swarm)|PartneredDDDoD} stat block).

entries.name: Power Syphon
entries: Each time a creature is hit by Over-Sized Bite attack, roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 1-10, nothing happens. On a roll of 11-20, the hit creature expends one unused spell slot (determined at random).

entries.altText: Several huge Giraffitian watch as two bulls prepare to fight while standing in the lapping waves of a rocky coastline.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD|Giraffatitan's} CR to 11 and increase its XP to 7,200 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Evolutionary Arms Race
entries: Each time {@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD} is hit by an attack or fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB}, roll on the {@area Minor Mutation Table|1e9|x} and apply the result to {@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD}, rerolling if {@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD} already has the effect that the mutation would confer.
Alternatively, instead of using the Minor Mutation Table you may increase the reach of both of {@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD}'s attacks by 5 ft.
{@creature Giraffatitan|PartneredDDDoD} gains the mutation or increased attack range for 1 hour.

entries.altText: As the rest of the herd watches silently, an older male Iguanodon prepares to see off an upstart youngster. Its hands are held ready with its thumb spike facing towards its foe.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD|Iguanodon's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Crystal Palace Horned History
entries: You may choose for {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD} to have a much more lizard-like appearance and a large, pointed horn on its snout instead of clawed thumbs. If you do, replace all instances of "Thumb Gore" in its stat block with "Horn Gore".

entries.name: The Bone Wars
entries: One of two greedy palaeontologists (Marsh or Cope) refuse to allow anyone to study {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD}'s remains and have hidden explosives on every member of this species. If {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD} is slain, do not end combat. A loud ticking sound can be heard emanating from its remains and, after 2 rounds, they detonate with a large explosion, creating the following effect:

{@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC 12, each creature in a 15 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD}'s remains. {@i Failure:} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Fire damage and 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Bludgeoning damage. {@i Success:} Half damage. {@i Failure or Success:} Iganodon's remains are completed destroyed.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Juravenator|PartneredDDDoD|Juravenator's} CR to 1/8 and increase its XP to 25 accordingly.

entries.name: Adult Form: Borb
entries: {@creature Juravenator|PartneredDDDoD} has a chubby and puffed-up feathered appearance. Double its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, movement speed, to-hit bonus, and its damage becomes {@dice 1d4}. {@creature Juravenator|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage and its size category is Small.

entries.name: Familiar
entries: Alternatively, you can choose to not increase {@creature Juravenator|PartneredDDDoD}'s CR and remove the Adult Form: Borb optional rule. {@creature Juravenator|PartneredDDDoD} may then be used as a familiar via the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell or any similar effect. If you wish, it may still maintain the appearance described in Adult Form: Borb.

entries.altText: Curious about something in the distance, a Kentrosaurus stands on a fallen branch to see further ahead. It has huge spikes pointing out of its back backwards, which gradually transition into plates towards its head.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Kentrosaurus'} CR.

entries.name: Traits
The Hoodening
entries: Channelling Kentish folklore, {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} is able to magically disguise itself as a horse. It will appear to be a wild horse to any observer. The disguise can be discerned by a DC 15 {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check, or is revealed when {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} attacks.

While {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} is disguised as a horse, any creature that attempts to mount or ride it suffers {@damage 2d10} Piercing damage and the disguise is revealed. If a creature otherwise attempts to touch {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}, they take {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and are made aware that something is amiss.

entries.altText: A flock of Klobiodon fish along a calm waterway during sunset. Their bodies are covered in white downy fur, but their wings are yellow with white stripes.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Klobiodon|PartneredDDDoD|Klobiodon's} CR.

entries.name: Hiding in Plain Sight
entries: Klobiodon's fossils sat unassigned to a new species for decades in a museum drawer. As long as Klobiodon is motionless, it has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. In the first round of combat, if Klobiodon was Invisible at the start of the round, its Toothed Gnaw deals an additional {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage this round.

entries.altText: Cautious of potential predators, a Kulindadromeus moves amongst a tree

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Kulindadromeus|PartneredDDDoD|Kulindadromeus'} CR.

entries.name: Progenitor of Giants
entries: {@creature Kulindadromeus|PartneredDDDoD} is among the first of the major herbivore lineage Ornithischia. All other herbivores within this lineage (Heterodontosaurs, Stegosaurs, Ankylosaurs, Iguanodontids, Hadrosaurs, etc. (e.g. {@creature Bolong|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Iguanodon|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Kentrosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Scelidosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}, {@creature Struthiosaurus|PartneredDDDoD}, and {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} in this book)) treat {@creature Kulindadromeus|PartneredDDDoD} as a close relative and will protect it with their lives. They will ward off any threats to {@creature Kulindadromeus|PartneredDDDoD} and ensure that it can feed safely.

entries.altText: Several Leptonectes ichthyosaurs dive down to the seafloor in search of food. Their long snouts turn have a downward turned mouth, giving them a frowning look.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD|Leptonectes'} CR to 5 and increase its XP to 1800 accordingly.

entries.name: Actions
Grimace
entries: {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD} grimaces with its down-turned jaw, creating the following effect:

{@i Charisma Saving Throw:} DC 11, each other creature within a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that can see {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD}. {@i Failure:} The {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Legendary Action Uses: 1
entries: Immediately after another creature's turn, {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD} can expend a use to take one of the following actions. {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD} regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Legendary Action: Sneering Swipe
entries: {@creature Leptonectes|PartneredDDDoD} swims up to 5 ft., then makes a Snout Skewer attack (this attack cannot benefit from from the additional damage).

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Mastodonsaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Mastodonsaurus'} CR to 5 and increase its XP to 1800 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Gurgling Energies
entries: When a creature is hit by {@creature Mastodonsaurus|PartneredDDDoD}' Tusked Bite, it suffers the following effect:

{@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 14. {@i Failure:} Roll a {@dice D4} on the table below. The hit creature takes 4 ({@damage 1d8}) damage of a type corresponding to the result. {@creature Mastodonsaurus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to that damage type until the start of its next turn.

entries.altText: A hungry Megalosaurus strips a carcass as several pterosaurs sit in the wings, waiting their turn to feed. The large bodied predatory theropod dinosaur has short arms, but a powerful head and neck.
A young sauropod bursts out of the tree line and tumbles into a river as it tries to escape a pursuing Megalosaurus. The Megalosaurus

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Megalosaurus'} CR to 5 and increase its XP to 1800 accordingly.

entries.name: Curse: First of its Kind
entries: The first time a humanoid (including player characters) sees {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} while within 60 ft. of it, they are affected by a curse that causes them to momentarily lose all understanding of dinosaurs and other Mesozoic creatures (no save allowed). The curse persists for two rounds or until they take damage. For each creature afflicted, roll a {@dice d4} and consult the table below to determine how they behave:

items: Curious - The humanoid becomes unaware of any threat {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} poses. They cannot attack it or cast detrimental spells/cantrips against it and must move directly towards it if possible.

Threatened - On the humanoid's next turn, they must make a ranged or melee attack against {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} or cast a cantrip that targets it. If the humanoid has Multiattack, they instead only make a single attack.

Adoring - The humanoid must attempt to feed or heal {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} on their next turn. {@creature Megalosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} can accept food as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and will then prioritise killing other creatures over any that have fed it or healed it.
Terrified - The humanoid becomes {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of {@i Megalosaurus}.

entries.altText: With the rain falls around them, a mated pair of the sauropod Mnyamawatuka perform a courtship dance.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Mnyamawamtuka|PartneredDDDoD|Mnyamawamtuka's} CR to 6 and increase its XP to 2300 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
Heart-Shaped Soul
entries: A creature hit by one of {@creature Mnyamawamtuka|PartneredDDDoD}'s attacks suffers the following effect:

{@i Charisma Saving Throw:} DC 10. {@i Failure:} The {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. The Charmed creature will fetch food for {@creature Mnyamawamtuka|PartneredDDDoD}. Once this charm ends, the Charmed creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

entries.altText: With blood streaming behind it as it rises to the ocean

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Mosasaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Mosasaurus'} CR to 12 and increase its XP to 8400 accordingly.

entries.name: Rogue Wave (1/day)
entries: If a storm is present, {@creature Mosasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} casts the spell {@spell Tsunami|XPHB} (level 8 version) without requiring components or a spell slot.

entries.name: Stormbringer
entries: {@creature Mosasaurus|PartneredDDDoD} creates a storm centered on itself that has a radius of 1 mile and persists for 1 hour.

entries.altText: An unhappy Nothosaurus hunkers down on a rock, pelted by tropical rains.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Nothosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Nothosaurus'} CR to 4 and increase its XP to 1100 accordingly.

entries.name: Charged Skin
entries: {@creature Nothosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Lightning damage.

entries.name: Spit Lightning
entries: {@i Ranged Attack Roll:} +5, range 100 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} 14 ({@damage 2d10 + 3}) Lightning damage.

entries.name: Legendary Action: Lightning Overload (Recharge 4-6)
entries: {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 11, each creature within a 15 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} 13 ({@damage 3d6 + 3}) Lightning damage. {@i Success:} Half damage.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Nyctosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Nyctosaurus'} CR to 1/4 and increase its XP to 50 accordingly.

entries.name: Aura of Blindsight
entries: {@creature Nyctosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} 60 ft. Any other {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} {@creature Nyctosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} within a 100 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} 10 ft.

entries.name: "Night Lizard" (2/day)
entries: {@creature Nyctosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} casts the spell {@spell Darkness|XPHB} (level 2 version) without requiring components or a spell slot. However, it automatically loses {@status Concentration|XPHB} if it takes damage.

entries.altText: Under the watchful eyes of their father, tiny Oviraptor chicks run along the top of a sand dune. Both the chicks and the father have mottled white and brown feathers.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Oviraptor|PartneredDDDoD|Oviraptor's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Egg/Offspring Thief
entries: The original misinterpretation of {@creature Oviraptor|PartneredDDDoD} as opportunistic egg thieves, when all evidence shows that they were actually attentive parents has left a bitter resentment within all {@creature Oviraptor|PartneredDDDoD}.

These creatures will now steal eggs and/or young of other species (including humanoids), but rather than devouring them, will instead care for them diligently and raise them as their own. {@creature Oviraptor|PartneredDDDoD} has proficiency in {@skill Stealth|XPHB} checks (for a total of +5) while stealing offspring.

entries.altText: As the migration season begins, juvenile Pterodaustro take to the wing alongside the adults. These pink pterosaurs have brush-like fine teeth.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Pterodaustro|PartneredDDDoD|Pterodaustro's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Swallowed Gemstone
entries: When encountering a group of {@creature Pterodaustro|PartneredDDDoD}, one or more of them may be enchanted with a magical element from a gemstone they have swallowed. That {@creature Pterodaustro|PartneredDDDoD} will glow with a soft hue and the damage type of its attacks will change to the corresponding type for that gemstone. You may roll a {@dice D10} or select from the table below to determine the gemstone swallowed, colour hue, and damage type:
When {@creature Pterodaustro|PartneredDDDoD} is slain, the gemstone it swallowed is regurgitated (worth 50 GP).

entries.altText: A towering Quetzalcoatlus looks down on an distinctly unimpressed woman.
Baby Triceratops cower as two hungry Quetzalcoatlus loom over them in a forest clearing

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD|Quetzalcoatlus's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Low-Gravity Aura
entries: {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} drastically reduces the weight of objects and creatures in contact with it (including itself). A real {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} would usually be able to carry a maximum weight of about 80-100 lb. This Trait to increases its carry weight limit to 500 lb. and any howdah or saddle attached to it are considered weightless for the purposes of its carry weight. For each 100 lb. {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} is carrying, reduce its fly speed by 10 ft.

entries.name: Aircraft-Sized Animal
entries: {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} can carry up to three Medium (or smaller) humanoids on its back, and two further Medium (or smaller) humanoids in its hind claws. For each creature carried in this way, {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD}' fly speed is reduced by 10 ft.
If {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} is carrying two or more creatures using this rule, it cannot use its Lift Off {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Feathered God
entries: You may choose for {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} to be covered in vivid feathers.

entries.name: Lift Off
entries: While flying, {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} picks up an object or creature weighing up to 500 lb. and up to Large in size. While carrying this object, its fly speed is reduced by 10 ft. for each 100 lb. the object/creature weighs.

entries.name: Drop Off
entries: While flying, {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD} drops an object or creature it is holding: {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC 16 or 12 (if dropped from above 50 ft.), a creature below {@creature Quetzalcoatlus|PartneredDDDoD}. {@i Failure:} The creature below takes 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage, or 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Bludgeoning damage (if from above 50 ft.). {@i Failure or Success:} The dropped object/creature takes appropriate falling damage.

entries.altText: The small pterosaur Rhamphorhynchus walks across a sandy shore, leaving footprints behind.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD|Rhamphorhynchus'} CR.

entries.name: Actions
Snatch & Swallow
entries: {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC 12, one creature within 5 ft. of {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD}. {@i Failure:} {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD} snatches and swallows a small item (trinket, Potion, wand, {@item dagger|XPHB}, etc.) that it can see that the creature is wielding or has on their clothing.

If the item is a wand, {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD}' Spike-Toothed Snap damage type becomes Force (or another appropriate damage type). If the item is a Potion or food, {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD} consumes that item. Any swallowed non-food or non-potion item is regurgitated upon {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD}' death, and each Potion is returned as an empty vial.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Rhamphorhynchus (Swarm)|PartneredDDDoD|Rhamphorhynchus swarm's} CR.

entries.name: Enchanted Swarm
entries: {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD} (Swarm) has already snatched dozens of magical items and incorporated them into their attacks. Each time {@creature Rhamphorhynchus|PartneredDDDoD} swarm makes a Spike-Toothed Snap attack, you may roll a {@dice D10} and change the damage type of the attack according to the list below:

entries.altText: An armoured Scelidosaurus carefully makes its way down an uneven slope covered in bushes and broken twigs.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Scelidosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Scelidosaurus'} CR.

entries.name: Domesticatable
entries: {@creature Scelidosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} is particularly trustful of Small and Medium-sized creatures, largely due to its formidable defences. It is relatively easy to domesticate, and players can befriend a {@creature Scelidosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} by feeding it consistently for a {@dice 1d4 + 1} days. However, its Razor Osteoderms prevent {@creature Scelidosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} from being ridden without a bespoke saddle. Nevertheless, they make for friendly travelling companions.

entries.title: Example damselfly: {@i Megaloprepus caerulatus}
entries.altText: A top-down view of the example damselfly Megaloprepus caerulatus.
In search of food, a Sharovipteryx glides between trees at sunset. It drifts on a membrane supported by its hindlegs.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Sharovipteryx|PartneredDDDoD|Sharovipteryx's} CR.

entries.name: Familiar
entries: {@creature Sharovipteryx|PartneredDDDoD} may be used as a familiar via the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell or any similar effect.

entries.name: Podopteryx (1/day)
entries: {@creature Sharovipteryx|PartneredDDDoD} takes on the appearance of its original namesake, the Damselfly Podopteryx, for 1 minute. During this time, it has a 40 ft. fly speed, its size becomes Tiny, and its AC becomes 17.

entries.altText: Tiny pterosaurs scatter to avoid a fight between two long-necked Tanystropheus in some scrubland.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Tanystropheus|PartneredDDDoD|Tanystropheus'} CR to 2 and increase its XP to 450 accordingly.

entries.name: Traits
entries: {@b {@i Basal Hydra}}. Increase {@creature Tanystropheus|PartneredDDDoD}' {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to 58. Each time {@creature Tanystropheus|PartneredDDDoD} takes damage, it grows an additional head up to a maximum of six. When {@creature Tanystropheus|PartneredDDDoD} uses Multiattack, it may make an additional Nip attack for each head beyond the first, up to a maximum of six Nip attacks.
{@creature Tanystropheus|PartneredDDDoD} starts with two heads.

entries.altText: Having just spotted prey, a Utahraptar slowly approaches through a forest, trying to get close enough to strike. Its yellow eyes are locked on its target.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Utahraptor|PartneredDDDoD|Utahraptor's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Mimicking Cry
entries: {@creature Utahraptor|PartneredDDDoD} can imitate the sound of any creature or noise it has heard with accuracy, much like a parrot. It tends to use this Trait while {@action Hide|XPHB|Hidden} to lure prey closer to it.

If a creature uses its {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to examine the sound, it can determine that it is a mimicked effect with a successful DC 14 {@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Perception|XPHB} check.

entries.altText: A Velociraptor spreads its feathers to hide the Protoceratops kill beneath its feet in an arid hilly badlands.
Small mammals flee up a rocky incline as a hungry Velociraptor gives chase.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Velociraptor|PartneredDDDoD|Velociraptor's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Vivid Familial Groups
entries: Each time the party encounter {@creature Velociraptor|PartneredDDDoD}, it may be present in groups of 3-6 animals, representing a family group. Some of these animals may be {@action Hide|XPHB|Hidden} nearby. This group consists of an adult male, adult female, and 1-4 subadult animals.
These animals all share a similar dazzling under-plumage that is hidden by overlying feathers (it does not hinder their ability to be stealthy) and is unique to their group.

entries.name: Actions
Dazzling Reveal
entries: {@creature Velociraptor|PartneredDDDoD} unleashes a dazzling array of magical display feathers.

{@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC 12, one creature withing 30 ft. that can see {@creature Velociraptor|PartneredDDDoD}. {@i Failure:} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) damage of a type corresponding to the feather's colours (DM's choice).

entries.altText: A juvenile Tyrannosaurus breaks into a sprint, throwing up a dust cloud as it passes.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Young Tyrannosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Young Tyrannosaurus'} CR, but keep in mind that this adds two extra CR 8 creatures to the encounter.

entries.name: Cliff Scene
entries: When {@creature Young Tyrannosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it lets out a shrill cry. A few moments later, the roar of two adult Tyrannosaurus rex can be heard in the distance. After 1 minute, two {@creature Tyrannosaurus Rex|XMM} (see {@book Monster Manual|XMM}) appear and attack the party, focusing initially on whoever reduced the {@creature Young Tyrannosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If another adult Tyrannosaurus is already present, this affect does not occur.

entries.altText: Lightning cracks above two armoured Zuul, which lie waiting by a stream and several felled trees for the storm to pass.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD|Zuul's} CR to 7 and increase its XP to 2900 accordingly.

entries.name: Ectoplasmic Reach
entries: A ghoulish jelly-like substance extends the from {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD}'s tail. Increase the reach of {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD}'s Clubbed Tail attack to 15 ft. and change its damage type to Necrotic.

entries.name: Actions
The Gatekeeper (1/day)
entries: {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} attempts to open an interdimensional portal directly in front of it that ejects malicious energies. Roll a {@dice D20}:

On a 1, {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} detonates with malicious magical energies, dealing {@damage 8d8} Necrotic damage to itself and {@damage 4d8} Necrotic damage to each other creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

On a 2-10, an unstable portal forms for 1 minute and pulses with malicious energy, triggering the following effect: {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 12, each non-{@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

On a 11-19, an metastable portal forms for 1 minute and pulses with malicious energy, triggering the following effect: {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC 12, each non-{@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. {@i Failure:} {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage for 1 minute and {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

On a 20, an stable portal forms for 1 minute and radiates malicious energy. Each non-{@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} creature within a 25 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} from the portal. has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage and takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage at the start of each of their turns.
If {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} is slain, the portal it created either closes or stabilises to another plane of existence (DM's decision) for {@dice 1d20} minutes.

entries.name: Pulse Portal
entries: {@creature Zuul|PartneredDDDoD} pulses an unstable or metastable portal, triggering the portal's effect again.

entries.altText: A wise Tyrannosaurus flees from a giant Alamosaurus bearing down on it. The titans kick up dust of the arid scrub as they run.
A brave but foolish knight faces off against the Ancient Tyrannosaurus in the darkness as his white horse rears in panic. His lance is a mere needle compared to the beast
A scarred blue Tyrannosaurus takes in its domain during sunset.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex|PartneredDDDoD}'s CR.

entries.name: Imparted Speech
entries: {@creature Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex|PartneredDDDoD} can understand Archosauric and another language of your choosing (usually Common). It can speak Archosauric, albeit slowly. Increase its Intelligence score to 8.

entries.name: Wise Old Beast
entries: {@creature Ancient Tyrannosaurus rex|PartneredDDDoD} has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws.

entries.altText: Big Al, a young female Allosaurus hobbles along a hillside near her freshly laid eggs. Her fingers are broken, her toes warped and she hasn

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD|Big Al's} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Big Al's Ballad
entries: When {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} awakens at dawn each day or is in combat, dramatic orchestral music plays loudly centred over her location and all of {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD}'s choices, thoughts, and actions are also narrated by a disembodied, stoic British voice. This music and voice can only be heard by player characters.

entries.name: Story Set in Stone
entries: {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} cannot be killed by normal means. If {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or suffers an effect that would kill her, she instead falls to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, cannot attack, loses her Steady {@variantrule Healing|XPHB} Trait, and will flee from combat.

She can only take lethal damage from her Clumsy Trait. If she does not trip while fleeing, she will wander for 24 hours, then die emaciated on the nearest riverbank. However, if {@creature Big Al|PartneredDDDoD} is healed during this 24 hour period (excluding from a Short/{@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}), she regains her Steady {@variantrule Healing|XPHB} Trait, is able to attack again, and may behave normally.

entries.altText: An enraged Carnotaurus chases down a horseman. The horse

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, you do not need to change {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Carnotaurus'} CR.

entries.name: Traits
Venerated Headwear
entries: Local people venerate the {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} and worship them by adorning them with a variety of headdresses as they sleep. This is seen as a right-of-passage or coming-of-age ceremony by some cultures and is a test of an individual's stealth and sleight of hand. With {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD}' short arms unable to reach its head, headwear may stay on one for several weeks or months. This headwear is often crafted from expensive silks or inlaid with precious gemstones and can be highly valuable (we recommend a value of {@dice 2d100 + 50} GP). This leads to {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} sometimes being targeted by bandits for raids which, more often than not, results in an easy meal for the {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD}.
Stolen headdresses are seen as contraband by their respective cultures.

entries.name: A Familiar Smell
entries: {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} becomes accustomed to the smell of its Venerated Headwear and will instinctively follow its scent if stolen. A player or NPC harbouring stolen Venerated Headwear will be hunted by its respective {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD}. That {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} automatically passes any {@skill Perception|XPHB} check to detect its Venerated Headwear that involves smell.

If that {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} is alive and not {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, roll a {@dice D6} whenever the harbouring player/NPC takes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. On a 5 or 6, the {@creature Carnotaurus|PartneredDDDoD} interrupts and attacks them during that {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.altText: Baby Dilophosaurus scatter as a hungry adult decides to resort to cannibalism in its search for food. The blistering desert behind it shows how desperate times have become.

entries.name: Optional Magical Rules
entries: If you choose to use the optional magical rules listed below, change {@creature Dilophosaurus|PartneredDDDoD|Dilophosaurus'} CR to 4 and increase its XP to 1100 accordingly.

entries.name: Anthesis to Spitting
entries: {@creature Dilophosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} could never spit venom and it despises all suggestions that it should. This has given it an innate magical aura that protects it from similar attacks. All ranged attacks against {@creature Dilophosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. Additionally, {@creature Dilophosaurus|PartneredDDDoD} has immunity to Poison and Acid damage.

entries.altText: Panicked cave divers within a huge, flooded cavern rush to the surface to try and escape the massive anglerfish-like Spinosaurus Wretchglow, the Last Light.

entries.title: {@i Melanocetus johnsonii}
entries.altText: A front view of a modern anglerfish, Melanocetus johnsonii.

In a volcanic cave, lava bubbles and steams as an adventurer leaps to attack the horrifically mutated Spinosaurus Xuthul, The Prismatic Terror. Crystals erupt from its body, replacing the spine and teeth.
A pile of large hexagonal crystals that are yellow, gold, and grey in colour.

While several strange semi-aquatic reptiles called Helveticosaurus rest in shallow marshy water, two decide to take the opportunity to battle for dominance, with one biting the other fiercely and kicking up water.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries: In fantasy games, worlds are typically populated by monstrous creatures behaving in ways that real animals don't. It's extremely rare for a real animal to attack on sight and fight to the death without ever considering fleeing, yet this is how the vast majority of roleplaying encounters play out. To better emulate realistic behaviour, you may use the tables here. These are designed to give approximations of behaviour that real dinosaurs exhibited, albeit designed in a way so that they can still be an interesting roleplaying encounter. You may roll or select the results and they may apply to an individual creature or a whole species. These tables are separated into carnivores and herbivores. If your chosen creature is an omnivore, you may pick any appropriate table.

entries.name: Fleeing Creatures
entries: Many creatures will attempt to flee when threatened. If a creature escapes the battle and the players wish to track it down, roll opposing {@skill Survival|XPHB} checks. Players may only attempt this once per fleeing creature.

entries.name: Carnivores
entries: {@i Some carnivores may be largely stationary ambush predators (similar to modern crocodiles). For those creatures, we suggest you use the ambush table when putting them in your world.}

entries.caption: Small and Medium Carnivore Table
rows: {@b Asleep} - The creature is asleep. If awoken by a failed {@skill Stealth|XPHB} check (with a DC equal to the sleeping creature's {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB}), treat this result as a 4-5.

{@b Skittish} - The creature will attack for one round, then attempt to flee. If this creature is present in numbers equal to or greater than the party, or if it is larger than every party member, treat this result as an 8 instead.
{@b Defensively fearful} - The creature will attempt to intimidate the players and attack if provoked. If it is becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, it will attempt to flee.
{@b Aggressively territorial} - The creature attempts to intimidate the party. If they attack it, or do not leave, it will attack and fight to the death.
{@b Opportunistic feeder} - The creature attacks, attempting to kill and devour the players. It will only attempt to flee if near death.

entries.caption: Ambush Carnivore Table
rows: {@b Waiting in ambush} - The creature uses any Traits or Actions it has to keep entirely {@action Hide|XPHB|Hidden}, attacking at anything (other than its own species) that comes within half of its speed. It will cease attacking and flee, attempting to hide again if near death.
{@b Basking} - The creature is conspicuously visible, basking in the sun to warm itself. It will only attack if threatened and will attempt to flee if it becomes {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.
{@b Patrolling territory} - The creature is actively patrolling its hunting or mating grounds. It will attack and fight to the death anything it encounters but won't pursue them if they flee.

entries.caption: Large Carnivore Table
rows: {@b Asleep} - The creature is asleep. If awoken by a failed {@skill Stealth|XPHB} check (with a DC equal to the sleeping creature's {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB}), treat this result as an 8.

{@b Rest and digest} - The creature is aware of the party, but cares little and has already fed. If they come within 10 ft. of it, it will attempt to intimidate them and will only attack if they touch it or attack it.

{@b Irritable} - The creature will attempt to drive the players away with an intimidating threat display. If they don't leave or if they attack, it will fight back. It will only attempt to flee if near death. If it escapes, it will recover to full strength (complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}) and then actively hunt the players.

{@b Territorial challenge} - The creature perceives the party's intrudance as a challenge. It attempts to intimidate the party once, then immediately attacks if the players do not flee. It will fight to the death.

{@b Actively hunting} - The creature attacks the players, only fleeing if near death. It will focus on the weakest-looking member of the party. If the party escapes, it will continue to pursue them as long as it is able. To track the players, the creature must roll a contested {@skill Survival|XPHB} check vs the party member with the lowest survival modifier. Abilities that cover the party's track (such as a Ranger's {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB}) renders the creature unable to track the party.

entries.altText: A Tyrannosaurus uses its head as a battering ram and drives it into the chest of a rival. A massive amount of dirt and grit is kicked into the air by their titanic fight.

entries.name: Herbivores
entries: {@i The behaviour of a herbivore that can flee a predator (i.e. a} Gallimimus{@i ) and one that can't (i.e. an} Ankylosaurus{@i ) is very different when threatened. Use your own judgement when determining whether a creature is 'fast' or 'slow', but we recommend treating any herbivore with a speed of 20 ft. or less as 'slow'. For very large and slow sauropods, you can roll on either the Large Herbivore or Armoured/Slow Herbivore tables.}

entries.caption: Large Herbivore Table
rows: {@b Oblivious} - The sheer size of this creature makes the party seem like little more than pests. It will only attack if they attack it first. Ignore this result if anything in the party is the same size category as this creature.
{@b Fearful} - The strangeness of the party intimidates this creature. It avoids them if possible and flees if they approach.
{@b Challenged} - The creature will make a threat display, attempting to intimidate the party. If approached or attacked, it will fight to the death.

{@b Rutting} - Select either oblivious or fearful and apply that result to all members of this species in this encounter, bar one or two (or more depending on population size) individuals. Those exceptions are rutting and will attack the party. They will knock players {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}, but not purposely kill them. They will submit and cease attacking if they become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. If there are two or more rutting creatures of the same species, they will prioritise attacking each other first.

entries.caption: Armored/Slow Herbivore Table
rows: {@b Immutable defence} - This creature trusts its defences and ignores the party. It will only attack if it is attacked first. If the attacker ceases attacking, so too will this creature.
{@b Stand ground} - The creature makes a show of strength, stomping and posturing. It will attack if approached or attacked. However, it will not pursue a fleeing target.
{@b Push back} - The creature immediately charges the party on sight, letting out an angry cry. It will attack until the opponent dies or flees, but will not pursue a fleeing target.

entries.caption: Small and Medium Herbivore Table
rows: {@b Skittish} - The creature will attempt to flee and only attack if trapped or immobilised.
{@b Frozen} - The creature will stay motionless until attacked. It will then either flee or fight, fleeing when near death.
{@b Backed into a corner} - The creature will fight to the death.

entries.altText: Two sauropods are too absorbed in their fight to pay heed to the raging storm or rising flood waters. Reared on their hind legs, they toppled their weight against each other.

entries.name: Mutation Tables
entries: Below are tables outlining genetic or magical mutations that you can use to make your creatures more flavourful, interesting, or simply more challenging. These mutations could represent regional variations of species, or perhaps the experiments of a mad Wizard. You may select or roll for mutations on the tables below. One or more of these could be applied to an individual creature, a group of creatures (i.e. a pack or herd), or for a creature's entire species in your world. Many of these mutations can be used to re-flavour a creature to fit in a particular environment, and we have indicated which environments match which mutation.

Many of these mutations make the creature more resilient or dangerous, sometimes by a significant amount depending on its initial stat block. We recommend increasing the CR of a mutated creature by between 0, ½, or 1 for minor mutations and 2 or 3 for major mutations, although some mutations may only increase a creature's CR under certain circumstances (e.g., #2 "Extended apnea" only poses an increased threat while fighting underwater). To ensure that these mutations scale with CR, we've included some that utilise stat bonuses and proficiency bonuses (abbreviated to "PB") to calculate save DCs, hit bonuses, and damage. Ultimately, how you balance these changes is up to your discretion, so if you find that these mutations are over/underwhelming in some situations, please do adjust them to fit your needs. When you apply a mutation to a creature, add the mutation's name, flavour text, and associated effect to that creature's {@b Traits}, unless it specifies that the mutation provides a {@b Action}, {@b Bonus Action}, or {@b Reaction}, in which case add it to that creature's respective {@variantrule Action|XPHB} type.

entries.caption: Minor Mutation Table
rows: Tusked–{@i Two bulbous teeth protrude from this creature's lower jaw.}

A creature hit by an attack that involves this creature's head suffers the following effect: {@i Strength Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Strength modifier + PB). {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Piercing damage.
Extended apnea–{@i High-capacity lungs allow this creature to hold its breath for a prolonged period.}
This creature may hold its breath for up to an hour with no detrimental side-effects.
Symbiotic–{@i This creature lives benevolently among another species.}

Select another non-humanoid creature. All creatures of that species treat this creature as an ally. Additionally, this creature gains {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} in all Ability Checks while within 5 ft. of the selected creature.
Diminutive size–{@i This creature is particularly small.}
Decrease the size category of this creature by one stage (to a minimum of Tiny), decrease any damage it deals by 2 (to a minimum of 1), but add +2 to its Dexterity Saving Throws.
Rapid coagulation–{@i Blood oozing from wounds instantly clots when exposed to air.}
This creature cannot lose more than one third of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in a single turn from any combination of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.
Elongate–{@i The limbs, tail, or muzzle of this creature are particularly long.}
Select one melee attack this creature has and increase its reach by 5 ft.
Vivid plumage–{@i Beautifully coloured feathers or fur cover this creature's body.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Charisma checks.
Thermal vision–{@i Fleshy red spots on this creature's head allow it to detect heat.}
This creature has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} 40 ft., but cannot distinguish creatures from other sources of heat (like Torches).
Pachycephalisation–{@i The skull of this creature is huge and bulbous, giving it bony nodules that it can use as a weapon.}

If this creature moves 20+ ft. straight towards another creature and is within 5 ft. of it, it can use its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make the following attack: Skull Bash. {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB). {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Bludgeoning damage.
Reinforced muscle fibres–{@i Metallic fibres line this creature's muscles.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength Saving Throws.
