Prehensile tail–{@i This creature can control its tail as though it were a limb, grasping or attacking with it.}
{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Tail Swipe.} Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB), a creature within 5 or 10 ft. (DM's choice). {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Bludgeoning damage.
Alopecia–{@i All feathers, hair, and scales fall away from this creature, leaving only bare skin.}
This creature has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Slashing damage. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, reduce it.
Digital pads–{@i Soft cat-like paw pads cover the soles of this creature's feet.}
This creature makes no sound when it moves. Once per day, the first time it fails a {@skill Stealth|XPHB} check, it may instead choose to pass.
Hypertrophy–{@i Huge, bulging muscles cover this creature's body.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks.
Spinnerets–{@i Silk-producing glands protrude from this creature's body, allowing it to spin webs quickly.}
{@b Action} {@i {@b Web.}} The creature casts {@spell Web|XPHB} (level 2 version, spell save DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB)) without requiring components or a spell slot.
Aquatic–{@i This creature has webbed hands and feet, as well as gills on its neck.}
This creature gains a swim speed equal to its speed and may potentially breathe underwater (DM's choice).
Thermal sink–{@i A specialised organ in this creature's chest is able to absorb heat.}

{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Thermal Sink.}} {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Constitution modifier + PB), each other creature within a 5 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d4 +  PB} Cold damage.
Toxic secretions–{@i Poisons seep through this creature's skin or scales.}
{@b Reaction} {@i {@b Toxic Secretion.}} {@i Trigger:} Hit by a Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}. {@i Response:} The attacking creature takes {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Poison damage.
Sail-backed–{@i A row of tall skin-covered bony protrusions line this creature's back, linking to form a sail.}
This creature gets +2 to {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks and is unaffected by temperatures as high as 40° Celsius (104° Fahrenheit).
Bristle-backed–{@i Large quills or spines protrude from this creature's back.}
{@b Action} {@i {@b Bristle Shot.}} {@i Ranged Attack Roll:} +(Dexterity modifier + PB), range 30 ft. {@i Hit:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Piercing damage.
Puffable coat–{@i This creature can puff itself up with a thick fluffy coat of fur or feathers.}

This creature is unaffected by temperatures as low as -20° Celsius (-4° Fahrenheit). {@b Reaction} {@i {@b Coat Puff.}} {@i Trigger:} The creature is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw. {@i Response:} The creature takes {@dice 1d6 +  PB} less Cold damage.
Photosynthetic–{@i This creature has a vibrant green colour, as it's skin, hair, or feathers contain plant-like cells.}
This creature requires only a few hours of sunlight for a full day's nourishment. It also counts as a plant for the purposes of spells and abilities that target plants.
Floral mimicry–{@i This creature's features look remarkably plant-like. Small frills of skin and feathers mimic leaves and flowers.}

While motionless, this creature is indistinguishable from plant life. A DC (8 + Charisma bonus + PB) {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check (your choice) will reveal that this is a creature.
Septic saliva–{@i A noxious smell emanates from this creature's mouth, as it contains a horrible mixture of dangerous bacteria.}
Add {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage to any attack made by this creature that involves its mouth.
Stem cell reservoir–{@i A specialised organ holds a cluster of blank cells that can rapidly redeploy, re-growing any damaged body part.}
{@b Action} {@i {@b Stem Cell Reservoir (1/day).}} The creature recovers up to one third of its lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Bioluminescent–{@i Some part, or all, of this creature's body glows beautifully with vibrant colours while in the dark.}
This creature emits a dim hue of light in a 15 ft. radius when in the dark.
{@item Club|XPHB}-tail–{@i This creature's tail ends in a bony mass that it can use to bash targets.}
{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Club-Tail.}} {@i Melee Attack Roll:} +(Strength modifier + PB), reach 5 ft. {@i Hit:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Bludgeoning damage.
Gastric barrier–{@i This creature has a specialised digestive system that makes it particularly hardy.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution Saving Throws.
Ink sacs–{@i By squeezing specialised sacs on this creature's neck, it can spray ink from its mouth.}
{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Ink Blot.} Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB), one creature within 20 ft. {@i Failure:} The {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 2 rounds.
Nocturnal–{@i This creature naturally prefers the dark and has very large eyes.}
This creature gains {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} equal to its normal vision, or increases its {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} range by 30 ft. It is generally only active at night.
Telepathic cortex–{@i A large bump at the back of this creature's skull houses an extra brain cortex.}
This creature is able to telepathically communicate with any other members of its species within 200 ft.
Opposable claws–{@i One claw on each hand is bent inwards, forming a thumb.}
This creature may take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action with objects that require simple or complex movements, such as opening a door or using a trinket.
Interlocking scales–{@i Thick, tightly locked scales coat this creature's body.}
This creature gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing damage.
Horned–{@i Fused scales protrude from this creature's forehead or snout, forming pointed horns.}

If this creature moves 20+ ft. straight towards another creature and is within 5 ft. of it, it can use its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make the following attack: {@i {@b Horn Pierce.}} {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB). {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Piercing damage.
Fusiform–{@i This creature can tuck its arms and legs to its sides and adopt a fish-like shape.}
If this creature has a swim speed, increase it by 30 ft.
Enhanced hepatocytes–{@i This creature's liver is able to filter out any poisons almost instantly.}
This creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
Quick-witted–{@i This creature can react quickly to changing situations.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence Saving Throws.
Elongated snout–{@i The snout and nose of this creature is extended, giving it a much more powerful sense of smell.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks that involve smell.
Dermal spines–{@i Thick scales protrude from this creature, giving its body a spikey appearance.}
{@b Reaction} {@i {@b Dermal Spines.}} {@i Trigger:} Hit by a Melee {@variantrule Attack Roll|XPHB}. {@i Response:} The attacking creature takes {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Piercing damage.
Gelatinous saliva–{@i Thick globules of slimy saliva drip from this creature's mouth.}
Attacks from this creature that involve its mouth reduce a hit creature's speed by 10 ft. (to a minimum of 5 ft., non-cumulative).
Tonic immobility–{@i This creature can feign death, falling on its back with its belly up and tongue hanging out.}

Once per day, if this creature would be reduced to 0 hit points, it is instead reduced to 1. It feigns death, appearing dead unless it is inspected with a DC (8 + Wisdom bonus + PB) {@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} check (their choice). It may choose to exit this feign at any point.
Fearsome roar–{@i Powerful lungs allow this creature to let out a gaudy and terrifying roar.}

{@b Action} {@i {@b Roar.}} {@i Wisdom Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Charisma modifier + PB). {@i Failure:} The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A creature may repeat this saving throw at the end of each of their turns. {@i Success:} {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of Roar for 24 hours.
Automimicry–{@i Strange patterns and growths make it difficult to determine where this creature's head is.}
If this creature would be Critically Hit, the attack is instead resolved as a normal hit.
Sciurus tail–{@i This creature has a large fluffy tail that it can flick rapidly.}
This creature is unaffected by temperatures as low as -20° Celsius (-4° Fahrenheit) and can communicate silently with any other creatures of the same species that can see it.
Serrated denticles–{@i The claws or teeth of this creature are jagged and saw-like.}
All melee attacks this creature makes deal an additional {@damage 1d4} Slashing damage.
Hereditary memory–{@i Ancestral memories are encoded into this creature's DNA.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom Saving Throws.
Antlered–{@i Multi-pronged antlers protrude from this creature's skull. It can swing them back and forth, slashing at foes.}

If this creature moves 20+ ft. straight towards another creature and is within 5 ft. of it, it can use its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make the following attack: {@i {@b Antler Slash.}} {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Dexterity modifier + PB). {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Slashing damage.
Pneumatisation–{@i This creature has air sacs and chambers within its bones, making it much lighter.}
Half this creature's weight and increase its speed by 10 ft.
Mana-infused cortex–{@i A pale-blue glow around this creature's head reveals it has innate magical abilities.}
Select one cantrip of your choice. This creature knows that cantrip. It may cast it and its spell save DC is (8 + Wisdom Bonus + PB) and spell attack modifier is (Wisdom bonus + PB).
Bombardier gland–{@i Bulbous sacs on this creature's body allow it to spit or secrete reactive chemicals that ignite when they mix.}
Add {@damage 1d4} Fire damage to any attack made by this creature.
Thin dermis–{@i The skin of this creature is sickly thin and its veins are visible below the surface.}
This creature has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Piercing damage. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, decrease it.
Waxy skin–{@i This creature has a thick waxy coating on its skin.}
This creature is unaffected by temperatures as high as 40° Celsius (104° Fahrenheit). When this creature takes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, reduce that damage by 2.
Viperism–{@i A soft tissue frill can extend from this creature's neck, and it can spit like a viper.}

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, this creature may make one attack with the profile: {@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Venom Spit.}} {@i Ranged Attack Roll:} + (Dexterity modifier + PB), range 30 ft. {@i Hit:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Acid damage.
Finned tail–{@i This creature has a large fleshy fin on the end of its tail.}
While in water, this creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws and can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Beaked–{@i A keratinous beak sheathes this creature's snout, concealing its mouth below.}
Add {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage to any melee attack made by this creature that involves its mouth.
Bony frill–{@i A broad bony frill projects from the back of this creature's head, allowing it to shield its body from attacks.}
Increase the AC of this creature by 2.
Strong swimmer–{@i This creature has powerful limbs and broad claws/paws/hands that aid it in moving through water.}
This creature gains a swim speed equal to 75% of its speed (rounded up to the nearest 5 ft.)
Augmentative size–{@i This creature is much larger than you would expect.}
Increase this creature's size by one stage, and its attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d4} damage (of the same damage type that they normally deal), but -2 from any of its Dexterity Saving Throws.
Hyper-bioluminescence–{@i Rather than glowing dimly, for a moment this creature can flash an extremely bright bioluminescent light.}

{@b Action} {@i {@b Flash.}} {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Constitution modifier + PB), each creature within a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} The {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of their next turn.
Complex inner-ear–{@i When other creatures would fall over, this creature is able to stagger and stabilise itself.}
This creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
Thick plumage–{@i Particularly dense and thick feathers or fur cover this creature, giving it a puffy appearance.}
This creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.
Xerophytic–{@i Specialised fleshy flaps cover this creature's nostrils, and it has waxy skin or scales.}
This creature can survive without water for up to one week.
Excessive myelin–{@i This creature has a reinforced nervous system.}
This creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition.
Frail–{@i This creature appears thin and brittle.}
This creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws. Instead of increasing its CR with this mutation, decrease it.
Venomous–{@i Horrible green venom seeps from grooves in this creature's claws and teeth.}
Add {@damage 1d4} Poison damage to any melee attack made by this creature.
Agile–{@i This creature is slender and lean, able to move quickly on its feet.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity Saving Throws.
Dorsal wings–{@i A small pair of wings or wing-like flaps extend from this creature's back.}

This creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to falling damage, so long as it does not have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, and can take the following action: {@b Action} {@b {@i Flap (1/day).}} The creature casts {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} (level 2 version, spell save DC (8 + Wisdom modifier + PB)) without requiring components or a spell slot.
Gripping digital pads–{@i This creature has rough pads on its feet that strongly grip surfaces.}
While climbing, this creature can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Sparse osteoderms–{@i Dense bony lumps dot this creature's back and flanks.}
This creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Slashing damage.
Symbiotic spores–{@i Unusual cysts cover this creature's shoulders. They can pop when disturbed, filling the air with a noxious cloud.}

At the start of this creature's turn, the following effect happens: {@i {@b Spore.}} {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Constitution modifier + PB), each other creature in a 10 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d4 +  PB} Necrotic damage.
Rapid thermal regulation - {@i This creature can flush extremities with blood to rapidly cool itself.}
This creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.
Spermaceti organ (minor)–{@i This creature can emit a deafeningly loud ultra-high-pitched sound.}

{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Sonic Shout.}} {@i Constitution Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Constitution modifier + PB), each other creature in a 20 ft. {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d4 +  PB} Thunder damage and the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.
Pachydermatous–{@i The skin and scales of this creature are noticeably thickened.}
This creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage.
Hyper-pigmentation–{@i This creature's skin, feathers, spines, and/or fur are jet black in colour.}
This creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage.
Alluring pheromones–{@i This creature gives off a sweet, intoxicating smell.}
{@b Action} {@b {@i Allure (1/day).}} The creature casts {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} (level 1 version, spell save DC (8 + Charisma modifier + PB)) without requiring components or a spell slot.
Arboreal–{@i This creature is adapted to climbing trees, with hooked claws on its hands and feet.}
This creature has a climbing speed equal to its speed.
Mana gland–{@i Specialised glands on this creature's body allow it to infuse magical energies into its attacks.}
Add {@damage 1d4} Force damage to any attack made by this creature.
Dazzling plates–{@i Large vertical plates line this creature's back that can produce sudden bright red colouration when flushed with blood.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks.
Chitinous–{@i Invertebrate-like plates cover this creature's flank.}
Lithophagic–{@i This creature is able to ingest rocks and stones for sustenance.}
This creature can sustain itself by consuming rocks. Add {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage to any melee attack made by this creature that involves its mouth.
Binocular vision–{@i Two forward-facing eyes allow this creature to easily track prey.}
This creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks that involve sight.
Hoofed–{@i This creature has single stub hooved/clawed feet.}
Increase this creature's speed by 20 ft. However, this creature is slowed to 10 ft. per round in {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} (rather than speed halved).
Enhanced cerebrum–{@i A bulbous node on this creature's skull causes its eyes to protrude a little.}
{@b Bonus Action} {@i {@b Mind Pulse.}} {@i Wisdom Saving Throw:} DC (8 + Intelligence modifier + PB), one creature within 60 ft. {@i Failure:} {@damage 1d6 +  PB} Psychic damage.
Fossorial–{@i Scoop-like powerful forelimbs allow this creature to dig.}
This creature has a burrow speed of 15 ft.
Hematophagic (minor)–{@i As it injures its opponent, this creature drinks their blood.}
Whenever this creature deals damage with a melee attack, it gains {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} ({@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} do not stack).
Macropod–{@i With its unusually large feet, this creature is able to jump or rear up and perform a powerful stomp.}

entries.name: Creature Naming Tables
entries: Just like in real life, in many fantasy settings animals are given colloquial names that differ from region to region. While we have given every animal in this book its real scientific name, you may want to use alternative names in your world. To help you come up with names, we've included a series of tables below.

These tables provide a prefix and suffix that you can combine with a verb to create compelling fantasy creature names. We suggest rolling or picking one-to-two prefixes, then a suffix, and finally a verb that combine to make a three-to-four word name. Alternatively, you can choose the words that you think best characterize particular aspects of the creature you are describing. Remember that a single species may have different colloquial names in different regions. Some example names include: Razor-clawed Slasher, Dusky-cheeked Hunter, Red Horned Crusher, or Gentle Cape Gorger.
You can include an optional colour and hyphened extras if you so desire:

entries.name: Designers' Note
entries: If you use these tables to create innuendos, the consequences that follow are your own fault.

entries.name: Taming and Domestication
entries: In this section we outline the rules for taming wild animals, as well as worldbuilding tools to help include domesticated animals. Wild animals are difficult and often dangerous to tame. Instinct can override learned behaviour and it can take years to train an animal well. In a fantasy game setting, we want this process to be much faster and more involved, but still challenging. Below, we have outlined a process for taming wild animals. You may want to adjust these based on player power or the type of creature that is being tamed.

entries.name: Taming Rules
entries: Each creature with the Beast type has a {@b Taming Score}. This score is 0 unless otherwise stated by the DM. Once a creature has been subdued and is tied/chained/caged so that it cannot escape (but not {@condition Restrained|XPHB}), a player may attempt to increase that creature's Taming Score. Unless otherwise stated, they may attempt to do this {@b once per day}, as the creature will be unreceptive to multiple training sessions.

In order to make this attempt, the player must have {@b appropriate food} in an {@b appropriate volume} to feed the beast, as outlined in the table below. The player then attempts to bond with the animal over the course of an hour. They must make a contested {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} vs {@skill Survival|XPHB} check against the creature. Each success by the player increases the taming score of the creature by 1. Each failure by the player drops this score by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and the creature makes a single attack at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} at the player attempting to tame it.

When the beast's Taming Score {@b exceeds that creature's Proficiency Bonus or CR} (whichever is higher), the animal is considered tame and is loyal to the player/NPC (or team of players/NPCs) who tamed it. It will follow them unless commanded to stay.

items: {@condition Charmed|XPHB} creatures make their {@skill Survival|XPHB} check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} and cannot make an attack if the player is unsuccessful.
Dominated creatures automatically fail their {@skill Survival|XPHB} check.
A player using Speak with Animals has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} and expertise on their {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} check.
